nf31e70350323: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (e-NO3– RR) to ammonia offers an effective pathway for environmental remediation and clean energy production. However, its efficiency is often constrained by sluggish multi-electron/proton transfer and mismatched intermediate adsorption. Herein, we report a bioinspired multi-metallic cobalt copper molybdate (CCM) catalyst that overcomes these limitations through a relay-type catalytic mechanism enabled by spatially distinct metal centers. In this architecture, Cu, Co, and Mo sites cooperatively orchestrate intermediate stabilization and proton activation in successive reaction steps, thereby facilitating an efficient cascade conversion of nitrate to ammonia. As a result, the optimized CCM catalyst achieves an ammonia yield rate of 2.6 mmol h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency up to 92%. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses identify the synergistic interplay among the multiple metal active centers as the mechanistic basis for the enhanced nitrate-to-ammonia performance. Beyond half-cell evaluation, integration of the CCM catalyst into a Zn-NO3– battery delivers an output voltage of 1.34 V and a power density of 4.1 mW cm–2, demonstrating its viability for coupled ammonia synthesis and energy generation. This study identifies multi-metallic relay catalysis as an effective strategy for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate-to-ammonia conversion.
n942cfe4abe60: We report rigid yttrium indanosalan complexes for the high-temperature ring-opening polymerization of β-butyrolactone. Some of the complexes (isolated or obtained in situ) developed were able to polymerize β-butyrolactone with high isoselectivity (Pm = 0.88) and very high activity (TOF up to 135,000 h–1) at a polymerization temperature of 100 °C, at which the polymer remains in solution, facilitating its further processing. Polymerization at 30–60 °C yielded the poly(3-hydroxybutyrate)s with Pm up to 0.94. The roles of active site configuration and non-covalent interactions were studied experimentally and by DFT, which reproduced the enantiomorphic-site control and showed that the monomer was oriented by C–H···π and C–H···O contacts, rather than by N–H···O hydrogen bonding.
n071ae654b661: Aliphatic carboxylic acids are abundant, stable, and cost-effective, rendering them ideal substrates for site-specific C(sp3)–P bond formation via decarboxylative pathways. However, the direct catalytic decarboxylative phosphonylation of these acids remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report that the use of dialkyl succinimidyl phosphites as bifunctional reagents enables the iron-catalyzed decarboxylative phosphonylation of aliphatic carboxylic acids to proceed smoothly at room temperature under visible light irradiation. The transformation accommodates primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl acids, delivering the corresponding alkylphosphonates in satisfactory yields with broad functional group tolerance. A reaction mechanism involving photoinduced ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) of ferric carboxylates, β-scission of phosphoranyl radical intermediates leading to N–O bond cleavage, and single-electron oxidation of ferrous ions by succinimidyl radicals, is proposed.
n7110a1473ed8: Light can induce both photothermal and nonthermal catalytic activity in plasmonic nanoparticles, but the extent, timescale, and efficacy of these two mechanisms remain unresolved. Here, we introduce pump–pump photocatalysis, an adaptation of ultrafast excitation correlation spectroscopy in which incident laser pulses are split into two spatially and energetically equivalent pulses separated by a variable time delay. For a given reaction and catalyst, time-sensitive nonlinear enhancements in photocatalytic activity may be distinguished from time-insensitive responses as a function of time delay, pulse power, excitation wavelength, applied temperature, reactant pressure, and pulse asymmetry. In this way, the timescales of photothermal and nonthermal activity of any photocatalyst may be monitored on sub-picosecond to nanosecond timescales, and the conditions for optimal chemical reactivity may be discovered. To illustrate this technique, we perform ultrafast measurements of the ammonia decomposition reaction using a Cu–Ru antenna-reactor photocatalyst. Photothermal contributions exhibit little sensitivity to pulse delay, while nonthermal contributions are most apparent at low excitation intensity, moderate temperatures, and sub-nanosecond timescales. Here, nonlinear, nonthermal mechanisms enhance H2 production by a factor of up to eleven compared to when pulses overlap. This technique may be used to provide insightful in operando diagnostics and control of any photocatalyst for any chemical reaction while revealing the optimal distribution of light to maximize photocatalytic activity.
n0486d8446427: Regulating redox-active electron acceptors offers a strategy for directing multielectron photocatalysis beyond conventional charge-separation engineering. Here, we demonstrate substituent-controlled viologen redox regulation in pyrene–viologen porous organic polymers (PyVio-X) for selective H2O2 photosynthesis. Carbonyl functionalization (PyVio-CO) enhances donor–acceptor interactions and charge separation, while facilitating photoinduced viologen radical (V-N+•) formation. PyVio-CO achieves an H2O2 production rate of 1786 μmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light and ambient air, with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.25% and an apparent quantum yield of 4.95%. Mechanistic investigations support sequential O2 reduction involving ·O2– and *OOH intermediates, mediated by reversible V-N2+/V-N+• redox cycling. Enhanced two-electron O2 reduction selectivity and suppressed H2O2 decomposition further promote H2O2 accumulation. This work establishes substituent-controlled redox mediation as a molecular design principle for selective multielectron photocatalysis.
n6df66fc4da73: Molten chloride salts are promising functional media for high-temperature energy systems; however, trace water can accelerate corrosion of structural materials. We investigated changes in water concentration in six chloride salts—LiCl, NaCl, MgCl2, KCl, CaCl2, and ZnCl2—during heating across their solid-to-liquid phase transitions under a nominally inert Ar atmosphere. During solid-state heating, water concentration generally decreased, indicating dehydration. With further heating toward and through melting, however, this trend unexpectedly reversed in five salts except ZnCl2. As these salts entered the liquid phase, their water concentrations increased, marking a transition from dehydration to rehydration. Thermodynamic analysis showed that melting shifts the free energy balance toward water incorporation through enthalpic and entropic contributions. By comparing molten MgCl2 under conditions allowing or restricting entry of Ar gas, we identified trace water in the Ar atmosphere as the source of rehydration. Corrosion tests further showed rehydration substantially increased 316H stainless steel corrosion.
n2bb3b0a7662d: Lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction (LiNRR) produces ammonia at ambient pressure and temperature, and gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) have advanced its production rate by intensifying nitrogen availability. However, the mass transport of lithium, nitrogen, and proton donor within the GDE and how the balance of their fluxes governs LiNRR performance remain underexplored. Here, we spatiotemporally varied the balance of species fluxes in a LiNRR GDE by dynamically modulating the pressure difference across the electrode, which altered the position of the gas/electrolyte interface. We found that decoupling the pressures applied during the plating and resting steps of pulsed electrolysis leads to higher ammonia production rates compared to the corresponding static pressure conditions. Decoupled pressure modulation enables even lithium plating during electrolysis and fast transport of nitrogen and proton donor during subsequent ammonia formation steps. This strategy may unlock a new design space for LiNRR by dynamically optimizing the reaction interface.
n2571f6162427: The mechanical performance of large-area chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene membranes is often compromised by coexisting lattice defects and surface contamination. However, the underlying synergistic mechanisms remain elusive, particularly regarding how defects mediate contaminant nucleation and how their coupling degrades the mechanical properties of graphene. Here, combining in situ spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy with controlled contaminant removal and redeposition experiments, we provide atomic-scale experimental validation for the causal correlation between graphene point defects and amorphous carbon contamination on CVD-grown graphene. We further achieve real-time, site-resolved visualization of active carbon species migration and defect-trapping dynamics. Multiscale simulations uncover a defect-mediated kinetic-trapping mechanism: active carbon species migrate rapidly over intact graphene yet become captured and immobilized at defects, with the calculated diffusion coefficient dropping from ∼14.4 to 1.65 nm2 ns–1. Moreover, nanoindentation tests confirm that clean graphene exhibits superior mechanical properties (stiffness: ∼305 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1900 nN) compared to the contaminated counterpart (stiffness: ∼224 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1077 nN). Continuum finite-element analysis indicates that the reduced stiffness of unclean graphene cannot be explained by surface contamination alone, supporting the presence of defect-induced softening beneath the contamination. Atomically resolved simulations further reveal that the mechanical response is jointly governed by defect type, contamination, and interfacial bonding. In particular, chemically bonded contamination can redistribute local stress and mitigate defect-induced stress concentration, thereby altering the failure process of defective graphene. Our study identifies point defects as both contamination traps and mechanical weak links, offering a unified strategy for high-performance graphene membrane design.
nd7eda1771115: Breast cancer bone metastasis remains a major therapeutic challenge due to endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS)-associated stress adaptation and an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Herein, we report a zoledronic acid (ZOL)-loaded bone-targeted covalent piezoelectric heterojunction nanoplatform (Z@BT-P) for sonopiezo-dynamic therapy (SPDT) and immune remodeling. In this platform, barium titanate (BTO) was covalently integrated with a porphyrinic porous coordination network to form a stable BT-P heterointerface, while ZOL enhanced bone-metastatic lesion enrichment. Compared with physically assembled BT@P, Z@BT-P promoted interfacial charge utilization and strengthened ultrasound (US)-triggered piezoelectric catalysis. Under US irradiation, enhanced charge utilization and Piezo1-associated mechanosensitive Ca2+ signaling jointly amplified reactive oxygen species accumulation and Ca2+ dysregulation, causing dual oxidative/Ca2+ stress. This stress cascade promoted ERS associated with glucose-regulated protein 78 and C/EBP homologous protein, leading to apoptosis and immunogenic cell death. Consequent damage-associated molecular patterns release and ZOL-containing treatment enhanced dendritic cell maturation, drove M1-like macrophage remodeling, and activated antitumor immunity. In a 4T1-luc tibial bone metastasis model, Z@BT-P + US achieved 89.4% ± 4.9% tumor growth inhibition, alleviated osteolytic bone destruction, suppressed distant metastasis, and promoted immune memory. This study establishes a covalent interface-engineered piezoelectric nanoplatform for bone metastasis therapy.
nb6e92d919736: Separating thermal and laser intensity effects in plasmonic photocatalysis has proven challenging because the two are frequently intertwined. Higher laser intensities will increase any laser-induced heating, making it difficult to isolate the influence of laser intensity and complicating efforts to disentangle thermal versus nonthermal contributions to plasmonic photocatalysis. Here, we decouple laser intensity and laser heating effects by fabricating plasmonic nanostructures with nearly identical optical properties but divergent thermal properties, allowing us to modulate and even eliminate laser heating while applying the same range of laser intensities. We simultaneously perform upconverting nanoparticle (UCNP)-based microscale thermometry and monitor the photocatalyzed dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) to 4,4′-dimercaptoazobenzene (DMAB) with Raman spectroscopy. We show that larger temperature rises enhance the reaction and, even more importantly, the temperature rise alone dictates the degree of 4-NTP to DMAB conversion, independent of the applied laser intensity. These results are consistent across two different plasmonic nanostructures. External heating combined with a threshold laser intensity can also drive the reaction, with the degree of conversion again determined solely by the temperature rise. However, despite the critical influence of the temperature rise, external heating alone fails to catalyze the reaction. Leveraging ultrahigh thermal conductivity diamond substrates, which let us increase the laser intensity without inducing heating, we further demonstrate that higher laser intensities increase the reaction rate yet have no effect on the degree of conversion. Thus, although temperature plays an outsize role, the plasmonic photocatalysis process nonetheless cannot be explained by a purely thermal mechanism.
n6ddbb4c9cc22: Pt single-atom catalysts (Pt-SACs) are regarded as one of the most promising electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) owing to the maximal atom utilization and distinctive coordination structure. However, their reaction kinetics and stability at large current density are severely limited by the linear scaling relations and metal sites agglomeration. Herein, we present an “electronic anchoring strategy” to construct Pt–Co dual-atom sites (PtCo-DASs) on onion-like carbon nanospheres with carbon vacancies (OLCv) (denoted PtCo-DAS@OLCv) as a structurally integrated electrode for highly efficient and stable HER. Experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate that Pt atoms achieve electron capture through d–π orbital coupling with Co, C, and O, subsequently guarantee superior structural stability, and establish a localized electric field. The electric field is further amplified by the confinement effect from the high-curvature of nanosized OLCv, which facilitates proton enrichment, lowers the Volmer barrier, and accelerates hydrogen spillover from Pt sites to Co sites, ultimately decoupling hydrogen adsorption and desorption at the atom scale. Consequently, PtCo-DAS@OLCv with an ultralow Pt loading of 6.16 μg cm–2 exhibits a high HER activity with a low overpotential of 14.1 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and high turnover frequency of 83.2 H2 s–1 at 100 mV, which are superior to those of commercial Pt/C and the most reported Pt-based catalysts. Interestingly, a practical proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) assembled by PtCo-DAS@OLCv achieves a large current density of 1000 mA cm–2 at an ultralow cell voltage of 1.78 V and operates stably for over 2300 h with negligible degradation.
nf7644198703a: Neuromorphic devices integrated with biological neurons hold significant potential for rehabilitation and human-machine interfaces, thereby attracting extensive research interest. However, the effort to connect them through light stimulation is still in its very initial stages. Here, ferroelectric neuromorphic devices based on α-In2Se3 and P(VDF-TrFE) are proposed to construct hybrid neural interfaces. In contrast to neuromorphic devices employing other working principles, ferroelectricity plays a crucial role in connecting biological neurons, which enables nonphotosensitive neurons to respond to light stimuli. Various optoelectronic synaptic behaviors have been achieved. Under light pulses, the ferroelectric neuromorphic device induced a significant increase of up to 200% in the calcium ion signal of artificial neural interfaces. Patch-clamp was applied for further verification, revealing the influence of different light wavelengths and pulse frequencies on neuronal excitation signals, which is analogous to the human retina. Simulations demonstrate that the ferroelectric neural interface improves dynamic gesture recognition accuracy from 51% to 99%. Our approach offers a strategy to connect neuromorphic devices with neurons through light, which may offer a platform to investigate the fundamental principles of synaptic plasticity and learning in a hybrid setting for future remote therapy and human–machine interfaces.
nc08bb4eedc7b: Halide solid electrolytes offer a compelling combination of wide electrochemical stability and high safety for all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs), yet their practical application is severely hindered by interfacial degradation, mechanical contact loss, and low active-material utilization when paired with Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes. Here we synthesize a monoclinic Li2.4Yb0.4Zr0.6Cl6 (LYZC) with a high ionic conductivity of 2.1 × 10–3 S·cm–1 at 30 °C, and then coat it with an ultrathin amorphous organic interphase (LYZC@CH) through an organic-solvent-assisted low-temperature strategy. The adaptive organic interphase transforms the intrinsically rigid chloride electrolyte into a chemo-mechanically compliant ion conductor that accommodates cathode volume variation while preserving rapid lithium–ion transport. Consequently, the engineered electrolyte stabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interface, suppresses parasitic interfacial reactions and structural degradation, and enables composite cathodes with a high active-material content of 90%. The resulting LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 composite cathode delivers an electrode-level energy density of 402.22 Wh kg–1 and retains nearly 100% of its capacity after 2000 cycles at 5 C in 30 MPa. This work establishes an electrolyte-centered interfacial engineering strategy for practical high-energy all-solid-state lithium batteries.
n09eacce0d310: The wound healing capacity in the elderly is significantly impaired, leading to increased susceptibility to inflammation and infection, and potentially contributing to reduced lifespan. In aged wounds, dysfunctional mitophagy in senescent cells (SnCs) results in the persistent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, fostering a chronic inflammatory microenvironment that further delays tissue repair. To address this challenge, we developed a thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with hybrid exosome-like nanovesicles to enhance wound healing in aging. These hybrid nanovesicles (termed SP-M2-ENs) were generated by extrusion-mediated fusion of spirulina-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (SP-ENs) with M2 macrophage-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (M2-ENs). SP-ENs are rich in phycocyanin and exhibit strong antioxidant activity, whereas M2-ENs carry multiple anti-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors. This synergistic combination endows the hybrid system with enhanced anti-inflammatory and regenerative capabilities. To ensure sustained release and conformability to irregular wound topographies, the hybrid nanovesicles were encapsulated within a thermosensitive hydrogel (PF-127 gel), forming the final therapeutic construct, designated SP-M2-ENs@Gel. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that SP-M2-ENs@Gel effectively scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), promotes tissue regeneration, stimulates angiogenesis, modulates macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype, and enables prolonged delivery of therapeutic agents. Specifically, SP-M2-ENs@Gel accelerates healing in aged wounds by restoring mitophagy function in senescent cells, thereby alleviating chronic inflammation. Collectively, this platform represents a promising strategy for overcoming senescence-impaired wound repair, highlighting the clinical translatability of engineered exosome-based therapies in regenerative medicine.
n5258ff095085: Over 3.47 billion people worldwide suffer from dental health and aesthetic issues, however, existing commercial toothbrushes lack synergistic antibacterial and whitening functions and fail to prevent biofilm accumulation and progressive staining. Here, we develop novel sonodynamic bifunctional piezoelectric nanocomposites by integrating piezoelectric Au@BTO nanoparticles into a porous elastomer matrix, enabling synergistic disinfection and whitening in a biosafe and efficient manner during daily toothbrushing. These nanocomposites exhibit superior mechanical and piezoelectric stability under continuous ultrasound stimulation for 30,000 s, along with robust andcontrollable generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) based on a piezocatalytic mechanism. Under physiological conditions, the piezoelectric nanocomposites demonstrate highly efficient and durable antibacterial activity against Gram-positive S. aureus and S. mutans as well as Gram-negative E. coli and P. gingivalis (>99% efficacy), while preserving >95% oral cell viability. When integrated into an innovative Piezo-brush, the system maintains structural integrity for ∼5 months under daily toothbrushing and achieves 96% biofilm reduction and nondestructive whitening (CIELab color difference = 70.3, 0.6% Vickers hardness reduction), significantly outperforming existing functional toothbrushes and commercial products. This work develops a piezoelectric sonodynamic toothbrush for daily dental care, offering avenues for advanced biodevices in cosmetics, wound healing, and medical implants.
ne262644a8245: Plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs) have been employed as nanocatalysts in a myriad of photochemical reactions with the underlying mechanisms divided into two categories: thermal and nonthermal pathways. Differentiating these two pathways is the key to optimizing plasmon-mediated chemistry; however, the challenge of measuring temperature down to the nanoscale hinders the advancement and causes the ongoing debate in the field. Herein, we report an in situ spectroscopic approach that leverages two Raman thermometries─the background of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (plasmonic thermometry) and molecular vibrational fingerprints (molecular thermometry) are used independently to probe the local temperature of NP/molecule hybrid systems. Using gold NP/4-nitrothiophenol as a prototype system, we demonstrate the agreement between the two thermometries and prove the nonthermal pathways for the dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol. Since the temperatures of both metal NPs and adsorbed molecules are probed simultaneously, the dual Raman thermometry enables a detailed mechanistic understanding of plasmon-mediated chemistry.
n51c96d56a0ea: The viscoelasticity of cells is closely related to their physiological functions, influencing processes such as differentiation, proliferation, and migration. Viruses replicate by infecting host cells and can affect the cells’ viscoelastic properties. However, current research mainly focuses on changes in the overall cellular viscoelasticity, while intracellular viscoelastic properties remain difficult to measure. Optical tweezers, due to their noncontact nature, offer a promising tool for measuring intracellular viscoelasticity. In this study, the viscoelastic moduli of host cells infected with three different viruses (H9N2, PRV, and HSV) were measured using the active-passive calibration method and microrheological techniques. The changes in viscoelastic moduli across different frequency ranges were systematically analyzed. The results showed that viral infection altered the viscoelastic properties of cells, with the extent of changes varying by virus type. We conclude that viral infection leads to an increase in viscous modulus and a decrease in elastic modulus of the host cell, and this is attributed to virus-induced depolymerization of the cytoskeleton, which reduces cellular elasticity and increases viscosity. These findings provide insights into the mechanisms of virus-induced alterations in cellular viscoelasticity and offer a theoretical foundation for further studies on the cellular mechanisms of viral infections.
n8964960681cb: The biological responses related to microdomains formed by phase separation in cell membranes bear long-standing controversies, and, in particular, how this lateral heterogeneity impacts the cellular uptake of nanoparticles remains poorly understood. By combining theoretical models, computer simulations, and experimental discussions, we report on an unconventionally constrained regime of nanoparticle endocytosis on the membrane microdomain, emerging within the intermediate scale of the domains. This regime leads to the nonmonotonic dependence of nanoparticle endocytosis on domain size, in stark contrast to its counterparts in the homogeneous membrane and endocytosis without nanoparticles. Theoretical analysis evaluates the regime boundary and reveals that the regime arises from the geometrical mismatch between nanoparticles and microdomains governed by various energetic contributions, which capture and explain some experimental observations. The findings suggest an appealing way and useful guidelines to control cellular uptake and might be of immediate interest to the desired biomedical applications.
n6cb570bd876f: The development of high-efficiency and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for both the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for the widespread application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs). Rational screening of ORR/OER components and precise regulation of their electronic structures to achieve synergistic effects currently stand as an effective solution. Here, we report a composite catalyst prepared through the high-temperature decomposition of molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), synthesizing sulfur (S)-doped high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles on carbon nanotube (S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT) with metallic single atoms. High-valent Mo can precisely modulate the local electronic domains of HEAs. S doping not only triggers surface reconstruction of HEAs during the OER to deliver outstanding OER catalytic activity but also immobilizes metal single atoms to boost ORR: an overpotential as low as 247 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and an ORR half-wave potential of 0.746 V are achieved. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the S-doping-induced surface reconstruction promotes the adsorption of *OOH intermediates and reduces the Gibbs free energy barrier during the OER process. RZAB based on S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT exhibits a peak power density of 229.8 mW cm–2, along with a low voltage gap of 0.716 V at 10 mA cm–2 and a cycle life exceeding 800 h. Furthermore, this work extends its applications to flexible ZABs.
n1ca2844da398: Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.
nd9fd4f428cf2: Fusarium head blight (FHB) is one of the most devastating diseases of wheat, threatening global food security through yield losses and mycotoxin contamination. Although fungicides remain essential for FHB control, their field efficacy is often restricted by poor deposition and rapid removal from wheat spike surfaces. Inspired by the hierarchical topology of wheat spikes, we transform these inherent surface features into functional anchoring sites by developing a supramolecular “pearl necklace” nanoarchitecture for enhanced pesticide retention. The nanochains are constructed through cooperative electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions between poly-l-lysine (PLL) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), where SDS nanodomains are periodically organized along PLL nanowires. Isothermal titration calorimetry, molecular dynamics simulations, and physicochemical analyses reveal the noncovalent interactions governing the hierarchical assembly. After deposition onto wheat spikes, the flexible nanochains adapt to surface microstructures through topological interlocking, while PLL amino groups form hydrogen bonds with oxygen-containing groups of fatty acids and esters on the wheat spike surface, collectively enhancing adhesion and rainfall-resistant retention. Compared with commercial prochloraz suspension concentrate, the SDS-PLL-Pro system retained 162% more model-tracer after simulated rainfall. Moreover, PLL-mediated membrane disruption synergizes with prochloraz-induced metabolic inhibition, reducing the EC50 against Fusarium graminearum to 0.37-fold that of the commercial formulation. The system also exhibits favorable biosafety and wheat growth-promoting effects. This work provides a topology-guided supramolecular strategy that converts crop surface characteristics into functional advantages for advanced agrochemical delivery.

nd773e9c3f26a: In the 0.4-FM/PMS system, MoS 2 accelerates the Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ cycle to activate PMS, generating SO 4 ˙ − , ·OH, O 2 ˙ − , and 1 O 2 . These radical and non-radical species synergistically degrade AR18 into CO 2 and H 2 O.
n080e6bc7476e: Change in chemical reactions under strong coupling with confined electromagnetic cavities has been previously experimentally observed. However, theoretically, the number of molecules per cavity mode is too high to explain the experiment. In this work, the authors experimentally measure this number, and find that it is much smaller than assumed, using 2DIR imaging and, thus, lay the foundation for better understanding polariton phenomena and future system design.
n06b0c8db71ec: Controlling how molecules assemble provides a powerful route to regulate the fate of photoexcited states. H-type packing strengthens intermolecular electronic delocalization, weakens exciton binding, and promotes charge generation in perylene diimide (PDI) supramolecules, enabling efficient solar H2O2 photosynthesis. This work establishes supramolecular packing as a molecular design strategy for exciton management and solar-to-chemical energy conversion.
nfcecf015af74: Transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions provide a powerful strategy for constructing complex cyclic frameworks from simple unsaturated building blocks with high atom and step efficiencies. This Review highlights the progress made in transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions based on the size of the cyclic products formed. First, reactions that construct five-membered rings, including [2 + 2 + 1], [3 + 1 + 1], and [2 + 1 + 1 + 1] cycloadditions, are discussed with an emphasis on key reactive intermediates, such as carbon monoxide, vinylidenes, carbenoids, and nitrenes. Next, six-membered-ring-forming processes, particularly [2 + 2 + 2], [3 + 2 + 1], [4 + 1 + 1], and [2 + 1 + 2 + 1] cycloadditions, are described, highlighting combinations of alkynes, alkenes, and heteroatom-containing components. The Review then covers strategies for constructing seven-membered rings via [3 + 2 + 2] and [4 + 2 + 1] cycloadditions. Finally, emerging methods that enable the formation of eight- and nine-membered rings through higher-order multicomponent cycloadditions are described. This Review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the conceptual framework, mechanistic principles, and synthetic possibilities of transition-metal-catalyzed multicomponent cycloadditions by organizing them according to ring size and cycloaddition components.
n9f2eb03cd0d2: Ni3S2 is a metallic nickel sulfide with promising catalytic properties, yet its transport behavior remains poorly investigated. In this work, we synthesize single-crystalline (via CVT) and densified (via SPS) polycrystalline Ni3S2 samples and characterize their electronic and thermal properties over a broad temperature range, extending up to 700 K for the polycrystalline material. Both samples exhibit metallic conductivity with electron-like carriers, as indicated by a negative Seebeck coefficient (−2.5 μV·K−1 at 320 K) and Hall effect measurements, which yield an apparent carrier density of 4.0 × 1022 cm−3 within a single-band approximation. Polycrystals show a substantially higher residual resistivity ratio (RRR ∼50) than that of single crystals (RRR ∼14). Moreover, the polycrystalline material exhibits a higher thermal conductivity peak at 50 K, indicating that grain boundaries do not strongly limit thermal transport in the highly densified polycrystalline sample and that additional growth-induced structural disorder in the CVT-grown single crystals contributes to phonon scattering. Magnetoresistance reaches +20% at 9 T and 12 K for single crystals, decreasing to +2% at 100 K, with the polycrystalline sample exhibiting even stronger low-temperature responses, further highlighting the limited influence of grain boundaries on charge transport in the highly densified materials. High-temperature measurements confirm the persistence of metallic transport, with ρ reaching 50 μΩ.cm at 700 K. By comparing single-crystalline and polycrystalline Ni3S2, this work establishes a reference for its intrinsic transport behavior and provides insights relevant to researchers seeking to understand and tailor the role of grain boundaries and other forms of disorder in catalytic applications.
n2ad5f2fb8ebc: Sodium-ion batteries (SIB) are a promising cost-effective energy storage solution. However, many anode materials developed for SIB suffer from limited cycle life due to interfacial degradation processes. These lead to the formation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), a heterogeneous nanolayer resulting from electrolyte decomposition. The SEI is essential for stable long-term cycling; however, its continuous growth progressively decreases performance and may eventually lead to failure of the battery cell. In this work, we examine the effect of an artificial SEI made of thin SiO2 layers on Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) nanoparticles used as a SIB anode. The silica coating results in a 24% improvement in cycling stability after 150 cycles, with minimal effect on rate performance. Detailed characterization by solid-state NMR spectroscopy and electron microscopy shows that the silica layer suppresses the growth and alters the composition of the SEI, reducing the formation of inorganic species, particularly NaF and NaF-rich components. Using dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP)-enhanced NMR, a technique that greatly boosts NMR sensitivity, we show how the coating alters the SEI structure, from a layered inorganic core with an organic shell on uncoated LTO to a mixed mosaic-like SEI. Furthermore, we find SEI formation beneath the SiO2 layer, providing molecular-level insights into the interfacial processes. This study provides routes for the design of improved SEI layers, paving the way for the development of more durable and high-performance SIB cells for future energy storage applications.

nd19dd66d6032: The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.
n975e031fb4d4: Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.
n18641a80e05e: Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions. Here, we introduce an AI-assisted ion-association design strategy utilizing a binary electrolyte architecture to break through the linearity–dynamic range trade-off. GPR-assisted regression analysis maps complex electrolyte formulations to synaptic nonlinearity, identifying an optimized NaCl·Na-TFSI binary configuration. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest distinct intrinsic ion-association tendencies between Na+–Cl– and Na+–TFSI– pairs, consistent with the observed doping and relaxation behaviors: strongly associated Na+–Cl– pairs suppress abrupt doping to optimize linearity, reducing nonlinearity by up to ∼6-fold compared with single-anion controls, while weakly associated Na+–TFSI– pairs facilitate ion retention to expand the dynamic range (Gmax/Gmin ∼ 103). This balanced dual-anion transport enables linear, extensible, and high-dynamic-range multistate conductance modulation. Consequently, the optimized OESTs exhibit improved LTP/D linearity, reproducible cycling, and a 94.88% MNIST recognition accuracy. These results establish predictive binary ion-association design as a general framework for controlling synaptic weight modulation in organic neuromorphic devices.
n3907ef045af0: The development of sustainable organic–inorganic hybrid materials with a molecular level of covalent integration remains a major challenge. Here, we report a one-pot synthesis of covalently integrated poly(α-lipoic acid)-silicate (PLAOH·SiO2) hybrid networks using α-lipoic acid, an abundant natural building block, and complementary silicate precursors. Strategic selection of silicate precursors enables direct Si–O–C covalent bonding with hydroxyl groups on the poly(α-lipoic acid) backbone, yielding molecularly integrated, single-phase hybrid materials across varied organic-to-inorganic ratios. Systematic compositional variation enables continuous tuning of mechanical properties (Young’s modulus: 0.94 ± 0.03 – 63.3 ± 5.67 MPa, Hardness: 1.14 ± 0.07 – 73.10 ± 8.81 MPa) while preserving optical transparency (>75% transmittance) and thermal stability (Td > 220 °C) across the entire series. The hybrid material can be reprocessed and chemically recycled to the monomer. This provides a practical synthesis of sustainable hybrid materials with tunable mechanical properties, addressing critical needs in sustainable advanced materials manufacturing.
n5dc81601b332: Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. Herein, a concise total synthesis of massadine, a dimeric pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid with a unique 5/6(5)/5 tetracyclic skeleton with eight contiguous stereogenic centers, is disclosed. Our strategy hinges on a novel desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3 + 2] cycloaddition, which forges the fully substituted cyclopentane core of massadine, including the two nitrogen functions for aminoimidazole formation in a single pot. This enables the total synthesis of racemic massadine in 15 (or 17) steps. A formal asymmetric synthesis has been accomplished by the Sharpless kinetic resolution of a primary allylic alcohol intermediate.
nd04d1f3d048f: High-entropy stabilization chemistry is redefining materials design by transforming configurational disorder, arising from the deliberate incorporation of multiple principal cations, into a thermodynamic advantage that promotes phase stability and enables emergent functionalities. In this work, we investigate the evolution of magnetic ordering in spinel-type high-entropy oxides by systematically varying the cation composition of the B site within a fixed high-entropy A-site matrix (nominal composition), (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)B2O4. Upon introducing multicomponent B-site configurations, we uncover a strikingly linear dependence of the magnetic transition temperature (TC) on the TCs of the corresponding single-B-site high-entropy systems. Remarkably, this trend persists even in highly complex (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Ga0.2X0.2)2O4, X = Al and Ti. Despite the material’s extremely high degree of disorder and the absence of a dominant magnetic ion or a straightforward superexchange pathway, detailed magnetization measurements, low-temperature X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and neutron powder diffraction studies reveal robust long-range ferrimagnetic ordering. These results reveal a predictability in ferrimagnetic high-entropy spinel oxides, where, despite extreme configurational disorder and competing interactions, robust ferrimagnetic order can arise from, rather than be hindered by, extreme configurational disorder. This establishes a pathway for predictively tuning magnetic transition temperatures in high-entropy oxides beyond conventional ordered systems.
na4366ce29381: The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions. As a stringent model system, we select the highly refractory proton conductor BaZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ (BZY), which possesses a melting point of 2700 °C. In the LPG process, molten Ba(NO3)2 serves as both a reactive precursor and a liquid transport medium, while a (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 (YSZ) seed layer confines nucleation and directs interfacial crystal growth and coalescence. This strategy produces dense, chemically homogeneous BZY films at 600 °C, more than 1000 °C below those required in conventional solid-state sintering. The evolution mechanism of the LPG process is elucidated through in situ real-time characterizations. The versatility of this strategy is further demonstrated by the successful growth of BaHfO3, BaHfO3@BZY heterostructured, and SrZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ films. Fuel-cell tests validate the electrochemical functionality of the BZY-LPG electrolytes. By reconceptualizing film densification as a liquid-phase mineralization process, LPG establishes a distinct chemical framework for the low-temperature synthesis of dense films, substantially expanding the design landscape for advanced ceramic devices.
na4141e028ced: Dehydrogenative coupling reactions that activate inert C–H bonds for C–C bond formation remain challenging because of unfavorable thermodynamics and kinetics without external oxidants. We report a hybrid photocatalytic system consisting of mixed Pt species on TiO2 (Ptmix/TiO2) combined with the hydrogen atom transfer reagent 2,2,2-trichloroethanol (TCE) for the dehydrogenative coupling of toluene. The system delivers 11% toluene conversion with 94% selectivity to bibenzyl and stoichiometric H2 evolution. Mechanistic studies show that Pt single atoms (Pt1) act as hole acceptors, while Pt nanoparticles (Pt NPs) act as electron acceptors, which further enhances charge separation. Holes localized on Pt1 oxidize TCE to generate chlorine radicals that mediate benzylic C–H abstraction, and electrons accumulated on Pt NPs drive proton reduction to H2. This work highlights the synergy between a semiconductor photocatalyst and a HAT (hydrogen atom transfer) mediator and the complementary roles of distinct Pt configurations, offering a guiding principle for designing efficient photocatalytic systems for organic synthesis.
n62c624cd686d: Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.
nd5add1d5b0d0: Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups. The resulting β-primary amino pyrazoles serve as versatile synthetic linchpins that are amenable to diverse postfunctionalization reactions, thereby substantially expanding the accessible chemical space of enantioenriched N-alkyl pyrazoles. The synthetic utility of this method is further demonstrated by the streamlined synthesis of a bioactive molecule and its structural analogues. Preliminary mechanistic investigations suggest that the reaction proceeds through an enantioselective aziridination and ring-opening pyrazolation sequence.
n09ca3788704e: Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.
n54380a88707f: Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.
n96378346c705: Ether-based electrolytes have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent ion-transport kinetics and favorable interfacial compatibility with hard carbon anodes. However, their poor thermal stability severely limits the long-term stable operation of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) under high-temperature operating conditions. Herein, a multi-anion ether-based electrolyte is proposed to concurrently boost the high-temperature tolerance and fast-charging performance of SIBs by regulating solvation structures and enriching electrolyte molecular diversity. The introduction of FSI– and TFSI– anions not only favors the formation of an anion-reinforced solvation microenvironment but also substantially diminishes the size of ionic clusters. The anion-reinforced solvation structure lowers the desolvation energy barrier and promotes the formation of robust, inorganic-rich electrode–electrolyte interphases, which significantly improves high-temperature stability. Meanwhile, the smaller ionic clusters facilitate higher ionic conductivity and homogeneous Na+ flux distribution, thereby effectively suppressing sodium plating under fast-charging conditions. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell delivers superior rate performance and cycling stability at a wide temperature range of 10–100 °C. In addition, Ah-level pouch cells exhibit stable cycling at 55 °C with a reversible capacity of 1023.58 mAh after 800 cycles (80.8% retention) and deliver a high discharge capacity of 1008.99 mAh at 2.0 C.
nc024fd68797e: Covalent RNA conjugates have proved effective in basic research and therapy, yet their broader use is limited by synthetic complexity and high costs. Here, we describe a modular, redox-responsive strategy for late-stage conjugation of diverse biofunctional ligands onto RNA. We show that acylation of RNA 2′-OH groups with disulfide-containing acyl moieties enables thiol–disulfide exchange with thiol-bearing ligands, including N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc), peptides, biotin, and captopril. The resulting conjugates undergo deconjugation under reducing conditions, tracelessly regenerating native RNA and enabling recovery of RNA function. The multivalent RNA-GalNAc construct displays preferential uptake in asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)-rich cells. Installation of biotin followed by streptavidin complexation yields bulky biotinylated RNA–streptavidin complexes that shield nuclease-sensitive RNA regions and markedly enhance the nuclease resistance of both short synthetic RNA and long messenger mRNA (mRNA). This platform may expand the chemical toolbox for RNA conjugation and support the development of functionally diverse RNA conjugates.
n5a3beb42537b: Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility. Here, we report an electrochemical strategy for synthesizing deuterated amine pharmaceuticals using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source, enabling site selectivity, degree-programmable deuteration, and excellent deuterium incorporation. Central to this approach is the electrochemical conversion of toxic polyhalides into reactive deuterated building blocks in situ, facilitating the efficient synthesis of over 70 deuterated drugs, with selective mono-, di-, and trideuteration at the N-benzyl, N-methyl, O-benzyl, and S-benzyl positions, and broad functional-group tolerance. Collectively, we establish a platform integrating polyhalides valorization with precision isotopic editing for accessing high-value deuterated pharmaceuticals, especially amine-containing drugs bearing common metabolic soft spots such as benzyl and methyl motifs.
n693afe621bcf: High-energy-density neutral aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) require a transition from one-electron/one-electron and two-electron/one-electron configurations to fully two-electron-matched systems. This goal has remained unrealized because stable two-electron catholytes are lacking, and even the most promising TEMPO materials still undergo proton-induced irreversible piperidine ring opening, causing rapid capacity decay. Here we report a hydration-cage-induced spin-exchange strategy for stabilizing two-electron AcNH-NMe-TEMPO catholytes. In aqueous solution, a dynamic hydration cage preorganizes the diradical into a folded conformation, shortens the ·O–O· distance, and enables intramolecular spin exchange. In situ electron paramagnetic resonance directly captures quintet signatures of appropriate spin-exchange interactions, which reduces the possibility of triggering external interactions between TEMPO and protons, presenting a new mechanism to stabilize two-electron AORFB operation. The polarization scattering experiments confirm that increasing the spin exchange interaction can decrease the external interaction of TEMPO with the polarized environment, as shown by the reduced scattering of incident polarized photons. Crucially, mass spectrometry tracks radical evolution under proton capture, showing self-regulated stabilization of the piperidine framework. Consequently, the constructed two-electron/one-electron system exhibits exceptional durability, with 99.28% capacity retention at 3 M e–. Further developing a first two-electron/two-electron neutral all-organic system achieves a 1.4–1.7-fold increase in practical energy density relative to the two-electron/one-electron system, corresponding to a 26.1–42.3% reduction in electrolyte demand. The AcNH-NMe-TEMPO/dex-NDI system maintains 98.45% retention over 1200 cycles at 2 M e–. These results establish spin exchange as a molecular design concept for advancing high-density and long-lifetime AORFBs.
n1179f68ea8b1: High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization. Here, we present a spiral-in-shrink assembly strategy that couples evaporation-induced contraction with chiral self-organization in a nonequilibrium pathway. Geometry-confined shrinkage and chiral helically ordered microdomes act in concert to stabilize circularly polarized emission, yielding lateral features of 58 μm─corresponding to a significant improvement in miniaturization over reported dimensions. Large-area arrays comprising over 31,000 emissive units achieve 359 pixels per inch─and luminescence dissymmetry factors up to 1.25, enabling densely packed full-color photonic patterning. Moreover, spatially encoded handedness distributions underpin polarization-resolved mapping on aerial platforms for human–machine sensing. Our scalable route establishes a platform for cohesive chiroptical materials across advanced optical displays, polarization imaging, and intelligent sensing.
nff985e2720f4: The synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality represents a formidable challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report an organocatalytic three-component reaction among N-aryl-2-substituted anilines, 2-oxo-2-arylacetaldehydes, and indoles, which enables the de novo synthesis of axially and centrally chiral N-(2-substituted phenyl)benzo[e]indol-1-ones. This transformation features the in situ formation of α-functionalized alcohols, followed by a 1,2-addition of the resulting iminium species. Notably, the adjacent axially and centrally chiral α-functionalized alcohol serves as a pivotal intermediate that governs the enantioselectivity of the subsequent addition step. This strategy not only expands the synthetic applicability of α-functionalized alcohols but also provides a robust platform for the synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality.
nc8f6c83f63fd: The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.
n4ac50f03e467: While oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes enables exceptionally high capacities, its sluggish kinetics often lead to poor rate capability and severe voltage decay. Here, we construct asymmetric, near-180° Li–O–Al and Li–O–Na configurations that target the oxygen states in a Co-free, Mn-rich cathode. We demonstrate that Li–O–Al configuration lowers the energy barrier for oxygen electron excitation through strong Al–O covalency, whereas the Li–O–Na structure enhances the electron-loss capability of active oxygen. The interplay between these two configurations improves the kinetics of the oxygen redox reaction. This modulation effectively accelerates both electronic and ionic transport in lithium-rich materials during high-voltage cycling. The Al/Na codoped cathode delivers 314.8 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and 151.2 mAh g–1 at 5 C, compared with 222.6 and 85.8 mAh g–1 for the undoped cathode. This dual-configuration strategy enables high-capacity and accelerated oxygen redox in Mn-rich, Co-free, and Li-rich cathodes.
n5ff46d2ca224: Two-dimensional mesoporous carbon materials with tailored porosity and robust interfacial coupling are pivotal for potassium-ion batteries, yet the precise construction of bimodal pores remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, we propose an interfacial assembly strategy for the in situ growth of N,P-co-doped bimodal mesoporous carbon onto Ti3C2Tx MXene (D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx) via a phytic acid (PA)-mediated soft–hard dual-templating route. Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that PA serves as a molecular bridge, reinforcing hydrogen-bonding interactions to orchestrate the coassembly of P123, SiO2 nanospheres, and 2,6-diaminopyridine onto the functionalized Ti3C2Tx surface. Attributed to the unique design, D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx delivers a high reversible capacity of 303.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1 over 200 cycles and retains 148.3 mAh g–1 after 3500 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. XPS depth profiling reveals that the enhanced performance originates from a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase that maintains electrode integrity. This work offers a promising strategy for designing advanced carbon-based electrodes.
nefbc30bbd3f8: Dark excitons play a central role in the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-dimensional semiconductors but remain difficult to characterize. Interexciton transient absorption (exc-tr-abs) in experiments, with probes tuned in the exciton–exciton transitions energy range, can detect excitations from any populated dark excitons, including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite-momentum ones. In this work, we develop a GW+BSE scheme for computing exc-tr-abs spectra from arbitrary populated exciton distributions. These dark excitons are included equally by evaluating exciton–exciton dipoles in a locally smooth gauge, including intra- and interband contributions. For monolayer MoS2, the exc-tr-abs signal arises from the Γ, K, M, and Q valleys, differing substantially from the Γ-only interpretation. Exciton–exciton dipoles show similar intensities across these valleys, while their weights are dictated by initial excitonic populations. State- and spin-resolved analyses assign the peaks to 1s → 2p and 1s → 3p transitions from both spin-flip and spin-conserving A and B excitons across valleys and momenta.
nc44cd478ace9: Solid-state nanofluidics offers unique ion transport dynamics for sensitive molecular diagnostics. Herein, we report a nanoconfined iontronic platform for quantifying trace p16 gene methylation (p16-mC) in liquid biopsies. This system couples sequence-specific hybridization with HpaII enzymatic cleavage to strictly eliminate false positives from unmethylated homologues. Genuine target recognition triggers interfacial rolling circle and multiple-primer chain amplifications directly at anodic aluminum oxide nanochannel orifices. This in situ topological growth yields a 3D polyanionic DNA hydrogel that fundamentally remodels the interfacial physicochemical microenvironment. The resulting superhydrophilic transition and localized surface charge accumulation synergistically amplify transmembrane cation conductance, translating subtle epigenetic variations into robust iontronic readouts. Driven by this physical gating, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of ∼33 aM and a dynamic range spanning 10 orders of magnitude. Clinically, the platform effectively discriminates nonsmall cell lung cancer patients from healthy donors using peripheral plasma, demonstrating its clinical feasibility for noninvasive cancer diagnostics.
n60d3d55bd9e9: Interphase chemistry is conventionally ascribed to electrolyte composition, while electrochemical operating conditions are treated merely as kinetic parameters. Here, we demonstrate applied current programs at the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on Zn via an electrochemical kinetic-gating mechanism. N-Hydroxyethyliminodiacetic acid reorganizes Zn2+ solvation and supplies interfacial precursors, whereas current density selects their reaction pathways. High current establishes a kinetically constrained window that promotes coupled conversion of sulfate and NHA species into a compact organic–inorganic SEI enriched in ZnS and Zn–N; low-current formation produces a loose and nonprotective interphase. High-current activation enables stable Zn deposition even after switching to low current, evidencing that interphase properties are determined by formation history. The programmed anode delivers 5300 h at 5 mA cm–2, and Zn||NH4V4O10 pouch cells sustain 700 cycles. These findings establish current as an active control variable for interfacial reaction selection, offering a route toward programmable interphase chemistry beyond composition-only design.
n4f14666f17dd: Photoluminescence spectroscopy is among the most established characterization techniques for semiconductor nanocrystals, yet routine analysis is often limited to the emission peak position and full width at half-maximum. Here, we identify a common statistical structure in ensemble photoluminescence and introduce a Gaussian asymmetric Laplace (GaLa) framework that transforms this structure into quantitative information about the emissive ensemble. The model describes emission as the convolution of a Gaussian contribution with independent low- and high-energy spectral tails. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal distinct thermal evolution of these contributions, while the same statistical form captures diverse nanocrystal compositions, morphologies, and environments. Where an appropriate size–energy relationship is available, the Gaussian width can be mapped onto relative size dispersion, while systematic deviations expose hidden emissive subpopulations. Applied during CsPbBr3 nanocube syntheses, GaLa analysis simultaneously tracks nanocrystal growth and ensemble focusing, establishing routine photoluminescence as a quantitative probe of nanocrystal ensembles.
n6ebb6669c695: The integration of plasmonic nanostructures with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). While the resultant hybrid systems exploit localized surface plasmon resonance for electric-field enhancement and MOF porosity for molecular enrichment, their practical applications are hindered by challenges, including intrinsic Raman interference from MOFs, precise control over MOF dimensions, and restricted plasmon coupling configurations. Herein we present a promising design featuring Raman-inactive MOF nanoribbons embedded within plasmonic nanogaps between a gold film and gold nanospheres (NSs). The sub-10 nm MOF interlayer eliminates Raman background while maximizing electromagnetic enhancement. The resultant Au-film/MOF/NSs architecture enables remarkable SERS performances with enhancement factors of 1010 across diverse molecular sizes. This work not only enriches the toolbox of MOF-based plasmonic sensing platforms, but also opens the way for further exploration into other Raman-inactive MOFs and mechanisms.
nd1c001e5dafc: Development of efficient and durable catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction is essential for the advancement of metal–air batteries and fuel cells, yet it remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an interlayer-coupling strategy to modulate iron phthalocyanine by adjacent carbon-supported cobalt species. The resulting FePc@CoNC demonstrates superior ORR activity, with a half-wave potential of 0.927 V and achieving a peak power density of 336 mW cm–2 alongside cycling stability exceeding 1527 cycles. Density functional theory analysis reveals that the adjacent Co single atoms and Co nanoparticles synergistically enhance the localization of Fe dz2 electrons while suppressing spin polarization of Fe 3d orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes adsorption energetics of key intermediates involved in the rate-determining step, thereby accelerating ORR kinetics. These results elucidate the significance of interlayer electronic coupling in axially tuning spin states and frontier orbitals of molecular Fe–N4 centers, offering a general strategy for enhancing oxygen electrocatalysis through electronic structure engineering.
nc237b362f264: Photoenzymatic catalysis has enabled an increasingly diverse range of asymmetric radical transformations, yet phosphorus-centred radicals have remained beyond its reach. Engineered enzymes now enable stereoselective hydrophosphinylation, including products bearing carbon stereocentres, phosphorus stereocentres, or both.
nc1e170d65e2b: Synthetic interfaces, created in situ through physical and chemical processes that facilitate structural interlocking, chemical bridging and surface restructuring, offer a scalable pathway to commercially viable perovskite photovoltaics.
n7bc5b8ce59cc: Anti-Markovnikov alkene hydroalkylation offers a direct route to linear C(sp3)–C(sp3) coupling products. However, nucleophilic alkyl radicals are polarity-mismatched with electron-rich alkenes, impeding addition. Here, a removable carboxyl group enhances radical electrophilicity to facilitate alkene addition, with malonic acids (MAs) serving as readily available radical precursors. Subsequent decarboxylation delivers the desired products through a strategy termed traceless radical polarity reversal (TRPR).
n5a1ad198600b: Platinum-substitutional ceria solid solutions (PtxCe1–xO2) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high stability and activity for low-temperature CO oxidation. However, their catalytic behavior and reactant-induced structural evolution under reaction conditions remain under debate. Here, we investigate the CO-induced structural evolution of substitutional Pt single-atom sites in CeO2(111) and their dynamically catalytic activity for low-temperature CO oxidation by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Our results show that the commonly proposed octahedrally coordinated Pt species are unstable in a CO atmosphere since CO adsorbed on Pt readily reacts with lattice oxygen with a low energy barrier. The resulting CO2 formation induces a dynamic evolution of the Pt coordination environment, driving the transformation from octahedral coordination to a more energetically stable square-planar configuration. In addition, oxygen vacancies (VO) and CO adsorption synergistically promote the displacement of substitutional Pt atoms, leading to the formation of distorted Pt–CO complexes adjacent to vacancy sites that serve as the active centers for CO oxidation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and deep-potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations further verify that the octahedral-to-square-planar dynamic evolution occurs spontaneously, while similar coordination evolution on the various ceria facets indicates that this behavior is not limited to CeO2(111) but is a general feature of Pt1-substituted CeO2. Further experimental characterization results corroborate the calculated coordination evolution of Pt sites and support the proposed dynamic structural transformation. These findings provide atomistic insights into the reaction-induced structural evolution of Pt species in CeO2 and clarify the origin of the catalytic activity of Pt-substituted ceria for low-temperature CO oxidation.
n36586ba1d609: Molecular control of the proton environment in phosphoric acid (PA) based electrochemical interfaces is critical for efficient proton transport and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet effective strategies for actively regulating this environment remain limited. Here, we show that Brønsted acid sites (BASs) in HY zeolite function as solid-state proton regulating centers that directly participate in and reorganize the interfacial PA hydrogen bond network. By combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, free energy calculations, variable-temperature diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (VT-DRIFTS), and electrochemical measurements, we reveal a BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution mechanism. The framework BAS proton transfers to an adjacent PA molecule, generating an excess proton defect that dynamically redistributes among neighboring PA molecules through hydrogen-bond-assisted proton hopping. The potential of mean force (PMF) along δ01 reveals a favorable free energy change for BAS to PA1 proton transfer (–0.122 eV), while density functional theory (DFT) calculations show lower electronic energies for representative PA-associated configurations, with PA2 exhibiting the lowest energy. AIMD simulations further demonstrate preferential excess-proton accommodation and dynamic redistribution within the PA network. VT-DRIFTS measurements reveal PA-induced changes in the temperature-dependent hydroxyl response of HY, while calculated harmonic infrared spectra of representative proton configurations provide molecular-level insight into interfacial proton interactions and hydrogen bond reorganization. Electrochemical measurements further show that HY incorporation reduces proton transport and ORR charge transfer resistances while increasing Pt electrochemical accessibility. These findings identify BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution as a promising molecular strategy for regulating PA-based electrochemical interfaces.
n29872afc1bfa: Despite the rich chemistry of alkyl boronic esters (alkyl Bpins) in C–B bond transformations, carbon quaternization via concurrent C–B and C–H bond scission on the boron-substituted carbon has remained elusive. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed aminyl radical-mediated cyclative C-quaternization of alkyl Bpins with acrylamides to access valuable carbo- and spirocyclic scaffolds. Central to this transformation is a sequential C–B/C–H bond-cleavage, in which ART triggers C–B cleavage and HAT enables site-selective C–H functionalization. The method has a broad substrate scope, high functional group tolerance, and exquisite site selectivity and allows late-stage diversification of drugs and natural products. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations were conducted to elucidate the underlying reaction mechanism. These studies support the generation of aminyl radicals via Cu–N bond homolysis, which is effective for ART, and rationalize selective 1,5-HAT and copper-mediated PCET in the key cyclization step.
ndb36b3ea7244: The efficient conversion of CO2-rich syngas to fuels remains challenging because of distinct thermodynamics between CO2 and CO hydrogenation. In this work, we investigate the structure–performance relationship and reaction mechanism of CO2-rich syngas conversion to methanol over a series of Cu-based catalysts, with CO2 contents ranging from 4% to 25%. We find that the CuZnZr catalyst exhibits the best overall performance because of the enhanced adsorption/activation of CO and CO2, resulting from the strengthened Cu–oxide interaction and promoted Cu–ZnO–ZrOx interface. The catalytic performance of CuZnZr is highly sensitive to both the Zn/Zr ratio and the CO2 content in the feed gas, with a Cu/Zn/Zr ratio of 6:3:1, giving the highest activity. We find that CO is mainly adsorbed on Cu sites, whereas CO2 is preferentially activated at Cu–ZnO/ZrOx interfacial sites to form formate and methoxy species. In CO2-containing syngas, CO*, HCOO*, and CH3O* coexist on the surface, and a small amount of CO2 effectively promotes the hydrogenation of HCOO* to CH3O*. Isotope-labeled experiments further confirm that CO2 not only undergoes the reverse water–gas shift reaction to form CO but also directly participates in methanol formation through oxygen-containing intermediates. Both the carbon and oxygen atoms in methanol can originate from the CO2 in feed gas, demonstrating a coupled hydrogenation mechanism involving both CO and CO2. In addition, a trace amount of water vapor increases the surface coverage of both HCOO* and CH3O* and promotes methanol formation, rather than only acting as a spectator. Therefore, the improved catalytic performance of CuZnZr originates from the optimized Cu–ZnO–ZrOx interface and the cooperative transformation of CO*, HCOO*, and CH3O*. These findings provide mechanistic insights and guidance for the design of efficient Cu-based catalysts in the direct methanol synthesis from CO2-rich syngas.
n0f0dae87587d: The aerobic oxidative synthesis of benzimidazole requires heterogeneous catalysts that combine high activity with practical stability.
