Because conventional catalyst optimization depends heavily on laborious experimental screening, we established an interpretable machine learning (ML) workflow to accelerate catalyst selection and identify the variables governing performance. An XGBoost model was trained to relate catalyst descriptors and reaction conditions to benzimidazole synthesis, and partial-dependence-plot (PDP) analysis was used to determine favorable catalyst compositions and operating windows. Guided by the model, we prepared the cobalt-based dual-site catalyst CoNP-CoSA@NC-800. Under mild conditions (90 °C, 9 h) with atmospheric air as the oxidant, this material delivered 100% conversion and 96% benzimidazole selectivity. It also tolerated a broad range of substrates and retained its activity during recycling. Control experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that the Co nanoparticle (CoNP) and Co single atom (CoSA) sites act cooperatively: the CoNP component modifies the d-band center and electronic structure of CoNP-CoSA@NC-800, thereby enhancing O2 adsorption and activation to facilitate benzimidazole formation.
nb6555785ba42: In-depth understanding of the reconstruction behaviors during photothermal reactions is of paramount importance for the design of highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, we demonstrate the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets during the photothermal reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction. Specifically, under the operating photothermal reaction conditions, the MoS2 nanosheet catalyst undergoes rapid surface temperature increase up to around 380 °C, which can react with the H2 gas to produce in-plane S vacancies, thereby leading to the reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets for enhanced RWGS reaction activity. An approximately 7.8 mmol g–1 h–1 evolution rate with a near-unity selectivity of CO (>99%) is achieved over MoS2 nanosheets during 100 h stability testing under flow-bed reaction and atmospheric pressure. Detailed structural characterizations combined with density functional theory simulations unravel that the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 can facilitate the charge separation and adsorption of reactants, lower the energy barrier of the *COOH intermediate, and meanwhile, improve the H2 dissociation ability for promoting the RWGS reaction.
n1cee8d003486: The straightforward construction of sterically hindered α-tertiary primary amines remains a stubborn challenge in organic synthesis. Although a wide array of approaches for the synthesis of this motif has been developed, the leveraging of ketimines as an amine source is underexplored. General reductive alkylative additions of unactivated alkyl halides to N-unprotected ketimines remain unknown. Herein, we disclose a nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling between N-unprotected heteroaryl ketimines and readily available alkyl halides, including primary, secondary, and tertiary ones, to directly furnish diverse primary amines with steric congestion without attendant deprotection sequences. This synthetic protocol circumvents the use of preformed organometallic reagents, leading to broad functional group tolerance and high step-economy. Preliminary mechanistic investigations support a radical-type cross-coupling pathway of N-H ketimines with unactivated alkyl radicals involving a Ni(I)/Ni(II)/Ni(III) redox cycle. The practicality of this method has been demonstrated in successful application in the synthesis of various cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors.
n35b1c449a8fb: Electrolyte cations in the electric double layer strongly influence electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multicarbon products, yet the microscopic origin of this cation effect remains elusive. Using metadynamics-biased ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we identify a cation-driven electrostatic traction mechanism, where the cation-induced local electric field promotes the interfacial water activation and directly steers nascent protons toward adsorbed *CO2 via an Eley–Rideal path, effectively bypassing the Volmer H adsorption intermediate as the dominant channel under these interfacial conditions. At the electrified interface, strong electronic coupling in this inner-sphere proton-coupled electron transfer process renormalizes the classical solvent reorganization energy to effective quantum reorganization energy, flattening the reaction potential energy surface. We further establish an adiabatic Marcus–Stark framework by nonlinearly coupling the interfacial electric field with the effective reorganization energy, which quantitatively accounts for a substantial part of the experimentally observed exponential acceleration of C2 product formation with K+ over Li+ and identifies interfacial proton supply as an important rate-modulating factor within the broader C2 reaction network. This finding partially decouples reaction kinetics from intermediate binding energy scaling relations, providing a physical framework for manipulating electrochemical selectivity through interfacial microenvironment engineering.
n7b4d1dceb62a: [PdCl2(NCPh)2] catalyzes the denitrogenation of mono(alkyl) diazirines in CDCl3 at 25 °C for 16 h to form the corresponding alkene in up to 70% yield. Reaction of (4-fluorophenyl)diazirine with a catalytic amount of [PdCl2(NCPh)2] (20 mol %) and excess styrene forms 1-(4-fluorophenyl)-2-phenylcyclopropane in 48% yield (cis/trans = 6.7:1). Kinetic experiments, in situ analysis of palladium coordination complexes, and DFT calculations support a mechanism for Pd(II)-catalyzed denitrogenation of benzyl diazirine involving C─N oxidative addition (ΔG‡ = 22.4 kcal/mol) of a four-coordinate trans-palladium σ-diazirine complex to form a five-coordinate Pd(IV) diazometallacyclobutane complex. Subsequent Pd─C bond cleavage (ΔG‡ = 8.8 kcal/mol) to form an N-bound diazo complex followed by isomerization to the corresponding C-bound diazo complex, presumably via intermolecular ligand exchange, and facile (ΔG‡ = 4.2 kcal/mol) extrusion of dinitrogen forms a trans-palladium alkylidene complex. Concerted, 1,2-H migration (ΔG‡ = 5.0 kcal/mol) forms the corresponding four-coordinate palladium π-styrene complex.
nea327f3ebd21: 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) have emerged as versatile strained precursors to saturated, three-dimensional azetidine scaffolds that are increasingly valuable in modern drug discovery. This Perspective contends that the recent proliferation of radical-based catalytic platforms, encompassing photoredox, metallaphotoredox, energy-transfer, and electrochemical manifolds, serves as an effective complement to classical polar chemistry, enabling diverse transformations and the construction of sterically congested carbon–carbon and carbon–heteroatom bonds through distinct reactivity profiles. We illustrate how open-shell intermediates enable the precise, regiodivergent, and multicomponent construction of sterically congested azetidines and azabicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes. We argue that while several mechanistic patterns have now been proposed, their underlying reactivity principles remain incompletely understood, and the broader synthetic potential remains largely underexplored. We therefore chart a forward-looking agenda: the development of alternative radical transformations, the expansion of radical coupling partners to include abundant and readily available feedstocks, the integration of electrochemistry for scalable and catalyst-free processes, and the design of radical relay sequences that access architecturally complex bridged azabicycles beyond simple azetidines. By framing these frontiers as both timely and achievable, we aim to catalyze the evolution of radical ABB chemistry from a specialized tool into a broadly enabling strategy for constructing the nitrogen-containing, sp3-rich chemical space that next-generation drug discovery demands.
n553290503ff6: The CO production by the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a promising bridge between CO2 conversion and well-established C1 chemistry. Currently, heterogeneous catalysts are mostly reported for this reaction, which usually require high operating temperatures (above 600 °C) and encounter poor selectivity of CO at lower temperatures (below 400 °C). Homogeneous catalysis may offer distinct advantages at a low temperature. Nevertheless, only some noble metal homogeneous catalysts for this reaction have been reported to date. Herein, we report the iron phthalocyanine (FePc) as a homogeneous catalyst to selectively produce CO via the RWGS reaction in the N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) solvent. The reaction started at a low temperature of 120 °C with a CO selectivity of 98.1%, and high CO selectivity was attained under various conditions. Large-scale DFT calculations and control experiments revealed a tri-active-center mechanism, wherein the Fe center and Pc ligand separately and simultaneously activate CO2 and H2 and then cooperatively catalyze their conversion to CO and H2O. In addition, this work quantitatively demonstrates that the dispersion interactions between the catalyst and solvent molecules play a critical role in homogeneous transition-metal-catalyzed CO2 conversion reactions.
n37a6a8d2599a: Photoelectrochemical seawater oxidation is limited by a coupled interfacial challenge: low-coordinated metal sites that favor hole utilization and oxygen evolution are also susceptible to chloride attack, whereas protective surface modification can compromise water access. Here, oxygen vacancies in amorphous NiCr2O4–x on α-Fe2O3 are repurposed to direct multidentate phytate coordination, constructing a molecular interface that couples Ni-site polarization with interfacial hydration. Catalyst-facing M–O–P coordination withdraws electron density from vacancy-activated Ni sites, strengthens interfacial polarization, accelerates hole delivery, and reconstructs oxygenated-intermediate bonding, lowering the free-energy requirement of the *O → *OOH step from 0.66 to 0.45 eV. Meanwhile, electrolyte-facing phosphate groups remain exposed as persistent hydrogen-bonding nodes, preferentially stabilize O-down interfacial water, and organize a continuous hydration network that preserves H2O/OH– accessibility while suppressing Cl– approach and adsorption. Operando infrared spectroscopy, in situ ATR-SEIRAS, molecular dynamics simulations, ion mapping, and dissolution analyses collectively connect this coupled solid–liquid interfacial regulation with accelerated intermediate turnover and reduced corrosion. The resulting photoanode delivers 4.43 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V versus RHE, operates for 300 h with negligible decay in alkaline simulated seawater, and retains 82% of its initial photocurrent after 200 h in alkaline real seawater. These results establish vacancy-directed molecular coordination as a strategy for coupling active-site polarization with hydration-mediated protection in durable seawater photooxidation.
nfdfce8ff68eb: Wadsley-Roth W3Nb14O44 is a fast-charging anode material but suffers from low electronic conductivity and electrochemical polarization. Here, anion-sublattice engineering is employed to regulate its electronic structure and Li+ storage kinetics. Density functional theory and kinetic analyses reveal that an appropriate concentration of oxygen vacancies enhances electronic conductivity, moderates Li+ adsorption, and facilitates Li+ diffusion, thereby reducing charge-transfer and diffusion impedances at low temperatures. In situ XRD and synchrotron radiation X-ray 3D nanocomputed tomography reveal reversible structural evolution with near-zero residual strain after cycling. Consequently, WNO-x delivers 77.4 mAh g–1 at 200 C and retains 72.6% capacity after 6000 cycles at 100 C while exhibiting low-temperature electrochemical activity. Moreover, the WNO-x||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cell delivers 85.8 mAh g–1 at 20 C and retains 77.1% capacity after 3000 cycles, with cycling capability at –30 °C. Such structure-property insight provides a strategy for designing niobium-based oxide anodes toward fast-charging and low-temperature batteries.
n1b1968ab57b1: A more profound understanding of battery interfaces, characterized by multiple components and dynamic interactions, can provide a theoretical foundation for the development of next-generation energy storage systems. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technology is enhancing scientific paradigms, offering significant benefits for the study of complex battery interfaces. Here, we examine how AI can facilitate a deeper understanding of these intricate interfaces in batteries, promote more standardized characterization analyses, and assist in designing interface materials. The introduction of AI models may facilitate the discovery of additional mechanisms and materials. Moreover, we discuss the trade-off between interpretability and accuracy in AI models, as well as the risk of narrow cognitive perspectives among researchers. We hope this perspective will inspire and advance the technological integration of AI in battery interface research.
n3073ef6b28de: Electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) to formic acid (HCOOH) provides a carbon-neutral route. SnO2-based catalysts suffer from limited activity and instability at industrial current densities. We develop a Cu-doped highly porous SnO2 catalyst (SnO2-Cu) that enhances activity and stabilizes the SnO2 framework. The porous structure exposes numerous active sites while confining local OH– within the bulk acid electrolyte, enabling high-current-density operation. Cu doping strengthens CO2 chemisorption and Sn–O bond covalency, boosting CO2RR activity while suppressing SnO2 self-reduction. SnO2-Cu sustains 1000 mA cm–2 for 19 h with 98.5% FE and 800 mA cm–2 for 72 h with 94.1% FE in a flow cell at pH 1.82. It achieves a HCOOH production cost of 722.7 USD tonne–1 in a solid-state electrolyte (SSE) device calculated based on onshore wind power, demonstrating economic competitiveness. This work demonstrates that rational Cu doping of porous SnO2 addresses activity and durability limits, offering an effective platform for high-rate, economically viable HCOOH electrosynthesis.
n58f93f4106ae: Interfacial degradation and dendritic lithium (Li) growth remain critical bottlenecks for practical Li metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we introduce a tough, ion-conductive poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate) (pDMAEMA) nanolayer on Li metal via photo-initiated chemical vapor deposition (piCVD). The photo-mediated, solvent-free piCVD enables nanometer-scale coatings with systematic control over photo-crosslinking and chain entanglement without compromising Li surface integrity. This systematic control yields an optimized polymer network balancing toughness (36.3 MJ m–3) and viscoelasticity (10.3% linear viscoelastic strain limit) to accommodate repeated Li volume changes. Furthermore, interactions between pDMAEMA and PF6– anions promote a mechanically durable LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, thereby supporting uniform Li deposition. Pouch-type bi-cells employing the optimized 100 nm polymer-coated Li anode achieve an energy density of 338 Wh kg–1 and 80% capacity retention after 90 cycles under practical conditions (N/P = 2, E/C = 3 g Ah–1). This ultrathin, tough polymer network offers a promising design principle for high-energy LMBs.
n5ea6661c07b7: The long-term stability of high-efficiency n-i-p perovskite solar cells is limited by coupled defect migration, residual lattice strain, and thermal–mechanical degradation. Here, we develop a non-ionic, interface-enriched zinc phthalocyanine derivative, 4PCSZnPc, as a molecular stabilizer for simultaneous defect anchoring and strain buffering. Unlike ionic additives that may introduce mobile species, 4PCSZnPc is distributed throughout the film, with enrichment near the buried SnO2/perovskite interface. Peripheral N/O/S heteroatoms coordinate with under-coordinated Pb2+ sites, while the Zn-regulated macrocyclic center interacts with iodide-related defects, forming dual-site Lewis acid–base anchoring. Meanwhile, the rigid phthalocyanine framework reduces residual tensile stress and may hinder strain-assisted ion migration. These combined effects of defect passivation and strain buffering reduce non-radiative recombination, improve film uniformity, and enhance thermal robustness. Consequently, 4PCSZnPc-treated devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.88% (certified 26.74%), a T80 lifetime of 1358 h under 1-sun at 85 °C, and 95% retention after 200 thermal cycles, providing a design principle for future thermally resilient photovoltaics.
na8c3b15efeb0: Anionic redox reaction (ARR) promises high energy density for Li-rich cathodes yet suffers from severe voltage decay. Here, we investigate ARR voltage modulation in a Li2S-modified quasi-solid Li-rich cathode (Li2S-LRM), which exhibits a distinct low-voltage ARR plateau (2.0–2.8 V). Combining in situ XRD, S K-edge XANES, EELS, Ar-etched XPS and DFT calculations, we validate in situ electrochemical sulfur doping. Upon cycling, the material forms bulk LixS/Li–S–O species alongside a dominant Li2SO3/Li2SO4 polyanion interphase that realizes oxygen trapping. Vacancy-cluster formation facilitates reversible S-involved charge compensation, where sulfur redox activity progressively intensifies during long cycling. Enabled by the band-modulation and oxygen-trapping effects, Li2S-LRM achieves a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.6% and suppressed voltage decay (0.28 vs. 0.83 mV cycle–1 for pristine LRM). This work deepens mechanistic insights into ARR and provides rational design guidance for high-performance anionic-redox cathodes.
n5487decdaca2: Perovskite/organic tandem solar cells (PO-TSCs) offer a route toward overcoming the efficiency limitations of single-junction photovoltaics. However, wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite sub-cells limit their performance, where uncontrolled crystallization leads to compositional heterogeneity, defect accumulation, and severe halide phase segregation. Here, we develop a template-bridge dual-control (TBDC) strategy using 2-thiophenemethylammonium bromide (2-ThMAB). Precisely controlling the introduction timing and spatial distribution of 2-ThMAB maximizes molecular regulation of crystallization. Surface-anchored 2-ThMAB molecules act as growth templates to induce (100) crystal growth, while grain-boundary-localized molecules regulate halide migration through molecular bridging, enabling homogeneous crystallization. The WBG perovskite films exhibit enhanced out-of-plane (100) orientation, reduced defect density, and suppressed halide phase segregation. Consequently, the optimized WBG device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.13% with improved operational stability. Integrated into PO-TSCs, the optimized WBG sub-cells deliver a PCE of 26.62%. This strategy enables concurrent control of crystallization and halide redistribution of efficient, stable tandem photovoltaics.
na81fc644f18d: Resolving how ensemble growth kinetics emerge from particle- and grain-level dynamics is essential for predictive control of nanocrystal synthesis. Here, time-resolved four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM), extended into five dimensions (5DSTEM) through continuous acquisition, is used to simultaneously resolve morphology, crystallographic orientation, and lattice strain during Au nanocrystal growth in aqueous HAuCl4. Although ensemble growth follows surface-reaction-limited kinetics, individual nanoparticles exhibit distinct pathways, including continuous growth and discrete coalescence through oriented attachment. These pathways display characteristic orientation dynamics, with stable or gradually selected orientations during continuous growth and abrupt reconfiguration followed by alignment during coalescence. At the ensemble level, the out-of-plane orientation distribution is established early and remains stable, whereas in-plane orientations remain broadly distributed without global alignment. Tensile strain develops progressively from particle surfaces and interfaces, directly linking lattice distortion with evolving morphology and crystallographic structure. By connecting ensemble kinetics with particle- and grain-resolved structural evolution, 5DSTEM provides a general framework for uncovering heterogeneous growth mechanisms and for relating synthesis pathways to structure-dependent properties in functional nanomaterials.
nf8fcafb72145: Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.
n9777533476f5: Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.
n009ed70db8e5: Copper is a powerful catalyst for the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), but it faces challenges with selectivity and stability dependent on its structural characteristics. We developed a platform that combines graphitized carbon nanofibers with identical-location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) to study individual copper nanoparticles at the atomic scale under various reaction conditions. Notably, we observed that competing phenomena such as Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation coexist in the same reaction area, with the latter being qualitatively consistent with a charge-driven fission pathway in larger nanoparticles (>10 nm). By tracking uniquely identifiable nanoparticles both individually and in groups, our findings focus on the range of surface-confined restructuring pathways during CO2RR. This contrasts with solution-mediated phenomena, such as dissolution–precipitation, which dominate under open-circuit potential (OCP) and significantly destabilize the catalyst prior to the reaction, highlighting the importance of eliminating this effect. Under CO2RR conditions, Cu nanoparticles are highly sensitive to subtle variations in the support’s nanotexture, defects, and electronic structure, leading to the coexistence of counteracting mechanisms we observed. These observations provide a structural framework for understanding the dynamic behavior of copper-on-carbon catalysts under CO2RR conditions, guiding the development of strategies to improve catalyst stability and performance.
n5458f0c98114: Quantum geometric quantities, such as Berry curvature (BC) and quantum metric, are known to govern the physical and topological properties of materials, making access to these quantities critically important for the comprehensive understanding of the materials. Chiral crystals offer a natural platform in which structural handedness can control quantum geometry and nonlinear transport, but direct experimental access to the quantum geometric quantities has remained elusive. Here, we show that trigonal tellurium (Te) hosts an enantiomer-dependent Berry curvature dipole (BCD) that can be accessed through the measurement of the cross-axial nonlinear Hall effect (NHE), unlike in previously studied in-plane configurations, where the BCD contribution vanishes. Angle-resolved measurements on left- and right-handed Te devices reveal a second-order transverse response whose sign reverses with crystal chirality. The extracted cross-axial nonlinear susceptibility, χyxz, exceeds the in-plane susceptibility, χxxx, by more than two-fold, indicating a strong BCD-driven contribution. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to a topologically nontrivial hedgehog-like BC texture near the H points and predict a BCD that reverses sign between opposite enantiomers, consistent with experiment. These results establish cross-axial nonlinear Hall transport as a symmetry-selective probe of chirality-controlled quantum geometry in tellurium and related chiral materials.
ne11169da3fc1: Interfacing integrated photonics with solid-state spin defects holds great promise for future quantum networks, but the scaling of spin-photon architectures is hindered by frequency mismatches arising from fabrication-induced variations in photonic cavity resonances and inhomogeneous optical transition frequencies of individual spins. These challenges call for a photonic platform with deterministic and wide-range tunability. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid nanophotonic platform based on direct bonding of silicon carbide photonic crystal nanocavity arrays onto a thin-film lithium niobate-on-insulator, enabling deterministic electrical tuning of multiple SiC nanocavities into mutual spectral resonance. By exploiting the strong electro-optic response of lithium niobate, we achieve continuous and wide-range cavity tuning of 380 GHz (∼1.1 nm), sufficient to compensate both cavity disorder and spin spectral inhomogeneity. The nanocavities balance strong optical confinement with electrical tunability, exhibiting a theoretical Purcell factor of approximately 400. This hybrid platform enables electrically reconfigurable spin-photon interfaces for large-scale integrated quantum photonics.
n7e2ca15a8467: Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.
n2c776367b69d: The development of scintillators that maintain excellent performance under high temperatures is a critical challenge. Here, by simply replacing the triphenylphosphine ligand with its fluorinated analogue, we successfully switched the emission pathway of Cu2I2 clusters from pure phosphorescence to a hybrid phosphorescence/thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) mechanism, enabling adaptive high-temperature X-ray imaging. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the fluorination strategy reduces the singlet–triplet energy gap to an exceptionally small value of 35 meV, thereby promoting efficient reverse intersystem crossing. The TADF contribution reaches 95.7% at room temperature. This temperature-responsive characteristic endows the fluorinated cluster with adaptive X-ray imaging capability across a broad temperature window from 293 to 413 K, overcoming the thermal quenching phenomenon in traditional phosphorescence-only scintillators. This work establishes a molecular design approach for smart scintillators capable of reliable operation in demanding thermal environments.
na2120e31b77c: Isolated, undercoordinated metal atoms exhibit enhanced reactivity central to catalysis, yet their stabilization on surfaces remains challenging. In heterogeneous single-atom catalysis, activity derives from interactions between individual atoms and a host matrix, but the absence of stabilizing ligands often leads to diffusion, aggregation, and sintering, obscuring structure–activity relationships. On metal surfaces, reactivity is typically limited to sparse, dynamic, undercoordinated sites lining step edges or lattice defects. Here we report a defect-engineering strategy to stabilize isolated adatoms on dilute metal alloy substrates. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals a high density of uniformly distributed adatoms on Au–Cu(111) terraces that persist under thermal cycling. Combined experiments and modeling attribute this stability to alloy-induced subsurface dislocation networks that trap adatoms and suppress diffusion, forming a two-dimensional frozen gas. These adatoms act as a reactive reservoir, enabling on-surface coordination chemistry inaccessible on pure metals, and providing insights into atomic-scale processes on the surfaces of defect-engineered alloys with implications for heterogeneous catalysis.
n9aa4c679df3b: Carbon materials with superior porosity and conductivity are widely adopted in aqueous zinc–iodine batteries to host iodine, but suffer from the polyiodide shuttle and cycling stability challenges. Traditional strategies mainly focus on pore structure engineering or heteroatom doping of carbon hosts to confine iodine, but fail to address the sluggish iodine conversion kinetics. Herein, we initially reveal the significant yet overlooked role of hybridization state in reforming the carbon intrinsic activity toward high-efficiency iodine conversion chemistry. With pitch-derived porous carbon as an example, we controllably regulate the C(sp2)/C(sp3) ratio (from 1.23 to 2.21) while maintaining high surface area. These properties lower the activation energy of iodine conversion and effectively suppress the polyiodide shuttle. The zinc–iodine battery exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability after 150,000 cycles and a low self-discharging rate with only 12.5% capacity loss after 20 days. Ah-level pouch cell with 66.6 mgiodine cm–2 achieves a cumulative discharging capacity of 103.51 Ah. The hybridization engineering was successfully extended to commercial porous carbon (YP-50F), prolonging the lifespan from 7425 to 27,000 cycles. This work presents a hybridization state engineering strategy to reform the intrinsic activity of the carbon host to favor the iodine conversion chemistry and beyond.
nb269684ace9c: Photoactivated metal-oxide gas sensors reduce the energy demand associated with continuous heating, yet selective detection of volatile organic compounds remains constrained by weak electrical transduction and complex surface oxidation pathways. Here, Au-functionalized anatase TiO2 nanofibers (Au/aTiO2 NFs) were integrated with a 395 nm microlight-emitting diode (LED) for low-power formaldehyde (HCHO) sensing. One-pot electrospinning followed by calcination enabled systematic control of Au loading while preserving the anatase nanofiber architecture. Au loading regulated TiO2 crystallite growth, defect states, dispersion, interfacial Au chemical states, and photoexcited carrier relaxation. At 0.15 wt % Au, finely dispersed Au nanoparticles produced a distinct Au/TiO2 interfacial environment and carrier-relaxation behavior, whereas higher loadings induced nanoparticle aggregation and additional nonradiative energy-loss pathways. Under UV micro-LED illumination at 2.63 mW, the optimized sensor exhibited a response of 1093 toward 1 ppm of HCHO, an estimated detection limit of 4.9 ppb, and stable operation over 40 consecutive cycles. Density functional theory calculations further supported the loading-dependent selectivity, showing that changes in the local Au environment selectively modify HCHO adsorption and bond reconstruction. These results identify local Au-site density as a key design parameter governing interfacial reactivity and molecular selectivity in low-power photoactivated gas sensing.
n606c78c35d0e: Optical control of photochromic properties is essential for optoelectronic devices. The manipulation of such properties has been limited to the microscale because of the wave nature of light; however, scaling down the volume is highly demanded for the future nanosized devices. Herein, we demonstrate optical switching at the nanoscale in an organic photochromic material. Photochromic materials such as diarylethene derivatives exhibit two different states with distinct optical and electronic properties under ultraviolet (UV) and visible light irradiation. We employed plasmon nanofocusing for optical switching of photochromic materials, which allowed the creation of a nanolight source at the apex of a tapered aluminum structure over a broad frequency range. We achieved in situ wavelength control between visible and UV light at the nanoscale for photochromic reactions. Using this technique, we demonstrated nanoscale optical switching between the two states of diarylethene. The switching performance was confirmed for at least nine cycles without degradation. This demonstration would constitute a significant step toward next-generation optoelectronic devices and benefit diverse scientific fields owing to the broad wavelength tunability of plasmon nanofocusing.
nddf390e7c0ec: Electrochemical-metallization (ECM) memristors can implement both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching, making them attractive for neuromorphic and reservoir computing; however, the stochastic formation of metallic filaments causes variability in the threshold voltage and switching instability. Here, we report a van der Waals α-In2Se3-based ferroelectric-semiconductor ECM (FeS-ECM) memristor in which a bidirectionally polarized α-In2Se3 layer is inserted between the inert electrode and the switching layer. The out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, programmed through a decoupled in-plane poling terminal, deterministically selects within the low-compliance operating regime between nonvolatile bipolar memory switching and volatile unipolar threshold switching within a single device, with a coefficient of variation in the set voltage of 4.7% and stable operation over more than 9000 cycles. Exploiting these two modes, a single α-In2Se3 platform exhibits both the volatile reservoir dynamics and the nonvolatile conductance modulation required for the readout weights of a physical reservoir-computing system, in which the pulse width electrically programs multiple relaxation time constants. This pulse-width multitime scale reconfigurability enables efficient temporal information processing, demonstrated through MNIST classification and chaotic time-series prediction.
nc8feefc5c30e: Antigenic variation severely constrains the durability and breadth of vaccine-induced protection against rapidly evolving viruses. Although conserved epitopes can support cross-variant immunity, antibody responses to viral glycoproteins are often biased toward exposed, mutable immunodominant epitopes, leaving conserved protective sites subdominant. Here, we present a modular “shield-and-amplify” nanoparticle vaccination strategy to redirect immunodominance toward this subdominant epitope. We engineered site-specific N-linked glycans─alongside the native N343 glycan to mask variable immunodominant regions while preserving accessibility to the class 5 epitope. The resulting glycan-masked RBD antigen (RGM) was displayed on p239 nanoparticles via nanobody-mediated assembly, yielding multivalent RGM@p239 immunogens. Antigenic profiling revealed that glycan shielding preserved recognition by 6D6 and 7D6 antibodies while reducing binding of representative class 1–4 antibodies by at least 80%. In immunized animals, RGM@p239 enriched 7D6-competitive serum antibodies blocking approximately 70–80% of serum binding to RGM and broadened cross-variant neutralization against 8 representative variant strains, including detectable activity against Omicron lineages. Furthermore, RGM@p239 reduced disease severity after Omicron EG.1 challenge in a hamster model. These results support a model in which glycan shielding and nanoparticle multivalency act as complementary immune-focusing modules: shielding attenuates competing responses, while multivalency amplifies responses to conserved subdominant epitopes. This study establishes a nanovaccine design strategy to address antigenic variation by focusing immunity on conserved viral vulnerabilities.
n20b03cc93c65: Cochlear implantation (CI) provides effective auditory rehabilitation for patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Implantation can nevertheless induce local foreign body response (FBR) and cochlear fibrosis, motivating strategies to reduce tissue reactions and preserve cochlear integrity. Therefore, more precise strategies are needed to modulate macrophage-mediated FBR after CI. Here, through transcriptomic profiling of cochlear tissues from rats 30 days after cochlear implantation, we identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as a prominent signature after CI. In vitro assays further verified the role of MSR1 in reshaping macrophage phenotype and inflammatory activation. To achieve targeted MSR1 regulation in the cochlea, we engineered iRGD-modified extracellular vesicles to deliver siMSR1 (iRGD-EV/siMSR1). iRGD modification enhanced macrophage uptake of EV and enabled efficient siRNA delivery. In a rat CI model, local administration of iRGD-EV/siMSR1 reduced cochlear fibrotic tissue formation and decreased fibrosis-related protein expression. Moreover, iRGD-EV/siMSR1 preserved spiral ganglion neurons and myelin structures, contributing to residual hearing protection after implantation. Early stage analysis at 7 days after implantation showed that iRGD-EV/siMSR1 suppressed macrophage inflammatory activation, reduced TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling, regulated matrix remodeling, and limited early apoptosis. These findings identify MSR1 as a promising molecular target for cochlear implant-induced FBR and support iRGD-EV/siMSR1 as a potentially translatable strategy for attenuating cochlear fibrosis and preserving the cochlear neural interface, also highlighting the importance of considering neural health when modulating macrophage-mediated responses to cochlear implants.
nb984ddc9d168: We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.
n47cce99067d5: Mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolic imbalance in senescent bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are critical pathological foundations for senile bone regeneration. Here, an ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold was constructed by anchoring barium titanate-transition metal carbide (MXene@BaTiO3) heterojunctions on the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) to reactivate mitochondrial energy metabolism and promote bone regeneration under senescence-associated bone loss conditions. These heterojunctions adhere to BMSC membranes and generate electrical stimulation upon ultrasound stimulation, which significantly inhibits abnormal opening of mitochondrial permeability transition pores (mPTP), reduces leakage of mtDNA and Cyt c, and maintains membrane potential stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that electrical stimulation activates the PI3K/Akt/MDM2 signaling axis to promote the degradation of accumulated p53, which relieves the competitive binding of p53 to TRAP1, thereby restoring TRAP1-CypD-mediated mPTP gating and mitochondrial homeostasis. Consequently, this ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold drives mitochondrial energy metabolism and osteogenic differentiation of senescence-like BMSCs in vitro, which is further confirmed in a rat model. These results demonstrate the potential of this electroactive scaffold as a regulator of mitochondrial energy metabolism for senescence-associated bone regeneration.

n94e1b2f5c96c: Different from the problematic elemental sulfur cathodes that suffer from severe polysulfide shuttling, the prepared a-CoS5 stabilizes an unprecedentedly high covalent sulfur content (∼73 wt %) and enables highly reversible S–S bond cleavage and reformation without forming dissolved polysulfides. As a result, it delivers an exceptionally large capacity and long cyclability, thus establishing new benchmarks for simultaneously achieving high sulfur content and long cyclability among currently reported sulfur and sulfur-equivalent cathode materials for Li-S batteries.
n0b632bd0cb36: Multicomponent vapor-deposited organic glasses are essential in organic electronic applications, but achieving controlled component segregation at the nano/mesoscale remains a challenge, hindering the rational development of high-performance devices. In this study, we investigate binary organic semiconductor mixtures of TPD (N,N′-Bis(3-methylphenyl)-N,N′-diphenylbenzidine) and TCTA (Tris(4-carbazoyl-9-ylphenyl)amine). Despite being miscible in the bulk liquid state, the co-deposited glassy films of these two organic semiconductors exhibit a range of segregation behaviors, from homogeneous to clearly phase-separated structures. We employed differential scanning calorimetry and resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) to study the component segregation behavior and used the National Institute of Standards and Technology RSoXS Simulation Suite, paired with Atomic Force Microscopy, to interpret the energy-dependent RSoXS spectra. Our results indicate that component segregation in co-deposited TPD/TCTA films is due to a kinetically-arrested nucleation-and-growth mechanism, in contrast to the segregation mechanism of a previously reported TPD/DO37 (disperse orange 37) mixture which is strongly immiscible in bulk. This work provides a demonstration of tunable molecular aggregation in organic semiconductor glasses, enabling access to a continuum of morphologies from homogeneously mixed to segregated phases.
nf12847c6df0b: Colloidal CsPbBr3 nanocrystals can be highly emissive, yet their chemical robustness is dictated by their native surface chemistry. Here, we show that aliphatic acids interact fundamentally differently with distinct CsPbBr3 surface terminations: they are largely benign toward conventional bromine-rich ammonium-passivated surfaces but strongly destabilizing toward carboxylate-capped, Pb-rich, Br-deficient surfaces synthesized in lauric acid-menthol deep eutectic solvent (DES). In the latter case, acid exposure quenches photoluminescence and sharply shortens the lifetime, indicating efficient activation of nonradiative decay pathways. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and 1H NMR reveal a PbBr2-terminated surface in which laurate is the dominant X-type ligand, while the DES stabilizes oleylammonium in the bulk through hydrogen-bonding interactions and thereby biases the nanocrystal surface toward carboxylate passivation. Density functional theory further shows that laurate is the thermodynamically viable bound ligand, whereas protonation to neutral lauric acid renders adsorption unfavorable once the entropic cost of binding is considered. Protonation-driven ligand desorption, therefore, exposes undercoordinated Pb and Br-vacancy motifs that act as electron traps. Further transient absorption spectroscopy links this surface transformation to ultrafast hot electron loss and rapid exciton trapping. These results reveal how the same class of aliphatic acids can be benign or fatal, depending on the initial surface termination and active ligand shell.
n3b613f551d52: The development of high-energy-density solid-state batteries is aided by the discovery of ionically conductive cathode active materials which can enable the production of cathode composites with high active material loadings. We find that the metastable Fd3̅m Li2FeCl4 phase produced by mechanochemical synthesis undergoes a room temperature structural re-ordering on the scale of months, which lowers the ionic conductivity and raises concerns for the shelf-life of metastable materials. We demonstrate that the structural disorder can be “locked-in” by introducing Mn2+ into the system without significantly impacting the ionic conductivity. We further elucidate the origin of the phase transitions and the role of enthalpic stabilization on ionic conductivity through density functional theory and machine-learning force field molecular dynamics calculations. These reveal a 3-dimensional Li+ conduction pathway in the disordered structure, which is not present when the material is ordered. By engineering high-conductivity disordered, Fd3̅m, phases of Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4, solid-state batteries containing zero catholyte are demonstrated with high voltage plateaus of 3.7 V and capacities of 115 mAh/gCAM and 90 mAh/gCAM, respectively. Considering the high cathode loadings, we demonstrate that the materials Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4 can be used to produce solid-state battery cathodes with higher energy densities than that of LiFePO4, with similar cost effectiveness.
n7b93781e4be7: The development of cost-effective alternatives to rhodium for catalytic NO reduction by CO remains urgent and challenging. Their activities exhibited a clear volcano-type dependence on the Ir content. Combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, in situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we revealed a synergistic bifunctional site mechanism, where Os sites promoted NO dissociation, while Ir sites enabled fast N−N coupling and CO oxidation, with electron transfer from Os to Ir further facilitating N2 formation. This work demonstrated solid-solution alloying as an effective strategy for designing high-performance, low-cost NOx-removal catalysts.
na00fd0187db4: A series of cluster oxides exhibiting a systematic increase in the degree of band condensation was synthesized by the reactive Sn-flux method: Ir3Sn12In3O14 (3-fold band), Ir2.3Ru1.7Sn19O18 (4-fold band), and Ir10Sn45O44 (5-fold band). The formal oxidation states were determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), and electronic band structure calculations reveal semiconducting band gaps consistent with the measured optical properties. Increasing band condensation is accompanied by a color change from red-orange for Ir3Sn12In3O14 to black for Ir10Sn45O44. Ir3Sn12In3O14 exhibits a photoluminescence emission centered at 566 nm (yellow light). These findings establish a homologous family of multilayer transition-metal/main-group cluster oxides with systematically tuneable crystal symmetry, electronic structure, nonlinear optical response, and optical properties.
nda78e5297508: Understanding and controlling the evolution of electrocatalyst structure, chemistry, and active sites under catalytically relevant conditions is critical in developing electrocatalysts with stable and durable activity toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Molybdenum (Mo) is routinely combined with cobalt hydroxide electrocatalysts to tune the electronic environment of the active sites and modulate their activity, contributing to improved OER activity. However, the phenomena that underpin the enhanced OER activity of the resulting materials largely stem from Mo dissolution, and their extent on the structure and activity remains elusive. Electrochemical benchmarking revealed that the high Mo content of electrodeposited CoMoOx(1:4) produces a Mo-rich surface with fewer accessible Co sites and slower charge-transfer kinetics, as evidenced by a Tafel slope of 73.1 ± 8.1 mV dec−1 and a high charge-transfer resistance of 5.74 Ω (over 4 times higher than CoMoOx(6:1)). Operando Raman spectroscopy, ex situ X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and inductively coupled plasma−optical emission spectroscopy collectively demonstrate that MoO42− dissolution begins on contact with 1 M KOH in the absence of applied potential and continues under anodic polarization, driving irreversible reconstruction of as-synthesized materials to Co(OH)2/Co3O4 sites and subsequently to CoOOH. These materials therefore function as pre-catalysts, and the working surface is determined by the starting composition rather than being the as-synthesized phase. Crucially, the reconstruction pathway is synthesis-dependent; crystalline hydrated CoMoO4(HT) proceeds via CoOOH to further-oxidized, partially deprotonated CoOOHx, at relevant OER conditions, whereas electrodeposited films form predominantly β-CoOOH as the surface species, with progression beyond CoOOH developing only partially and to an extent that scales with the initial Mo content. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for leveraging controlled cation dissolution to engineer defect-rich, high-performance electrocatalytic interfaces.

n78a01f1344cb: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are a promising next-generation energy storage technology, but their development is often constrained by the thermal instability and high cost of solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). Amorphous oxyhalide electrolytes, while mechanically deformable, are particularly susceptible to thermal degradation. Here, we report a novel and cost-effective composite SSE fabricated by embedding LaCl3 nanocrystals within an amorphous Li–Al–O–Cl (LAOC) matrix. This unique architecture synergistically combines the high ionic conductivity of the amorphous phase with the enhanced thermal and mechanical robustness imparted by the crystalline phase. The resulting Li–La–Al–O–Cl electrolyte achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity exceeding 1 mS cm–1 and demonstrates exceptional thermal stability, remaining a solid powder at 150 °C, a temperature at which the baseline LAOC melts. This enhanced thermal and thermo-mechanical integrity, combined with excellent deformability, enables superior interfacial contact and stability with cathodes. The Li–La–Al–O–Cl-based ASSBs maintain stable operation at 80 °C, in stark contrast to the rapid failure of LAOC-based cells. This strategy of reinforcing a soft amorphous matrix with a rigid crystalline offers a new pathway for designing thermally robust, high-performance, and commercially viable SSEs.
nfcacd6d53824: The synthesis, characterization, and catalytic polymerization results of an unprecedented double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complex (4) are discussed. Complex 4 is active for the polymerization of acetylenes. Complex 4 polymerizes tert-butylacetylene to form cyclic poly(tert-butylacetylene). Evidence for a cyclic polymer topology comes from size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and intrinsic viscosity (η) measurements. This unusual reactivity of complex 4 toward a tert-alkylacetylene is attributed to its fluxional behavior, which arises from the double tethering of an yne-ol proligand (2) that facilitates monomer access and catalytic turnover. The preliminary scope of this complex design is demonstrated through modification of the yne-ol proligand, which afforded two additional double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complexes 10 and 11 that are also catalytically active for polymerization.
na4b691b72564: The molybdopterin-dependent ergothioneine synthase (MES) from Caldithrix abyssi is the first molybdoenzyme known to catalyze the formation of carbon–sulfur bonds. To complete its catalytic cycle, this bifunctional enzyme desulfurates l-cysteine at a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate binding site and transfers the harvested sulfur atom (S0) to the molybdenum center of a bis-molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide cofactor more than 50 Å away. Subsequently, the sulfurated Mo-center transfers the labile sulfur atom onto the imidazole ring of Nα-trimethyl histidine (TMH). Combining experimental observations from cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, sequence-activity correlation, and substrate-specificity studies, we delineate the structural basis for long-distance sulfur transfer via a persulfide relay, the identity of the imidazole sulfurating species, and key sequence motifs that are indispensable for activity. Furthermore, the reversibility of MES-mediated sulfurization of TMH under physiological conditions suggests that ergothioneine may serve as a soluble reservoir of oxidizing equivalents, supporting anaerobic metabolism in deep-branching bacteria such as C. abyssi.
n6dd959bdb55e: Iodine chemistry has an outsized role in the atmosphere and environment due to its highly reactive nature. Unlike chlorine and bromine, around 80% of atmospheric iodine is emitted directly from the ocean through the reaction of iodide and ozone at the sea surface. Uncertainties remain, however, in the effects of hydration, salinity, temperature, and other factors on this globally significant reaction. Using linear ion-trap mass spectrometry, a single water molecule is shown here to provide a 23 (±6)-fold acceleration to the rate of iodide oxidation. The first step in reaction of both I– and I–·H2O with ozone is oxidation to IO– with subsequent fast reactions to yield IO3–. No evidence is found for direct routes from I–·H2O to IO2– nor any incorporation of the water oxygen into ionic products. Ab initio calculations show that the initial rate-determining step for both reactions proceeds on the singlet surface with water playing an active role to lower the barrier through hydrogen bonding. Kinetic modeling based on the computed energetics is in excellent agreement with experimental measurements and enables extrapolation of this reaction to lower temperatures relevant to polar regions and the ozone layer. This analysis shows that (i) I– may outcompete I• for ozone destruction as temperature decreases, and (ii) I–·H2O reacts more than an order of magnitude faster than I• over 350 to 230 K. This work demonstrates that iodide has a previously underappreciated role in multiphase ozone destruction in the atmosphere and lays the foundation for understanding microscopic environmental influences in salt clusters and nanodroplets.
n7635d3bad75f: The sustainable synthesis of nitric acid (HNO3) directly from air via N2 oxidation is a dream reaction but remains a long-standing challenge, owing to formidable thermodynamic and kinetic barriers. Here, we report a photoassisted thermocatalytic strategy in which acetaldehyde as a key medium enables efficient N2 oxidation to HNO3 under mild conditions. Acetaldehyde is oxidized to peracetic acid over 316L stainless steel, which subsequently generates radicals (CH3COOO•) under visible-light irradiation. These CH3COOO• radicals are highly reactive and can oxidize N2 at 200 °C and near-ambient pressures (1–5 bar), affording an HNO3 formation rate of 110.8 μmol h–1 with a concentration of 13,961 ppm and an N2 conversion of 0.45% within 2 h─approximately 2 to 4 orders of magnitude higher than previously reported systems. Notably, the kinetic irrelevance of H2O enables operation in a gas-phase flow configuration, allowing continuous and stable HNO3 production and gram-scale accumulation at the laboratory scale. This work introduces a groundbreaking reaction paradigm that couples organic radical chemistry and surface catalysis, offering a scalable and energy-efficient pathway for the green synthesis of HNO3.
n1173d7dcc5ae: The electrolyte and applied potential are known to impact a catalyst’s structure and performance, yet the role of reaction intermediates and products in driving surface evolution remains largely unexplored. Here, using electrochemical atomic force microscopy, we show that the dynamic restructuring of copper (Cu) surfaces during nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) directly correlates with the rate and selectivity of ammonia (NH3) formation. At moderate overpotentials, where nitrite formation dominates, lateral expansion of Cu terraces is observed, whereas rapid NH3 formation at higher cathodic potentials induces Cu adislands enriched in low-coordinated step sites, revealing distinct restructuring pathways that accompany the transition from nitrite- to ammonia-selective NO3RR. These transformations are rationalized by an NH3-mediated Cu dissolution-redeposition mechanism. Our results identify reaction products as active modulators of catalyst surface structure, establishing a framework for understanding reaction-driven catalyst restructuring and enabling in situ control of catalyst surfaces through the interfacial reaction environment.
n75456024163b: Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.
n84ab52e3992e: Lithium–air batteries suffer from moisture-induced parasitic reactions and electrolyte evaporation in ambient air. A fundamental challenge is the “micro-size inversion” paradox, where H2O (0.275 nm) is smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), rendering conventional size-based sieving ineffective. Here, we report a composite membrane composed of polydimethylsiloxane and fluorinated vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-VF) to break this selectivity barrier. By grafting 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorodecyl groups onto a vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-V), we establish a surface-chemistry-driven sieving mechanism. This design creates a molecular-level hydrogen-bond-repellent barrier that specifically inhibits polar H2O penetration while maintaining high nonpolar O2 flux, effectively decoupling the permeability-hydrophobicity trade-off. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate this mechanism, demonstrating that the COF-VF exhibits significantly reduced adsorption affinity toward H2O compared to the pristine COF-V. In 40% RH ambient air, the battery equipped with this membrane delivers a discharge capacity of 3596 mAh g–1 and sustains cycling for 2700 h (270 cycles), a 10.8-fold improvement over unprotected cells. Advanced characterizations via DRT and DEMS confirm that the membrane promotes reversible Li2O2 formation and significantly suppresses LiOH accumulation. This work provides a multiscale strategy for molecular-level selective separation in practical energy storage.
ne417d4918359: Charge carrier dynamics in wurtzite CdS quantum dots (QDs) form the basis for applications in optoelectronics and photocatalysis. We demonstrate that the quantum dynamics, energy gaps, and energy level alignments at CdS QD interfaces can be controlled by the polarity of the CdS QD surface. By performing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations within a density-functional tight-binding framework, we demonstrate a strong dependence of photoinitiated processes in CdS QDs/graphene nanoribbon (GNR) hybrids on interface polarity. At room temperature, hole transfer is accelerated by a factor of 2 and exciton lifetime is enhanced by nearly an order of magnitude when the CdS QD surface is switched from polar to nonpolar. Remarkably, the interfacial bandgap for the polar QD/GNR hybrid is reduced to half upon heating from 0 K to room temperature, while it remains nearly unchanged for the nonpolar hybrid. At an intermediate temperature, the ultrafast charge separation is maintained; however, charge recombination shows the opposite trend relative to room temperature. The polar interface exhibits a longer lifetime than the nonpolar interface, due to weakened electron–phonon Fröhlich interaction and decreased gap renormalization. The strong and highly nonlinear dependence of bandgap renormalization and carrier dynamics on temperature in the polar QD/GNR hybrid is associated with significant structural reconstruction, which is absent in the nonpolar counterpart. The demonstrated control of excited-state processes by interface polarity and the strong dependence of the dynamics and energy level alignment on temperature provide key fundamental insights for informed design of modern materials for optoelectronics and energy conversion.
n6e5b795a5d5d: Although catalysis is widely exploited by nature to orchestrate noncovalent supramolecular assembly and build up complex living systems, its utilization in synthetic chemistry has conventionally been limited to accelerating covalent reactions. Consequently, the development of artificial systems for catalytic assembly remains a formidable and largely unexplored challenge. Here, we present a rationally designed strategy of electron-catalyzed supramolecular assembly, wherein the electron acts as an efficient, robust, and versatile catalyst to accelerate the formation of a donor–acceptor complex. Optimization of the elementary steps and intermediate stability yields an efficient catalytic cycle, furnishing the process with both a high turnover number and operational robustness in open air. Furthermore, the electron catalysis can be readily triggered by diverse external stimuli─including electricity, light, and mechanical force─enabling precise spatiotemporal control over the assembly process and near-quantitative synthesis of supramolecular complexes. Collectively, this work establishes a well-elucidated strategy of catalytic assembly with remarkable practicality, advancing the frontiers of noncovalent synthetic chemistry.
nfd1eb7fc9ddf: The development of practical synthetic methods for incorporating trifluoromethyl (CF3) groups into organic scaffolds is of paramount importance in medicinal chemistry, as such modifications profoundly modulate the physicochemical properties of drug candidates. 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) is widely utilized as a unique solvent in synthetic chemistry and also represents a promising CF3 source due to its high availability and low cost. Here we report an unprecedented photoelectrochemical iron-catalyzed protocol for radical trifluoromethylation that employs commercially accessible HFIP as the CF3 radical precursor. This method enables efficient trifluoromethylation of unactivated arenes, heteroarenes, and alkenes with a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, this photoelectrocatalytic system is readily scalable for practical synthetic applications, and its utility has been demonstrated in the trifluoromethylation of peptides, allowing preferential modification of tryptophan residues in a chemoselective fashion.
n2136194cebe4: Engineering single-atom catalysts has predominantly focused on tailoring the primary coordination sphere, whereas whether distinct coordination spheres can be endowed with independent catalytic functions remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the functional specialization of coordination spheres by constructing a phosphorus-modified Ni–N2O2 single-atom catalyst for site-selective C–H deuteration. Advanced spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations show that phosphorus is incorporated outside the preserved primary Ni–N2O2 coordination environment and support an O-linked phosphorus environment as a preferential second-sphere motif. This architecture decouples substrate recognition from catalytic activation. Specifically, second-sphere phosphorus selectively recognizes and anchors the amino group of haloanilines to dictate deuteration site selectivity, whereas the preserved primary Ni–N2O2 coordination sphere promotes H2 activation and undergoes H2-assisted regeneration following D2O-induced hydroxylation, facilitated by P–O–Ni electronic communication, thereby sustaining efficient catalytic turnover. Consequently, the catalyst achieves highly site-selective C–H deuteration of chloro-, bromo-, and iodoanilines using H2 and D2O while completely preserving carbon–halogen bonds, whereas the phosphorus-free analogue exhibits negligible activity. This work identifies the structural origin and catalytic function of second-sphere phosphorus and establishes functional specialization of coordination spheres as a general design principle for independently programming substrate recognition and catalytic turnover in single-atom catalysis.
ndf282a0086ff: Despite the widespread utility of N-substituted 1,3-diamines across numerous fields, their selective synthesis directly from readily available feedstocks remains a long-standing challenge. In this context, we report a room-temperature electrochemical protocol for the synthesis of both symmetrical and unsymmetrical N,N′-disubstituted 1,3-diamines through electrochemical transformation of azoarenes with enoates, followed by convergent reduction of the resulting β-amino amides. This method features broad substrate scope, operational simplicity, no need for noble transition-metal catalysts, and high chemoselectivity. Mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction is initiated by the reduction of azoarenes, facilitated by HCOOH, while Zn2+ ions leached from anodic oxidation serve as a Lewis acid to promote intramolecular cyclization via ester amidation. Subsequent cathodic reduction drives N–N bond cleavage to afford the β-amino amide intermediates, thereby endowing azoarenes with dual-nitrogen synthon capability. This work provides a practical platform for the general synthesis of N,N′-difunctionalized 1,3-diamines and convenient late-stage structural editing of biomedicals.
n29cb20f28308: The application of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) in wide-temperature and fast-charging scenarios is severely constrained by the performance limitations of electrolytes. Conventional ester-based electrolytes struggle to simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity, low desolvation energy, and excellent interfacial stability. Herein, we propose a hybrid solvent system comprising ethyl propionate and ethoxy(pentafluoro)cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN), aiming to synergistically enhance the rate capability and temperature adaptability of SIBs. The relatively weak coordination ability of both solvents effectively promotes anion participation in solvation structure, significantly lowering the Na+ desolvation energy barrier and inducing the formation of stable, inorganic-rich electrode/electrolyte interphases. Meanwhile, the dual-solvent combination increases the diversity of solvation configurations and reduces ion clustering, thereby enhancing ionic conductivity. The intrinsic nonflammability and excellent film-forming ability of PFPN further enhance safety and synergistically strengthen interfacial stability. Therefore, Prussian blue||hard carbon full cells operate stably over a wide temperature range from −50 to 100 °C. Notably, ampere-hour-level pouch cells deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 300 cycles at 25 °C and maintain stable operation for over 100 cycles even at −20 and 80 °C. This solvent synergy strategy offers a practical new pathway for the development of electrolytes for SIBs in extreme environments.
nb42e3e53c572: Terawatt-scale deployment of proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires low iridium (Ir) loading, which disrupts the catalyst layer’s in-plane electronic percolation network and severely degrades performance. Here, we overcome this bottleneck via an interfacial confinement strategy that electrostatically enriches cationic Ir intermediates on the negatively charged, oxygen-deficient TiOx surface, thereby redirecting Ir deposition from three-dimensional island growth to a two-dimensional conformal film on TiO2 supports. The resulting IrOx-NF@TiO2 catalyst with low Ir packing density maintains long-range in-plane electron percolation, reducing reliance on the high Ir loading typically required by conventional IrOx nanoparticle catalysts to establish quasi-continuous conductive pathways. At a loading of 0.166 mgIr cm−2, blade-coated membrane electrode assemblies incorporating this architecture feature ∼7 μm-thick catalyst layers with an Ir packing density of only ∼0.25 gIr cm–3, allowing an ∼84% reduction in Ir use while achieving performance comparable to that of commercial IrO2. This work highlights the potential of supported conformal IrOx catalysts as competitive candidates for next-generation low-Ir PEMWEs.
ndd67cd4bcac9: The widespread contamination of water by emerging contaminants (ECs) demands the development of efficient remediation technologies. Although advanced oxidation processes reliant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) show promise, they typically depend on energy- or reagent-intensive activation methods. Here, we introduce a linker steric hindrance-induced defect engineering (LSH-DE) strategy for metal–organic frameworks, which enables catalytic ROS generation using molecular oxygen (O2) as a benign terminal oxidant at ambient temperature and pressure. By systematically modulating the steric bulk of organic linkers, we precisely create missing-linker defects and direct the formation of oxygen vacancy (Vo) in robust Ce-UiO-66 during a rapid 15 min synthesis. Spectroscopic and computational analyses confirm that these oxygen vacancies promote O2 adsorption and activation to yield superoxide radicals (•O2–). The optimized catalyst, Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2, demonstrates superior activity in degrading ubiquitous ECs without requiring external energy inputs or chemical mediators. Furthermore, integration of Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2 into a membrane-based recirculating flow-through system enabled sustained water treatment, maintaining >90% BPA removal over 48 h with a high water permeance of 101.5 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. This work presents a general and sustainable approach for designing catalytic defects in MOFs, advancing the development of green, next-generation water purification technologies.
nb0ecb4981d0e: Mesoporous structures with highly permeable channels are of great significance for fast diffusion; however, the delicate engineering of straightforward pores remains quite limited, with most of mesostructures are tortuous pores derived from spherical micelle assembly. Herein, we explore a novel lamellar–micelle assembly approach that enables to generate a type of wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres with highly interconnected divergent mesopores. In place of the conventional spherical micelles, the key for controlling such unusual assembly is determined by the construction of laminar micelles (copolymer L121/F127 composite) and heterogeneous growth on sedimented F127 seeds at a low temperature of 5 °C. The fabricated wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres after template removal possess a particle size at ∼910 nm, a high surface area of 315 m2 g–1, a uniform pore size at 36 nm, as well as radial mesochannels with high interconnectivity up to 96%. Further regulation on the reaction temperature and template ratio allows for a high tunability over the pore size and wrinkle degree. When employed as a sodium storage anode, the radially aligned large-pore structure drastically facilitates charge transport and electrolyte penetration, thus delivering rate capability (142 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1) and long-term cyclability (90.5% retention after 1000 cycles at 2 A g–1) compared to commercial hard carbon. Our work underscores a particular assembly pathway through lamellar micelles as an effective approach for building up ultrafast mesopore highways toward promising diffusion-related applications.
nc7da435e4abb: Biomarker-specific molecular imaging is vital in precision medicine. However, a fundamental challenge of most molecular imaging methods is the difficulty of distinguishing specific molecular signal from nonspecific signal arising from the distribution of the molecular probe. This is even more pronounced in metabolically active organs such as the kidney and liver where the probe may concentrate prior to elimination. As a result, almost all molecular imaging relies on delayed imaging to achieve specificity, but this constrains clinical throughput and impedes rapid assessment of the diseased organ. Here, we report a magnetic resonance (MR) probe, Fe(II)-IAFP2, which combines 3 drivers of relaxivity enhancement to decouple disease specificity from probe distribution. Fe(II)-IAFP2 is MR-silent in its Fe(II) state, producing negligible MR signal even at high concentrations. In inflammatory, fibrogenic microenvironments common to many diseases, rapid oxidation to Fe(III) activates MR enhancement, while reversible aldehyde-mediated binding to remodeled extracellular matrix further amplifies relaxivity and promotes retention at the site of tissue injury. This dual activation–retention mechanism enables robust signal generation within minutes of administration. In mouse models of renal and liver fibrogenesis, Fe(II)-IAFP2 generated disease-associated MR contrast within minutes after intravenous administration. Together, this work demonstrates an effective strategy for rapid, activity-based molecular MR imaging through the combination of pathological activation and complementary tissue retention.
nf038e2616e95: Order–disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. We applied time-resolved serial oscillation crystallography to establish the structural kinetics of the light-triggered order–disorder transition of an animal-like cryptochrome as a six-second-long molecular movie with near-atomic all-residue spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Our 29 structural snapshots mapped the propagation of disorder across the tertiary structure motifs of a cryptochrome’s C-terminal region, triggered by a single broken D321–R492 salt bridge. The order–disorder transition followed a nucleation-propagation mechanism reminiscent of helix–coil dynamics and proceeded over up to five seconds, with regions distal to the D321–R492 trigger initially undergoing slow zero-order disordering before switching to first-order unfolding kinetics. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order–disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.
nb097597fc148: Mechanophores provide an in situ and remote tool for quantifying invisible stress in polymers by photonic signals, offering distinct advantages for stress distribution analysis of large-area surfaces and instrument-free stress observation. However, achieving an ideal mechanophore that integrates with sensitive, reversible, and molecular-level stress sensing is attractive yet challenging.
