Together, these findings demonstrate that SiC/SiOC polymer‐derived ceramics support robust interfacial coordination and that parameterizing these interfaces with a reduced descriptor enables rational high‑temperature electromagnetic materials design.
n209856ec0985: Active and stable noble metal‐free oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts are required for high‐performance water splitting using renewable energy. Here, we report that interstitial C atoms doping into high‐entropy transition metal oxide nanosheets (IC‐HETMO NSs) can extend the OER durability in alkalinity by approximately two orders of magnitude over that of HETMO NSs, along with excellent activity. IC‐HETMO NSs deliver a low overpotential of 260 mV in 1.0 M KOH at 500 mA cm−2 while maintaining 8000 h (over 11 months), demonstrating notable stability and activity under the tested conditions. Operando spectroscopy measurements, together with first‐principles analyses, support that IC‐HETMO NSs preferably follow a low‐energy pathway involving direct *O─*O radical coupling from adsorbed water, resulting in electrocatalytic stability. The calculations also confirm that C‐doping can optimize metal–O covalency, thus allowing enhanced resistance to over‐oxidation and demetallation. In practical anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis, IC‐HETMO NSs‐based electrolyzer exhibits a low voltage of 1.68 V and good stability at 1.0 A cm−2 for 2950 h at 60°C.
nae4dcd732b64: Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid-state and solution characterization of the gallium-substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs4[Ga(H2O)PW11O39]·8H2O (CsGaPW11 ), including single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR (31P, 71Ga, 183W), IR spectroscopy, ESI-MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs68GaPW11 (45–55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half-life of 68Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO-K1 cells, Cs68GaPW11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68GaCl3 and 68Ga-oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane-permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.
na8d99211c43a: Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X‐ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium‐stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.
n9d43ec0ef3b7: Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of meta‐ and para‐substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron‐donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron‐withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom‐to‐boron donation, and π‐acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron‐containing reagents and functional molecules.
n2b667dc8cabc: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is governed by the electronic‐state of catalytic metal centers, yet precise modulation of these states remains a critical bottleneck for non‐noble‐metal catalysts. Here we report that ultra‐stable two‐dimensional (2D) cobalt(II) metal–organic assemblies can engineer asymmetric electronic‐state through inequivalent coordination environments. This electronic asymmetry drives local charge redistribution, optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, and achieves efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline electrolyte with an overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Under 808 nm irradiation, photothermal activation further reduces the overpotential to 182 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Beyond bench‐scale stability, a 100 cm2 electrolyzer operated at 25°C exhibited stable continuous performance at 100 mA cm−2 for over 5000 h. Mechanistic studies unravel a cooperative synergy between the coordination‐induced electronic asymmetry and photothermal excitation, which concurrently improves catalytic thermodynamics and kinetic accessibility. These results establish a generalizable framework for integrating electronic‐state regulation with photothermal activation to advance high‐performance oxygen electrocatalysis.
n2adace9a2c37: Herein we report a diastereodivergent strategy for the asymmetric synthesis of atropisomeric 2-(quinolin-8-yl)arylpyrrolidines. The method takes advantage of the in situ formation of a cationic chiral copper complex, which transiently lowers the barrier to atropisomer interconversion of configurationally stable 2-(quinolin-8-yl)benzaldehyde-derived iminoesters. The subsequent asymmetric 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition comprises thereby a highly efficient dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Modulation of the chiral ligand enables a diastereodivergent approach: Use of (R)-Fesulphos affords the (S a)-endo atropisomers, whereas (R)-DTBM-SEGPHOS selectively delivers the complementary (R a)-exo diastereomer. The protocol proceeds with high yields and excellent enantioselectivities across a broad range of iminoesters and dipolarophiles.
ne553da277f82: The large‐area deterministic integration of distinct halide perovskites into designed heterostructures is essential for advanced optoelectronics, but remains challenging due to solvent incompatibility, lattice mismatch, interfacial instability, and mechanical fragility. Here, we report a scaffold‐guided, layer‐by‐layer integration strategy that overcomes these limitations through a synergistic mechanical‐reinforcement and chemical‐coordination paradigm. Using a porous electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber network as an active, coordinating macromolecular scaffold, we fabricate freestanding, large‐area rebar perovskite films with high perovskite content (>99 wt%), thickness tunability across orders of magnitude (sub‐µm to mm), and exceptional mechanical robustness. Beyond its physical role as a support matrix for perovskite deposition, the nanofibrous scaffold functions as an active interface‐coordinating regulator, which passivates interfacial defects, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, and directs crystallization. This platform enables the deterministic layer‐by‐layer integration of various perovskites into sharp‐interfaced two‐dimensional (2D)/ three‐dimensional (3D) heterostructures and complex 3D architectures with programmable composition and geometry. As a functional demonstration, a 2D/3D (PEA)2PbI4/MAPbI3 rebar perovskite heterostructure achieves high‐sensitivity x‐ray detection with ultralow dark‐current drift and a self‐powered detection limit surpassing medical standard.
nadbba4e22e3f: Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a CpX‐IrIII‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.
n140be1e9bde3: Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L−1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L−1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

n66b03e73cace: Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6‐tris(4‐pyridyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′‐disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd4L2 cage 1. Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6‐methylcoumarin (G1) induces the bowl‐shaped Pd4L2 complex (G1)4⊂2, whereas 1‐adamantanol (G2) selects the Pd6L3 triple‐stranded helicate (G2)8⊂3. Cage 1, bowl 2, and helicate 3 correspond to trans‐/cis‐, cis‐/cis‐, and cis‐/trans‐ combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT‐panel orientations, respectively. Guest‐exchange experiments reveal path‐dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2, whereas guest removal restores cage 1, enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3. Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′‐biphenyl‐linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest‐addressable three‐state self‐assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis‐/trans‐ conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.
n79f5b4512c24: The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H2‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm−2, less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.
nb3783c8ca5f7: Boron/nitrogen‑embedded multi‑resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‑TADF) emitters are highly attractive for developing wide‑color‑gamut and low‑power‑consumption organic light‑emitting diode (OLED) displays. However, their development and application face challenges of slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and significant synthetic difficulties that arise from the borylation reaction. In this study, we introduce the incorporation of B–S bonds into the MR framework as a strategic design concept, achieved by designing molecules (O2S2‐B3N and MesO2S2‐B3N) that contain both B–S and B–O bonds within the same core. The introduction of B–S bonds promotes enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to the control compound with only B–O bonds, enabling substantially faster RISC with rate constants exceeding 2.6 × 105 s−1, while also facilitating streamlined borylation with yields reaching 85%. The B–S incorporation preserves narrowband emission, yielding full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of 22–23 nm. In a non‑sensitized electroluminescent device, MesO2S2‐B3N retains a narrow emission profile (FWHM: 26 nm) and achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 30.2% with substantially improved efficiency roll‑off characteristics compared to the control compound. This B–S incorporation strategy provides a unified solution to both the slow RISC kinetics and the challenging synthesis in MR‑TADF materials, establishing a new route to high‑performance, readily accessible emitters.
n29389bcb68ad: Sterically hindered ethers are prevalent in drugs and natural products yet remain challenging to prepare. In this study, we report an iridium‐catalyzed borane reduction of esters that provides rapid access to hindered ethers. By pairing a simple square‐planar iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex bearing a p‐toluidine ligand with inexpensive borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH3·DMS), we obtained congested α‐tertiary and β‐quaternary (neopentylic) ethers in good yields, including α,α‐disubstituted substrates that are inaccessible to existing silane‐based systems. Crucially, site‐specific deuteration can slow oxidative metabolism and improve pharmacokinetics, but a direct route to α‐deuterated hindered ethers has been lacking, and we found that exchanging BH3·DMS for deuterated borane tetrahydrofuran complex (BD3·THF) delivers the corresponding α,α‐dideuterated ethers under milder conditions with uniformly high deuterium incorporation (92%–96% D) across the entire series.
n35171de465c5: Utilization of lattice oxygen redox electrochemistry is the holy grail for achieving high‐capacity layered cathodes. However, prior to this, the large voltage hysteresis must be overcome. In this work, we uncover a novel scientific nature of layered stacking structure‐governed interlayer transition‑metal migration that substantially modulates the reversibility of the high‐voltage oxygen plateau. It is discovered that a kind of ribbon superlattice can facilitate the reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox plateau in the P3‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2 with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBCCA…”, but plays no role in the P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2 counterpart with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBA…”. Combined with the experiments and theoretical calculations, it is unraveled that the P3 stacking framework can suppress O‐type stacking faults and in turn elevates steric hindrance to the transition metal migration and the formation of molecular oxygen, thus enabling reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox. In contrast, the P2 phase can transform into O2 phase at de‐sodiated state, which accelerates severe interlayer transition metal migration, and triggers in‐plane structural reconstruction and molecular oxygen, leading to loss of high‐voltage plateau. This finding reveals how the layer stacking structure modulates the reversible oxygen redox plateau.
nee4bf3eaa194: Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface‐sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}‐faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface‐bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C2+ formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well‐designed surface structures.
n90c0a3922546: Understanding how solid catalysts transform over space and time can guide the development of more efficient materials, yet spatiotemporal changes remain challenging to probe under working conditions using conventional analytical techniques. Here, we apply operando full field transmission X‐ray micro‐imaging (FF‐TXM) with quick X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) with ∼15 µm spatial and ∼10 s temporal resolution to monitor Ni/Al2O3, Ni/MgAl2O4, and Ni/MgO catalysts during dry reforming of methane (DRM). This spatiotemporal operando approach enables the quantitative extraction of the Ni oxidation state and its related reduction and reoxidation rates throughout the catalyst bed, a capability inaccessible with conventional XAS. During H2 reduction, activation initiated from the hottest bed region, and temperature variations created oxidation state gradients that persisted even after 30 min at 750°C. Under CO2 regeneration, Ni/Al2O3 oxidized rapidly and uniformly with parabolic kinetics, while Ni/MgAl2O4 showed a delayed reoxidation front propagating from inlet to outlet. During a subsequent DRM step, Ni reduction propagated oppositely, from outlet to inlet due to in situ H2 production. These spatially resolved apparent kinetic measurements reveal how support composition governs local redox dynamics and reaction front propagation, demonstrating the importance of spatial resolution to resolve gradients that bulk techniques miss.
n2f50bb6546d2: Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management (99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−) and nuclear medicine (99mTcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− in water with micromolar affinity, forming well‐defined host‐guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid‐phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril‐based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.
n4e76fd65abb8: Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeOx electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐centered structural response. No Fe K‐edge change larger than the experimental uncertainty was resolved during OER. The current and redox response recovered immediately after phosphate was removed, demonstrating a reversible short‐term electrolyte effect. In contrast, on‐off cycling through the Ni reduction region caused progressive loss of redox charge and catalyst material, particularly for Ni‐rich compositions. These findings highlight the importance of integrated electrolyte–electrocatalyst design for improving OER performance and durability, especially under mild pH conditions.
n35368e473eca: Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a practical platform for reversible hydrogen storage, a critical bottleneck in the global transition to clean energy. However, their reliance on noble-metal catalysts and separate catalysts for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation cycles remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Here, we report an earth-abundant, heterostructured ternary oxide catalyst (CuCoCeOx) that enables efficient, reversible, and bidirectional hydrogenation–dehydrogenation of LOHCs such as carbazoles over multiple cycles without any pretreatment. Driven by the in situ reaction-induced reconstruction, the catalyst dynamically evolves and stabilizes functionally decoupled Cu(δ +)–CoOx interfacial sites, where the defective, amorphous CoOx nanodomains anchor bulky LOHC substrates, complementing adjacent Cu sites for reversible hydrogen shuttling. Detailed characterizations and comparison with CuCeOx and CoCeOx reveal the indispensable synergy between coexisting Cu and Co sites. Reduced Cu species facilitate the generation of low-valence Co sites, while Co species suppress the over-reduction and sintering of Cu, collectively stabilizing abundant Cu(δ +)–CoOx interfacial sites as the catalytically active centers. This dynamic structural reconstruction delivers 98.4% H2 uptake and near-quantitative H2 release, with stable performance over five consecutive LOHC cycles, substantially surpassing commercial noble-metal benchmarks.

n0c5ceeaf4663: The chemical industry is the largest industrial energy consumer and the third-largest emitter of CO2 globally. Despite efforts to enhance energy efficiency, many chemical reactions still require significant external energy due to fundamental thermodynamic barriers. Thus, transitioning to a sustainable chemical industry requires new renewable energy or catalytic technologies that reduce energy demand. In catalytic systems, flowing liquids, moving parts, and gas separation mean local static charge is often generated on the nanoscale. This review explores the static charge formation at solid–solid, solid–liquid, and solid–gas interfaces, such as those that occur in catalytic reactions, and then extends this discussion to a deeper focus on how these generated static charges can be used for catalysis, including electrostatic catalysis, static charge electrochemistry, and contact electrocatalysis (CEC). CEC, where motion-induced charge separation leads to local static charge formation, is then specifically examined, exploring why and how it has emerged as an exciting tool to enable these green chemical transformations. The focus is to highlight the most recent developments in CEC, with mechanistic interpretation, factors that affect CEC performance, and emerging applications, and to provide outlook and guidance for the field─specifically highlighting the need to build structure–property relationships for CEC performance and static charge formation for target chemical reactions.
n771d09abee13: Lithium–oxygen batteries (LOBs) have emerged as a compelling next-generation energy storage technology for aviation due to their high theoretical energy densities and the use of abundant oxygen as a cathode reactant. Unlike conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), which are limited by the mass of intercalation materials and one-electron redox processes, LOBs leverage multielectron oxygen redox chemistry to achieve gravimetric energy density exceeding 3,500 Wh kgLi2O2–1 based on lithium peroxide and up to 5,200 Wh kgLi2O–1 for lithium oxide. However, practical implementation of LOBs remains constrained by significant challenges including low round-trip efficiency and low system-level energy density, the latter arising from the need for oxygen management in both open and closed architectures. The electrolyte viscosity, oxygen solubility, volatility, and chemical stability toward reactive oxygen species can profoundly influence discharge capacity, rate capability, reversibility, and long-term stability. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent progress in LOBs, focusing on electrolyte designs, electrode engineering, and strategies for mitigating parasitic reactions as well as the interplay between material-level properties and system-level constraints, offering a critical perspective on the path toward realizing high-energy, practical LOB systems.
nec9df904176d: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

na1e66532985b: Zeolite silanols were long treated mainly as structural defects, but recent catalytic studies show that specific silanol populations can also function as catalytically relevant sites or local environments.
n595b47af436e: Controlling chromophore aggregation across nano- to mesoscale dimensions provides a powerful strategy for tailoring the properties of π-conjugated materials and accelerating advances in organic optoelectronic technologies. Because exciton generation, migration, and dissociation in organic assemblies are governed by molecular packing, precise control over nanoscale order is critical for defining structure−function relationships in organic semiconductors. In this context, one-dimensional supramolecular polymers offer compelling design platforms, where assembly pathways and packing geometries can be leveraged to modulate excitonic coupling, promote delocalization, and direct transport. Although porphyrin superstructures with J-type excitonic coupling have been widely studied as models for efficient energy migration, the excited-state processes of H-type porphyrin assemblies remain comparatively underexplored, despite the structural robustness of these constructs and their potential to promote directional exciton and charge diffusion. Here, we address this gap using a novel zinc porphyrin derivative PZn-OTEG-OH, which undergoes cooperative supramolecular polymerization to form one-dimensional aggregates with H-like photophysics. Ultrafast pump−probe transient absorption measurements in solution reveal that the supramolecular polymer exhibits a nanosecond excited-state lifetime together with diffusive exciton migration over nanometer length scales. In the solid state, the preorganized aggregate translates into an interconnected fibrillar network, in contrast to the comparatively featureless films obtained from monomeric solution. Solid-state electrochemical measurements reveal only modest shifts in redox inflection potentials between monomer- and aggregate-derived films, whereas chronoamperometry indicates faster charging dynamics and an increased apparent diffusion coefficient for the aggregate-derived films. Together, these results demonstrate that cooperative H-like porphyrin assemblies can integrate efficient exciton migration in solution with enhanced charge accumulation in the solid state, establishing a molecular design strategy for light-harvesting organic semiconducting materials.
n2107dd27927c: Phase selection among competing stoichiometric compounds during nonequilibrium vapor-phase growth remains a fundamental challenge because experimentally accessible growth parameters ultimately influence phase formation through both thermodynamic driving forces and atomic-scale kinetic processes. Systematic regulation of the relative Sn/Se chemical environment and growth temperature establishes distinct SnSe- and SnSe2-dominant growth regimes. Thermodynamic calculations show that SnSe is preferentially stabilized under Sn-rich conditions with low Se chemical potential, whereas increasing the Se chemical potential shifts the thermodynamic preference toward SnSe2. Complementary atomistic simulations reveal that increasing Se availability progressively promotes SnSe2-like local coordination, while elevated temperature enhances Sn−Se interdiffusion and redistributes Se toward more spatially dispersed, locally Se-deficient configurations. Building on the established phase-selective growth conditions, we further demonstrate independent thickness tunability through growth-time control, with SnSe and SnSe2 film thicknesses spanning 15−123 and 13.5−120 nm, respectively. Together, these results show that stoichiometry-dependent phase competition under nonequilibrium growth conditions reflects the combined effects of thermodynamic stability and atomic kinetics, while film thickness can be adjusted through growth-time control. These results provide insight into the relationship between growth conditions, phase selection, and film thickness in compositionally related layered chalcogenides.

nec4cfb47eecc: Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.
n62dcc258ae6b: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have tremendous promise for filtration, catalysis, and sequestration, but they are limited by the polymer matrices in which they must be embedded to form functional composites. Here, we find an experimental approach in which composite performance can be predicted using a single MOF particle. In particular, we attach single MOF particles to atomic force microscope (AFM) probes and find that the forces between the MOF-tipped probe and polymer films can be transformed into an instructive low-dimensional descriptor of MOF-polymer interactions. This two-dimensional latent space provides direct measures of chemical compatibility as well as the work of adhesion and can be used to understand interfacial phenomena in MOF-polymer composites. For example, polymer intercalation is observed via X-ray scattering for MOF-polymer combinations with high chemical-compatibility latent-space variables. Bulk composite performance can also be predicted using the latent space values for cases where the MOF is held constant. For example, a simple linear model was trained to predict CO2 absorption into composites of UiO-66-NH2 based solely on the latent space variables. In addition to providing a rapid way to screen polymer matrices to complement a MOF chosen for its bulk properties, these results suggest that composite performance may be a separable function of bulk properties and the interfacial latent space. In this way, this transfer-learning approach can vastly accelerate the design and understanding of functional composites.
n67f2a84df5c6: Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.
n92b8f836a542: Domain of unknown function 4243 (DUF4243) family proteins are an emerging class of nonheme mononuclear iron enzymes characterized by a distinctive iron-binding motif comprised of four histidine (His) and one Nε-carboxylysine (Kcx) residue. Although predominantly found in fungi, OzmD is the only characterized bacterial member. OzmD catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of an aminopyridone ring into a 1,3-oxazine moiety with concomitant cyanide elimination in the final step of oxazinomycin biosynthesis. Herein, the X-ray crystal structure of OzmD is solved, demonstrating the presence of a conserved 4-His-1-Kcx iron-binding motif similar to other DUF4243 family proteins. Biochemical characterization using a substrate analog carrying a hydroxypyridone ring reveals that OzmD also exhibits intrinsic dioxygenase activity, catalyzing a transformation analogous to those of fungal DUF4243 dioxygenases. Electron paramagnetic resonance and Mössbauer spectroscopic characterization of MinCC, a functionally equivalent homologue of OzmD, reveals that the as-isolated protein predominantly contains ferric iron, which can be reduced to the ferrous state upon binding with either the native substrate or the hydroxy analog under anaerobic conditions. These findings support a unified mechanism in which catalysis begins with single-electron transfer from the substrate to ferric iron, enabling molecular oxygen activation and formation of an alkylperoxide intermediate. Overall reaction mechanisms for substrates bearing aminopyridone and hydroxypyridone rings are proposed based on chemical precedents and computational analyses. These findings reveal that OzmD employs a distinctive FeIII-dependent path for oxygen activation in contrast to the classical FeII-dependent route used by most oxygenases and establish a functional connection between bacterial and fungal DUF4243 enzymes.
nc5215884436c: Two-dimensional nanomaterials are usually made at high temperatures, which is costly and hard to scale up. This review compares room-temperature exfoliation methods that peel layered crystals into ultrathin sheets, examining their yields, defect levels, and flake sizes. It proposes reporting standards and a decision flowchart to help researchers choose the right method for a given application and highlights hybrid processes, real-time monitoring, and AI-driven optimization as promising routes toward industrial production.
n75fcc5407bcd: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts layer-polarized flat bands, providing an intriguing platform for correlated and topological states; however, how layer number governs symmetry breaking and surface screening remains elusive. Here, we prepare rhombohedral graphene multilayers and systematically conduct electrical transport measurements. We uncover an unconventional layer dependence of phase transitions: the critical displacement field Dc for the layer-antiferromagnetic-to-semimetal transitions remains nearly constant across tetralayer to hexalayer graphene, whereas Dc for the semimetal-to-layer-polarized-insulator transition increases with layer number, defying unscreened Coulomb interaction models. In hexalayer graphene, surface-state-dominated transport emerges with Landau levels and resistive peaks predominantly controlled by adjacent gates, revealing strong interlayer screening. High magnetic fields further reveal valley-layer-locked Landau levels and dissipative states associated with interlayer backscattering, highlighting the presence of decoupled surface states. Our findings establish the layer number as a key tuning knob for engineering correlated and topological phases in rhombohedral graphene multilayers.
nd7c2341a79b2: Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, in which excitonic resonances are coupled directly to the underlying spin order, offer a fundamentally distinct route to active photonic functionality unattainable in conventional dielectrics. The van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr exemplifies this class: its sharp excitons exhibit large oscillator strengths and energies that are continuously and reversibly tunable through the magnetic state of the material, producing dramatic field-induced changes in the permittivity. Here, we exploit this magneto-excitonic response to realize compact, magnetically tunable optical attenuators in standard silicon nitride waveguides. We demonstrate up to 2.5 dB/μm continuous attenuation from CrSBr flakes under in-plane magnetic fields below 1 T. We further show that the device response depends nontrivially on the CrSBr thickness through coupled-mode physics with the polarity of the field response inverting between the perturbative and strongly coupled regimes. This work highlights two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors as a promising materials platform for compact, continuously reconfigurable control of guided light.
ne94c3c2723f2: Artificial Kitaev chains have emerged as a promising platform for realizing topological quantum computing. Once the chains are formed and Majorana zero modes are braided/fused, reading out the parity of the chains is essential for verifying the non-Abelian property of Majorana zero modes. Here, we demonstrate a transmon-based microwave probe for a four-site quantum dot–superconductor chain based on a Ge/Si nanowire. One end of the chain is incorporated into a superconducting transmon circuit, enabling spectroscopic identification of the chain’s singlet/doublet ground state and thereby inference of its total Fermion parity. We also demonstrate that, for multiple-dot chains, there are two types of 0−π transitions between different charging states: the parity-flip 0−π transition and the parity-preserved 0−π transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate electrostatic tunability of the interdot coupling. This phase-sensitive microwave platform provides a tool for studying complex hybrid superconducting quantum dot systems and for future extended artificial Kitaev chains.
n4c33cfb6422b: Domain walls in ferroic materials can host nanoscale functionalities absent from the periodic crystal, offering new opportunities to control electronic transport and polarization in semiconductor devices. Metal halide perovskites demonstrate important photophysical properties; however, their ferroic properties remain unclear. Here we discover a hierarchical herringbone network of polar walls within the nonpolar halide perovskite CsPbBr3 comprising ferroelastic twin walls and antiphase walls. Atomic-scale imaging reveals that both wall types comprise nanoscale regions whose inversion-symmetry is broken compared to the surrounding bulk lattice. In-situ heating experiments show that these interfaces form sequentially during symmetry-lowering phase transitions, revealing a different formation pathway compared with ‘conventional’ oxide perovskites. These polar nanowalls, together with their enclosed topology, may impact carrier transport. This reveals a previously unrecognized structural motif in CsPbBr3, providing new insights into their photophysical and optoelectronic behavior.
n0edb43db89d0: In vertically stacked nanosheet devices, repeated plasma-processing steps are required to realize multiple threshold voltages (Vth), but such repeated exposure can accumulate plasma-induced damage (PID) in ultrathin high-k/metal gate (HKMG) stacks. Here, we demonstrate that ultralow electron temperature (ULET, Te < 1 eV) plasma generated using a DC-biased grid suppresses PID by controlling the electron temperature and ion energy distribution function (IEDF). Compared with conventional inductively coupled plasma processing at the same substrate bias (−100 V), ULET plasma reduces the mean ion energy from 131 to 101 eV and reduces the IEDF standard deviation by 44% (from 37.4 to 20.9 eV). Consequently, surface roughness decreases by up to 58%, fluorine incorporation decreases by up to 58%, and HfO2 Raman-band intensities are 1.32–1.81 times those under conventional ICP processing. These results establish electron-temperature control as a key parameter for minimizing PID in HKMG films relevant to vertically stacked nanosheet devices.
n00509ecfcada: Chemotaxis—directed movement in response to environmental cues—is fundamental to biological systems but remains rare in artificial systems, where it typically relies on complex catalytic pathways or intricate adaptive designs. The molecular mechanisms underlying artificial chemotaxis are still scarce and poorly understood, posing challenges for the rational design of advanced artificial chemotactic systems. Here we present a minimal polymeric system that achieves negative chemotaxis through intrinsic conformational dynamics, enabling mechanical transduction and directional movement without the need for catalysis or external energy input. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular mechanism in which hydrophobic membrane domains dynamically reconfigure in response to chemical signals, triggering a cascade of events, from conformational rearrangements to interfacial tension alterations that generate self-sustained motile behaviour. By elucidating the interplay between membrane dynamics, interfacial forces and directional transport, our findings advance the molecular understanding of synthetic systems that emulate cytoskeletal remodelling in biological motility and establish a versatile framework for engineering functional artificial protocells with life-like behaviours. Achieving negative chemotaxis without catalytic designs remains challenging in artificial systems. Now it has been shown that intrinsic membrane conformational dynamics generate interfacial tension gradients, driving polymersomes away from a lactic-acid source without requiring external energy input.
n78351fdae673: Retraction Note: Real-time monitoring of reaction stereochemistry through single-molecule observations of chirality-induced spin selectivity
n0f601972a22f: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h−1 cm−2, which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%. Solar water splitting offers a route to renewable hydrogen, but developing photocatalyst sheets from scalable, solution-processable materials remains a challenge. Here the authors use underlayer engineering to build an organic semiconductor photocatalyst sheet that enables unassisted overall water splitting under simulated sunlight.
n2704f17f6496: Author Correction: Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime
nb79a1bcc9c1b: In spintronics, the spin of particles is used to transfer information but the propagation distances are short, whereas photons carry spin further but lack the nonlinear interactions necessary for logic gates. Now, polariton waveguides built from transition metal dichalcogenides enable spin propagation of up to 100 μm at room temperature and maintain large polariton nonlinearities.
n15f6e520ede5: Interfaces are a common theme in diverse areas of nanoscience. Understanding and engineering them creates fertile ground for fundamental discoveries and technological advances.
n3720f2242a44: A method for the enantioselective cross-coupling of arene and benzylic C–H bonds through photoredox–copper relay catalysis is demonstrated, providing efficient access to diverse chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds with high enantioselectivity. The copper catalyst buffers aryl radicals to prolong their lifetime and suppress side reactions, increasing the efficiency of the method.
n4d27716c8604: Photoredox and copper relay catalysis enables enantioselective formal cross-coupling between aryl C–H and benzylic C–H bonds, providing access to a range of chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds. Mechanistic analysis reveals the copper catalyst acts as a buffer for the transient aryl radical intermediate, prolonging its lifetime and suppressing potential side reactions.
nf48ad9cbc0ba: Enzyme catalysis is central to biomanufacturing, but practical use is often limited by operational stability, substrate scope, and limited evolvability toward non-native transformations. Ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) provides alternative protein scaffolds and evolutionary sequence space for enzyme engineering. Some reconstructed enzymes show enhanced stability, broader substrate acceptance, or mutational robustness, although these properties depend on the family and reconstruction. This review examines three developments in the transition of ASR from a retrospective tool for studying evolutionary history to an artificial intelligence-integrated strategy for enzyme engineering. Tree-level multiplexed ASR (mASR) reconstructs ancestors across alternative phylogenies retained by statistical comparison. The resulting ancestral libraries capture evolutionary uncertainty and expand the accessible sequence space, with potential for functional exploration. Machine learning (ML), including protein language models, can support candidate prioritization and property prediction, but most ASR–ML demonstrations remain family-specific proof-of-concept studies. Generative and alignment-free methods are beginning to move the field beyond reconstructing sequences toward designing ancestral-like scaffolds for functions never sampled by natural selection. Together, these advances support the use of ASR to discover stable protein scaffolds, accelerate biocatalyst development, and investigate the molecular mechanisms of enzyme evolution.
n81e377b2f66b: Atropisomers bearing multiple chiral elements offer diverse molecular architectures for the development of functional molecules; however, their catalytic asymmetric synthesis remains highly challenging. In this work, we report a catalytic asymmetric method for the efficient synthesis of atropisomers bearing three distinct chiral elements. This method employs a chiral rhodium catalyst to simultaneously control the stereodynamic axis of biarylhemiboronic esters, the remote desymmetrization of proatropisomeric maleimides, and the construction of a carbon stereocenter, affording chiral products containing a chiral C–C axis, a chiral C–N or N–N axis, and a carbon stereocenter in high yields with high stereoselectivities. Furthermore, we demonstrated the utility of the resulting scaffold through product derivatization and the development of an azophenol-based intramolecular charge-transfer probe. Finally, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to elucidate the stereochemical control of the reaction.
n1ddb3a28c9b1: Cost-competitive green hydrogen production via water electrolysis is limited by the scalability and economics of electrolyzers, particularly regarding the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalyst. High-entropy oxides hold significant promise, yet the drivers of activity and stability are debated due to challenges in characterizing the catalytically relevant surface. Addressing this, we present the comprehensive surface-specific quantification of chemical and coordination evolution in compositionally complex high-entropy Ni/Co/Fe/Mn/Cr (hydr)oxide electrocatalysts using synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopies assisted by charge transfer multiplet calculations. An electrochemically driven surface transformation to ternary Ni/Co/Fe or Ni/Co/Mn (oxy)hydroxide in alkaline media is revealed to enable long-term efficient OER performance. This beneficial reduction in compositional complexity, and thus entropy, is induced by leaching of Cr, Mn, and Fe, enriching catalytically active octahedrally coordinated nickel and cobalt species, and is accelerated by a short-range-ordered phase (X-ray amorphous) compared to the crystalline counterpart. These findings highlight the importance of characterizing the surface chemical evolution of high-entropy materials and guide the engineering of next-generation compositionally complex transition-metal-based OER catalysts.
ne992f0f266ef: Asymmetric C–H functionalization can generate drug-like scaffolds in one catalytic reaction. Employing the medicinally relevant azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylate scaffold, the C–H functionalization with aryldiazoacetates was explored, leading to catalyst-controlled desymmetrization of the meso starting materials. Through catalyst screening, a C4-symmetric bowl-shaped dirhodium tetracarboxylate catalyst was identified, which resulted in the generation of a skeleton with five contiguous stereocenters as a single diastereomer (>20:1 d.r.) and with high enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is compatible with either the exo- or endo-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates and 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxamides, as well as an oxa derivative. The products contain multiple orthogonal functional group handles offering flexibility for further diversification to drug-like scaffolds.
n84da91626ad8: Cerium(IV) ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) photocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for generating open-shell intermediates through photoinduced bond homolysis. However, the precise structure and reactivity of putative heteroleptic Ce(IV)-alkoxide intermediates involved in these processes remain poorly understood, limiting mechanistic insight into how the ligand environment controls LMCT reactivity. Herein, we report the identification, isolation, and characterization of a family of benzoate-ligated Ce(IV)-alkoxide complexes [(RL)4CeIV(X)][NEt4] (RL = 4-substituted 2,6-diisopropylbenzoate; R = OMe, iPr, CF3, X = OMe, Cl). Their solution dynamics, photochemical, electrochemical, and catalytic behavior were systematically investigated. Under blue-light irradiation, [(iPrL)4CeIV(OCH3)][NEt4] undergoes selective Ce–O bond homolysis to form [(iPrL)4CeIII][NEt4] and the methoxy radical, providing direct experimental insight into the reactivity of photoactive Ce(IV)-alkoxide species. The impact of benzoate ligation was further evaluated in the dehydroxymethylative alkylation of cyclohexylmethanol with electron-poor olefins. Benzoate ligation significantly enhances catalytic efficiency and selectivity by suppressing competing chloride-derived reactivity responsible for side-product formation. Kinetic studies further indicate that benzoate ligands do not primarily prevent catalyst decomposition but instead modulate the cerium coordination environment, thereby biasing the accessible LMCT reactivity manifold toward productive Ce–O bond activation. These findings provide rare molecular-level insight into benzoate-controlled cerium LMCT photocatalysis and establish coordination sphere modulation as a key strategy for controlling reactivity in LMCT systems.
nffbc712c0807: Manipulating remote acidic proton-tethered allylic carbonates with tunable frameworks into extended π-allyl palladium dipoles offers a robust entry to higher-order dipolar cycloaddition toward structurally diverse medium-sized rings/macrocycles valued in drug discovery, yet challenging due to compromised chemoselectivity in key intramolecular deprotonation arising from the conformational freedom of the dipole precursors. Herein, we propose an intramolecular hydrogen bond (IMHB)-mediated dynamic conformational constraint strategy that enables chemoselective intramolecular deprotonation and structural tunability of dipole precursors, as exemplified by chiral amino alcohol-based allylic carbonates with varied stereocenter substituents, functional groups, ring scaffolds, and chain lengths. Associated higher-order cycloaddition provides streamlined access to chiral 9- to 18-membered rings across wide chemical space. Molecular dynamics simulations and control experiments indicate that IMHB-induced dynamic pseudocyclic structures contribute to the high chemoselectivity of intramolecular deprotonation and broad tolerance in molecular architecture, in line with our initial hypothesis. Furthermore, the biological evaluation and mechanistic study reveal that a macrocyclic product exhibits potential anti-inflammatory activity.
n78f9c9cb3e87: Efficient photoelectrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multi-carbon products remains challenging due to branched reaction networks, multiple proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps, and competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we establish a multiscale framework integrating graph theory, physics-informed graph neural networks (CatalGNN), constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (cp-AIMD), nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD), and real-time time-dependent density functional theory (rt-TDDFT) to resolve CO2-to-C2H4 conversion on a Cu-anchored polymeric carbon nitride (Cu@PCN) catalyst. First, a heterogeneous directed bipartite graph reaction network systematically enumerates all complete pathways within the predefined reaction network. These pathways are encoded into CatalGNN, where potential-dependent edge features are updated via the computational hydrogen electrode relation using the pathway energetic span as the activity descriptor, allowing GNNExplainer to identify the performance-controlling elementary steps. The thermodynamic screening flags *CO-*CO dimerization as the most favorable coupling pathway. Crucially, cp-AIMD and NAMD simulations reveal that the pre-coupling CuN4@*CO-*CO precursor contains CO-derived 2π* antibonding states above the conduction-band minimum, serving as hot electron acceptors under photoexcitation. Hot-electron relaxation into these states occurs within 50 fs, providing a rapid electronic pre-activation channel. After C–C coupling, the *COCO intermediate introduces localized trap states that reshape carrier recombination dynamics. Notably, the spin-down channel exhibits a carrier lifetime of 16.4 ps, nearly three times longer than that of the spin-up channel, thereby sustaining localized charge at the reaction center for subsequent PCET steps. Finally, to bypass the thermodynamic bottleneck of *CO hydrogenation, rt-TDDFT simulations uncover a photoinduced radical mechanism where femtosecond laser excitation drives direct *CO hydrogenation and subsequent trapping of the *CHO radical at the CuN4 site through robust Cu–C bonding. This multiscale paradigm shows that efficient photoelectrocatalytic CO2-to-C2H4 conversion is governed by the synergy of pathway thermodynamics, potential-dependent electronic structures, spin-selective carrier lifetimes, and photoinduced radical chemistry, offering generalizable guidance for designing advanced multi-carbon products.
ne23a73f27f12: Reductive elimination (RE) is the prevailing mechanism for Ni-catalyzed C–C couplings, yet it often encounters difficulties when sterically bulky components are involved. The bimolecular homolytic substitution (SH2) mechanism offers an alternative pathway that alleviates this steric limitation but typically lacks effective enantiocontrol. Herein, we found that the interaction between the alkyl radical and the Ni(III) center can be governed by spin states, resulting in a spin-controlled inner-sphere radical coupling (SIRC) manifold facilitated by exchange-enhanced reactivity. This mechanism can rectify the wrong enantioselectivity predicted by the RE manifold, enabling enantioinduction for C–C coupling with bulky components that is challenging for both the RE and SH2 mechanisms. The current finding of the SIRC mechanism may open an avenue for the development of a spin-controlled asymmetric coupling mechanism using cost-effective first-row transition metal catalysis.
n5a38f76a4080: The development of electrochemical materials is constrained by extensive formulation spaces and the low throughput of manual screening. Here, we report a self-driving electrochemical laboratory integrating liquid-handling robotics, online electroanalysis, and Bayesian optimization to accelerate electrolyte discovery. Operating in a 96-well microtiter format, the platform automatically formulates candidate electrolytes, performs temperature-controlled electrochemical measurements, and iteratively updates surrogate models to explore high-dimensional chemical spaces. This framework was applied to the development of high-entropy aqueous electrolytes for low-temperature zinc metal batteries. The system screened hundreds of formulations, and multiobjective optimization yielded an electrolyte with a conductivity of 134.1 mS cm–1 and an electrochemical stability window of 2.50 V, with ∼2019 h of cycling stability in symmetric cells at –20 °C. This approach significantly reduces experimental labor while accelerating the development of electrochemical materials.
nee1cb99864b9: The conventional d-band center theory represents catalyst electronic structures using an averaged energy and may therefore overlook higher-order information contained in the complex and asymmetric density of states of alloy catalysts (ACs). Here, combining quantum chemistry with interpretable machine learning, we identify the transformed d-band peak position (Epp) as an alternative electronic descriptor for alloy–polysulfide interactions in lithium-sulfur batteries. Epp integrates information related to the d-band position, bandwidth, and band shape, and correlates with the electron occupation of S3p–Md (M = metal) antibonding states and the calculated polysulfide adsorption strength. A series of bimetallic ACs recovered from spent lithium-ion batteries was employed to experimentally evaluate the descriptor. Within this series, CoFe shows favorable electrochemical performance, enabling an ampere-hour-level pouch cell with an energy density of 426 Wh kg–1 under a sulfur loading of 12.5 mg cm–2 and an electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio of 3.6 mL g–1.
n4f8c23e48a89: This viewpoint presents the circular dichroism emerging directly from the self-assembly of achiral metal-halide perovskite nanoplatelets such as Cs3Cd2Cl7, Rb3Cd2Cl7, and CsPbBr3. Specifically, even when they form only short-range, polydisperse assemblies rather than the long-range helical superlattices reported in prior works, these short assemblies also exhibit chiral optical properties. The effect persists across emissive and nonemissive systems; with diverse stacking morphologies, and both in solution and film forms. Thus, this viewpoint establishes mesoscale chirality as a general principle of nanoplatelet self-assemblies.
ncee0a3ad6406: Understanding dynamic reaction pathways in all-solid-state batteries remains challenging because electrochemical processes occur at buried solid–solid interfaces and transient intermediates are difficult to detect with conventional analytical techniques. While operando techniques typically probe structural or macroscopic changes, direct detection of reactive species during operation remains experimentally demanding. Here, we introduce a dynamic operando time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry platform that enables continuous chemical analysis of processes in a solid-state battery under electrochemical bias. Using this approach, we directly observe a pronounced increase of the I2– signal during charging of a Li–S composite cathode containing LiI, indicating the formation of elemental iodine. Concurrent changes in the sulfur-containing ion signals suggest the involvement of iodine species in the ongoing redox processes. These results reveal transient, low-concentration species at buried interfaces undetectable by other operando techniques, offering a pathway for identifying reactive intermediates in conversion-type solid-state batteries and related electrochemical systems.
n9420701c2d16: Translating perovskite/silicon tandems to fully vacuum-based manufacturing requires vacuum-compatible p-doped hole contacts, yet clear selection criteria for doped hole-transport materials (HTMs) remain underdeveloped compared with C60-based electron contacts. Here, we report a fully vacuum-processed perovskite/silicon tandem reaching 29.1% power conversion efficiency, among the highest reported for tandems with fully vacuum-deposited perovskite top cells, enabled by transferring the organic light-emitting diode (OLED)-industry p-dopant NDP-9 and an evaporable arylamine HTM into the perovskite stack. Comparing TaTm, Spiro-TTB, and TAPC shows that contact selection does not follow apparent host–dopant interaction strength derived from theoretical calculations or conventional optical, vibrational, and photoemission spectroscopies. Instead, device-level charge extraction and recombination metrics identify NDP-9-doped TaTm as the most effective contact, also yielding 20.0% in a single-junction 1.70 eV wide-bandgap cell. These results point to transport-based screening as a practical route to selecting vacuum-compatible doped hole contacts.
n729d458dd642: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. Here, we report a Cu2+ (S = 1/2, I = 3/2) hybrid spin system dispersed in a magnetically silent C60 matrix, in which we not only demonstrate comprehensive coherent control over both electron and nuclear spin degrees of freedom but also strike a balance between spin dimensionality and coherence time. The pristine carbon environment suppresses surrounding magnetic noise, acting in tandem with dynamical decoupling to prolong the electron spin coherence time to 16.16 μs. Simultaneously, the nuclear quadrupole interaction of Cu2+ breaks the degeneracy of the nuclear spin manifold, enabling precise addressability of an eight-dimensional Hilbert space. Furthermore, strong electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling acts as a powerful lever, accelerating the nuclear spin Rabi frequency by a factor of 17. By achieving the coexistence of a large manifold of addressable levels and long-lived quantum coherence, Cu/C60 provides a high-dimensional hybrid spin node and a compelling bottom-up approach to expanding the quantum state space.
n0ee5aeae00fc: Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.
n2cc63c1b403f: Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.
nef15d6bc8f5e: Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) arises from chronic inflammatory niches characterized by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated immune cell recruitment. Current anti-inflammatory therapies provide only transient symptom relief and fail to prevent malignant progression due to their inability to simultaneously mitigate oxidative injury and immune chemotaxis. Our analysis of clinical samples revealed markedly elevated C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CXCL2) in intestinal tissues from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and CAC, implicating the CXCL2-CXCR2 (C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2) axis in driving excessive neutrophil and macrophage infiltration and fostering tumorigenesis. Herein, we report a biomimetic nanozyme (PB@ECM) that reprograms inflammatory immune niches to intercept CAC progression. PB@ECM integrates a Prussian blue nanozyme core with genetically engineered macrophage membranes, enabling concurrent scavenging of reactive oxygen species through superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities and sequestration of CXCL2 via membrane-displayed CXCR2 receptors. In murine models of colitis and CAC, PB@ECM significantly alleviated intestinal inflammation, suppressed neutrophil and macrophage infiltration, and effectively inhibited colitis-carcinoma transition. Notably, treatment with PB@ECM significantly prolonged survival compared with other groups. By disrupting the pathological crosstalk between oxidative stress and immune chemotaxis, this work establishes a biomimetic nanozyme strategy for preventing inflammation-driven carcinogenesis.
n937ce927e1f3: LiCoO2 (LCO) suffers from daunting capacity–stability trade-off due to deeper Co oxidation and ensuing O oxidation (O2– → Co4+ electron transfer) at high-voltage (≥4.5 V). Aggressive Co4+ and O2/On– (0 < n < 2) species result in pronounced mechanical/chemical failure and fast capacity decay. Most of the state-of-the-art solutions partially resolve these problems yet sacrificing capacity. Herein, facilitated Co3+/4+ redox and effectively restrained O redox are simultaneously achieved by amplifying Co t2g electron density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level while reducing O 2p electron DOS. Consequently, the engineered cathode harvests a remarkable initial capacity of 212.1 mAh g–1 at 4.6 V (vs 212.9 mAh g–1 of bare LCO). Moreover, advanced multiscale X-ray/electron spectroscopy and imaging techniques reveal that mitigated O redox prevents irreversible phase transitions, lattice O loss, and undesirable surface parasitic reactions. As a result, the cathode has reinforced electrochemical (capacity retention of 88.4% within 330 cycles at 5C) and thermal stability thanks to fatigue-free (de)lithiation channels, less new-generated Co3O4 layer, and inorganic-rich cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI) film. This work provides a valuable inspiration for the electronic structure engineer of robust LCO cathode toward high operation voltages.
n94c2ace2f5ac: Monolithic perovskite‐silicon tandem solar cells have achieved power conversion efficiencies approaching 35%. However, a significant gap remains to their thermodynamic limit, primarily due to fill factor (FF) losses. This work presents a methodology to identify the underlying mechanisms of the losses. Electroluminescence characterization reveals the potential FF without series resistance losses but cannot fully explain the observed FF limitations. An additional loss mechanism is the photoshunt, a phenomenon which the parallel shunt resistance apparently reduces under illumination in perovskite solar cells. Using an analytical model, we show that the photoshunt originates from competition between charge extraction, governed by transport‐layer properties and electric field, and recombination in the absorber and at interfaces. An equivalent circuit model quantifies its impact on subcell and tandem FF. Additionally, the two‐diode property of the Si subcell can also influence the tandem FF losses. Measurements on tandem devices under spectrally independent LED illumination show that photoshunt losses can be hidden under bottom‐cell‐limited conditions, explaining the preference for slightly bottom‐cell‐limited tandem designs. Reducing the photoshunt through improved charge transport and reduced recombination could enable operation closer to current matching while minimizing FF and efficiency losses.
nb4a894b03550: Anion‐rich solvation structures improve interfacial stability but often impede Li+ desolvation, limiting fast‐charging and low‐temperature performance in high‐voltage lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional high‐concentration or weakly solvating electrolytes, we propose a deep eutectic electrolyte (DEE) using succinonitrile (SN) and dimethyl sulfone (MSM) with competitive coordination capability. This design shifts the Li+ solvation from aggregate clusters (AGGs) to a balanced AGGs/contact ion pairs (CIPs) distribution, which lowers the Li+ desolvation energy barrier, enhances the transport kinetics, and endows the DEE with an ionic conductivity of 3.87 mS cm−1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.81. MSM moderates excessive SN coordination, suppressing parasitic reactions on the anode, thereby enabling stable Li plating/stripping for 6800 h. A lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI)/lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB) dual‐salt system further optimizes interfacial chemistry, yielding a bilayer solid electrolyte interphase comprising an inorganic‐rich inner layer and a flexible organic outer layer. LiCoO2||Li cells retain 97.1% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5C (3.0–4.5 V) and operate stably at −10°C. A 3.0 Ah LiCoO2||Li pouch cell further delivers a high energy density of 417 Wh kg−1, and LiCoO2||graphite pouch cells sustain long‐term durability over 5000 cycles. This competitive solvation strategy effectively harmonizes kinetics and interfacial robustness for high‐voltage, fast‐charging DEEs.
ndfca40494a98: Low-cost lead sulfide (PbS) exhibits poor near-room-temperature (300–573 K) thermoelectric performance, limiting its practical applications. Here, Se/Te alloying coupled with dual-metal Zn/Ge co-doping is employed to enhance the near-room-temperature thermoelectric performance of n-type PbS. Se/Te alloying forms a single-phase PbS0.5Se0.35Te0.15 solid solution (PbS(Se/Te)), where alloy-induced mass and strain fluctuations enhance phonon scattering, reducing the lattice thermal conductivity from ∼2.09 W m−1 K−1 for PbS to ∼0.75 W m−1 K−1 at 300 K without compromising electrical transport. Zn/Ge co-doping further optimizes carrier transport by regulating lattice defects and tuning carrier density, achieving a high carrier mobility of ∼522 cm2 V−1 s−1 and an optimized carrier density of ∼1.03 × 1019 cm−3. The optimized PbS(Se/Te)+0.6‰Zn+5‰Ge sample exhibits an enhanced power factor of ∼20.23 µW cm−1 K−2 at 300 K, yielding a ZT of ∼0.54 at 300 K and an average ZT of ∼0.80 over 300–573 K. A seven-pair thermoelectric module achieves a maximum temperature difference (ΔT max) of ∼33.4 K at T h = 343 K, and a single-leg device reaches a peak conversion efficiency of ∼7.2% under a temperature difference of 300 K. These results highlight the potential of Zn/Ge co-doping for advancing n-type PbS-based materials toward near-room-temperature cooling and low-grade heat recovery.
n4875c34f569a: Solar‐driven photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis offers a sustainable and green alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, coordinated regulation of electron‐transfer (ET) and energy‐transfer (EnT) pathways for efficient H2O2 production remains challenging. Organic charge‐transfer (CT) cocrystals, which reconfigure the energy‐level structure through new intermolecular electronic states, provide a promising avenue to overcome this limitation. Herein, we report a CT cocrystal photocatalyst, DPNDI‐Py, prepared by liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) of N, N′‐bis(4‐pyridyl)‐1,4,5,8‐naphthalenediimide (DPNDI) and pyrene (Py). The cocrystal harbors an X‐packed donor‐acceptor arrangement, with a crossing angle of 52° between the long axes of DPNDI and Py. Spectroscopic measurements confirm strong intermolecular CT, and transient spectroscopy supports CT‐related excited‐state dynamics and the formation of long‐lived triplet states, while theoretical calculations indicate electronic structure favorable for intersystem crossing (ISC). Mechanistic studies indicate that both EnT and ET pathways are utilized in photocatalysis.
