Under LED irradiation in air, DPNDI‐Py delivers an average H2O2 production rate of 18.47 ± 0.57 mmol g−1 h−1 coupled with an 83.7 ± 2.26% dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) yield from ascorbic acid (AA) oxidation. This work provides mechanistic insight into CT‐mediated photocatalysis, offering a design principle for organic photocatalysts.
n57a04cda272c: Powering autonomous electronics, sensors, and wearable systems using small‐scale daily mechanical energy is becoming increasingly important. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a lightweight, flexible, and adaptable route for such applications, particularly when movements are involved. Here, we present a first‐of‐its‐kind unified dynamic energy‐transfer framework for TENGs, coupling their mechanical and electrical domains through a lumped element‐based equivalent circuit (LEEC) model. The framework captures time‐varying electrostatic behavior and key mechanical parameters, mass, damping, and stiffness, within a single predictive platform, enabling system‐level analysis of dynamic efficiency, impedance, resonance, and power transfer under different excitation conditions. The Thévenin equivalent model reveals that TENG performance is dynamically governed by excitation frequency, resonance, load matching, and surface charge density, approaching a time‐averaged theoretical efficiency of ∼54%. Experimental validation across devices with varied mechanical parameters shows close agreement with theory in electrical response and frequency‐dependent behavior. Furthermore, four borophene‐modified TENGs with different charge‐generation characteristics exhibit a systematic increase in electrical output and an estimated efficiency of up to 14.2% for the examined parameter space, supporting the model‐predicted dependence of energy‐conversion performance on surface charge density. The LEEC‐guided platform enables coupled energy and information harvesting through resonance‐enhanced capacitor charging and self‐powered road‐state sensing.
n1240161b5150: Cosolvent engineering for aqueous Zn metal batteries has traditionally emphasized thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the kinetic dimension of Zn2+ charge transfer—particularly in multi‐cosolvent systems—remains far less understood. Here we conduct a systematic study on a dual‐cosolvent electrolyte pairing a strong cosolvent (DMSO) with a weak cosolvent (DMC). Through spatial decoupling, the strong cosolvent directly coordinates to stabilize the primary solvation shell, while the weak cosolvent forms a dynamic outer‐shell buffer. This unique context modulates Zn–ligand binding, facilitates desolvation, and guides the formation of a regulated SEI. Consequently, this architecture preserves comparably high thermodynamic stability while unlocking a nonlinear kinetic optimization exclusive to the dual‐cosolvent regime. Using a multi‐descriptor framework, we demonstrate a ∼40% reduction in the charge‐transfer barrier relative to single‐cosolvent systems. This kinetic enhancement translates into robust practical performance, establishing strong–weak cosolvent synergy as a versatile design principle for next‐generation aqueous batteries.
nc052dd5fc2d1: Perovskite thin films featuring out‐of‐plane oriented (100) crystallographic facets are pivotal for advancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells, owing to their superior charge transport properties and reduced deep‐level defect density. However, conventional single‐strategy modification approaches are typically constrained by limited control over crystal orientation and spatially heterogeneous orientation distribution, hindering the full exploitation of such beneficial facets. Herein, we present a surface‐bulk synergistic induction strategy that overcomes the limitations of single modification approaches, effectively promoting directional grain alignment and cooperatively guiding ordered out‐of‐plane growth during thermal annealing. Benefiting from the successful fabrication of a perovskite film with a uniform and predominant preferred orientation, the inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.98% (certified 26.41%). Furthermore, the homogeneous texture and high intrinsic stability of the (100) facets enable the devices to retain 93.5% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of operational stability testing. This strategy effectively tackles the technical constraints of precursor solution regulation and solid‐state surface treatment, offering a novel research model for the precise modulation of perovskite thin film crystal facets and the secondary growth of polycrystalline thin films.
n76be03421574: Given the prominence of azetidine derivatives in pharmaceutical chemistry, developing their catalytic synthesis continues to attract strong attention from synthetic chemists. While the strain‐release ring opening and functionalizations of 1‐azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) has become a promising route to access diverse azetidines and 1‐azabicyclic molecules since their discovery in the late 1960s, such transformations were mostly operated under stoichiometric conditions, and reactions facilitated by catalysis have only emerged recently. The integration of catalysis in ABB chemistry has enabled innovative reaction development, particularly through the interception of transient reaction intermediates—for instance, C3‐radical and N1‐anion—to allow divergent transformations, thereby achieving unprecedented synthetic versatility. This mini‐review summarizes recent advances in catalytic strain‐release ring opening and functionalizations of ABBs from a mechanistic‐centered perspective. The reaction pathways are categorized into polar ring opening, radical ring opening, and polar ring opening with radical crossover. The features of each class of reaction are presented for the identification of mechanistic commonalities and differences across diverse transformations.
nd899260105ef: The application of cycloparaphenylene (CPP) macrocycles in organic photovoltaics has remained largely unexplored despite their unique three‐dimensional (3D) topologies. Herein, we expand the functional scope of CPPs by covalently integrating a carbon‐nanohoop scaffold with Y‐series electron acceptors to develop a novel 3D trimeric acceptor, CPP‐3Y. Distinct from conventional planar molecules, CPP‐3Y combines radially oriented π‐conjugation, a continuously curved π‐surface, and sterically hindered 3D topology, resulting in strong aggregation with low crystallinity. When introduced as a third component into the D18:L8‐BO‐X binary system, CPP‐3Y preferentially associates with the L8‐BO‐X‐rich acceptor phase, resulting in large fibrillar structures in blended thin films. This narrows the energetic tail‐state distribution, suppresses trap‐assisted and non‐radiative recombination, and enables more balanced charge transport. Consequently, D18:L8‐BO‐X:CPP‐3Y ternary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.62%, outperforming binary devices (19.90%). They also retain over 80% of their initial efficiency after 964 h at 70 °C, whereas the binary devices fall below this level after 432 h. This work demonstrates that cyclic electron acceptors with 3D configurations and strong aggregation can act as morphological regulators to tune the phase separation of photoactive layers and hence realize high PCEs in OSCs.
n1750bf2dcda0: Programmable soft actuators require independent control over both deformation pathways and driving‐force output, yet conventional shape‐memory systems generally encode these functions within a fixed network and therefore exhibit predetermined recovery behavior. Herein, we report a porous shape‐memory polymer/hydrogel actuator (SMP‐Net gel) that transforms fixed‐force shape recovery into ion‐programmable actuation. The actuator integrates a thermally programmable glycerol‐polycaprolactone methacrylic anhydride (GPCL‐MA) scaffold with an interpenetrating PAM/PVA hydrogel network. The porous scaffold determines the macroscopic shape‐memory trajectory, whereas the confined hydrogel functions as a Hofmeister‐responsive internal force reservoir. Ion‐specific regulation of chain aggregation and hydrogen bonding enables broad adjustment of the mechanical state, with strain and stress tunable over 43%–140% and 0.83–1.80 MPa, respectively, while simultaneously accelerating or retarding NIR‐triggered shape recovery. This dual‐driving architecture further supports reversible shape programming, controllable bending amplitude, recovery‐time regulation, and spatially selective deformation under localized NIR irradiation. Remote gripping, release, and multistep motion demonstrate the capability of the SMP‐Net gel for complex actuation tasks. This work establishes a general strategy for integrating shape‐memory scaffolds with ion‐regulated soft networks, opening a new route toward adaptive actuators, biomimetic machines, and intelligent soft robotic systems.
n9d02bbb15f0e: The introduction of polycatenane junctions into dative B←N bond‐linked covalent organic polymers (COPs) poses a significant synthetic challenge for the synergistic optimization of both geometric stabilization and molecular functionality. Herein, we strategically employ tritopic borate ligands bearing terminal –Br substituents, rather than their ditopic counterparts, as precursors to construct a single‐crystalline COP (JNP‐7) featuring polycatenane‐like topological junctions. Specifically, B‐centered Lewis acceptors and N‐donor units initially assemble into 1D nanoribbons via dative B←N linkages. By leveraging inter‐nanoribbon halogen···halogen interactions between the semi‐interlocked Br‐containing motifs, the architecture is further extended into 2D arrays, thereby elevating the geometric dimensionality of JNP‐7. Critically, the resulting polycatenated halogen‐bonded network imparts exceptional structural rigidity, and the dative B←N motifs are found to concurrently promote visible‐light harvesting and facilitate charge‐carrier migration. Consequently, JNP‐7 enables highly efficient H2O2 production via both the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and water oxidation reaction (WOR) under ambient sunlight, operating without sacrificial agents, photosensitizers, or metal cocatalysts, and outperforming state‐of‐the‐art covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) in terms of photocatalytic activity and apparent quantum yield (AQY). By aligning molecular topology with catalytic function, this work establishes a generalizable framework for the rational development of topologically sophisticated, high‐performance COP systems.
nf685e4208bb7: Solid tumors pose major therapeutic hurdles due to pathophysiological barriers such as hypoxia and dense stroma, which severely restrict drug penetration. Conventional nanomedicines lack the autonomous capability to navigate these evolving obstacles. Here, we engineer a DNA‑based nanorobot constructed on an optimized tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNA) that co‑assembles tumor‑targeting aptamers, catalytic platinum nanoparticles (Pt‑NPs), and the therapeutic payload methylene blue (MB) into a single modular platform. This integrated design enables three coordinated functions: tumor‑specific recognition, self‑propelled transport driven by oxygen generation, and concurrent hypoxia alleviation to potentiate photodynamic therapy (PDT) in hypoxic tumors. The Pt‐NPs catalyze the decomposition of overproduced hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in the tumor microenvironment, generating oxygen bubbles that both drive deep tissue penetration (to depths > 300 µm) and alleviate local hypoxia. This self‑powered propulsion enables efficient delivery of MB, leading to cascaded PDT activation. In vivo, the nanorobot achieves 85% tumor regression through the coordinated actions of deep penetration, hypoxia relief, and enhanced PDT. This modular DNA nanoplatform provides a promising strategy for advanced nanomedicine by autonomously addressing key delivery barriers in solid tumor therapy.
nae8d96df1b32: Developing molecular materials with high intrinsic n-type electrical conductivity (σ) independent of extrinsic doping remains a formidable challenge in organic electronics. Herein, we report a novel acceptor–acceptor type open-shell conjugated polymer (OSCP), PBBT-gDPP, featuring a proquinoidal benzobis(1,2,5-thiadiazole) (BBT)-based backbone and polar oligo(ethylene glycol) side chains. In-depth spectroscopic, electrochemical, and magnetic characterizations uncover that this acceptor–acceptor architecture, benefiting from its planar backbone and multiple proquinoidal units, yields an ultra-narrow bandgap (E g < 0.6 eV), an open-shell triplet ground state (S = 1), and significant diradicaloid character. These features, complemented by polar side chains that modulate the local dielectric environment to assist in polaron transport, result in a high intrinsic σ of 9.21 S cm−1 with substantial ambient stability and a power factor of 6.49 µW m−1 K−2 when PBBT-gDPP is applied as an n-type single-component organic thermoelectric material. The conductivity surpasses those of previously reported undoped conjugated materials. Notably, the near-amorphous morphology, characterized by a high paracrystalline disorder parameter of ∼23%, imparts exceptional mechanical robustness, retaining 80% of its initial σs after 3000 bending cycles. This work underscores the significant potential of polar high-spin OSCPs for next-generation, dopant-free, and flexible organic electronics.
nbd875668bd4c: Bacteria compete not only by killing rivals but also by disrupting their developmental programs, yet the molecular basis of such nonlethal interference remains largely unknown. Here, we report tamastrepamides, a family of alkylproline‐containing cyclodepsipeptides from Streptomyces sp. HL19 that function as interspecific effectors by selectively downregulating transcription of the master developmental regulator bldD. The horizontally acquired tam biosynthetic gene cluster is conspicuously enriched in rare TTA codons, functionally coupling its expression to the developmentally regulated tRNALeu(UAA) encoded by bldA. Tamastrepamide A arrests sporulation and diminishes secondary metabolite production in diverse actinomycetes without inhibiting vegetative growth, thereby chemically phenocopying a ΔbldD mutant. Promoter‐specific reporter assays demonstrate that tamastrepamide A reduces bldD promoter activity, while the producer strain is intrinsically insensitive to this effect. Production of tamastrepamides strictly depends on the functionally specialized tRNALeu(UAA), revealing a self‐contained regulatory circuit in which a developmentally gated metabolite disables the same developmental program in neighboring competitors. These findings illustrate an ecological strategy in which a developmentally regulated biosynthetic pathway produces a diffusible metabolite that interferes with the sporulation program of competing actinomycetes.
nbdd0ef6ce48c: Hydride addition to diphosphine‐borane (DPB) coinage‐metal complexes affords an unprecedented series of Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I) hydridoborate complexes 2‐M featuring bridging B–H···M interactions. Combined multinuclear NMR, IR, single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, and DFT studies reveal the presence of agostic‐type σ(B–H)→M interactions across the series, with the strongest interaction observed for copper. These hydridoborate species are thermodynamically favored over the corresponding metal hydrides. Markedly distinct reactivity is observed depending on the coinage metal. Whereas, the Cu and Ag congeners proved to be unreactive toward CO2, the Au complex 2‐Au cleanly and reversibly fixes CO2 to form the isolable Au(I) formate complex 3‐Au. In addition to quantitative and reversible CO2 uptake and release, the Au hydridoborate complex 2‐Au is an efficient and robust catalyst for the hydroboration of CO2 to HCO2Bpin and the dehydrogenation of formic acid, both with complete selectivity. Experimental and computational studies support a cooperative mechanism in which the B─H─Au motif acts as a masked gold hydride, thanks to hydride transfer.
n492674506d67: Electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to formate offers a sustainable route for carbon utilization, converting a greenhouse gas into a valuable chemical feedstock. Although Sn‑based catalysts are among the most promising candidates, their formate selectivity often suffers a marked decline at ampere‑level current densities, and operating efficiently in various electrolytes, especially acidic media, remains a major challenge. In this work, we report a grain boundary‑rich sulfur (S)‐doped SnO2 catalyst that enables CO2‐to‐formate electrosynthesis at ampere‐level current densities across alkaline, neutral, and acidic electrolytes. The catalyst achieves formate Faradaic efficiencies exceeding 90% at 1 A cm−2 in acidic, neutral, and alkaline electrolytes. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations reveal that S doping reduces the reaction free energy change for the key *OCHO intermediate and promotes its protonation to formate. Meanwhile, S‑doped SnO2 with abundant grain boundaries facilitates the formation of an enhanced interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, which promotes efficient proton transfer while suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work provides new insights into the design of high‐performance electrocatalysts through elemental doping and elucidates the governing role of the interfacial microenvironment in reaction activity and selectivity, offering design principles applicable to broader electrochemical syntheses.
n7f5acbcfc7d7: Plant polyphenols and related oxygen‐donor phytochemicals are attractive natural ligands for metal–organic materials owing to their rich chemical reactivity, structural diversity, and sustainability. However, current phytochemical coordination chemistry remains dominated by amorphous systems, and structurally resolved crystalline frameworks are still largely restricted to simple and symmetric molecules. This gap has hindered atom‐level understanding of phytochemical coordination and limited the rational development of crystalline materials from these abundant natural ligands. Here, we report SCU‐1, the first structurally resolved crystalline coordination framework constructed from hematoxylin (HMT), a historically important but structurally complex and asymmetric phytochemical. Structural modeling, three‐dimensional electron diffraction (3DED), Rietveld refinement, and quantum‐chemical calculations together reveal that such an asymmetric phytochemical can assemble into periodic crystalline frameworks while generating coordination heterogeneity. Structural resolution further defines precise pore architectures, coordination environments, and host–guest interaction sites, thereby enabling direct elucidation of structure–property relationships. Importantly, SCU‐1 exhibits exceptional robustness, strong CO2 affinity, and visible‐light‐driven photocatalytic CO2 conversion in water with selective ethanol production. These results establish asymmetric phytochemicals as viable building units for robust crystalline metal–organic materials and demonstrate the importance of structural determinacy in advancing phytochemical coordination chemistry and structure–property relationships.
n091f8a4c9f24: “I chose chemistry as a career because I fell in love with it in eighth grade, and the reaction has proved irreversible… The most important feature of a good working environment is a shared sense of humor and the ability to discuss mistakes openly, learn from them, and move forward together…” Find out more about Andrey Belyaev in his Introducing… Profile.
n8fe546e82c67: Surface frustrated Lewis pairs (SFLPs) have been widely studied as active sites for light‐assisted CO2 hydrogenation, while most efforts have focused on cation engineering to tune the Lewis acidity of metal centers, leaving the Lewis‐basic component less directly controlled. Here, we report an anion engineering strategy based on nitridation to prepare nitrogen‐doped, non‐stoichiometric spinel zinc gallium oxide catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. Nitrogen incorporation modifies the local anion coordination environment, promotes oxygen vacancy formation, and reconstructs the coordination structure around Ga sites, thereby generating defect‐associated Ga–O/N Lewis acid–base pairs that favor heterolytic H2 splitting. Nitridation also narrows the band gap and introduces localized electronic states, leading to improved light absorption. As a result, the optimized catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 1203.7 µmol h−1 g−1 with enhanced methanol selectivity and apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) under illumination. This work demonstrates that anion engineering provides an effective route to regulate oxide SFLPs and promote light‐assisted CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.
n5f99ad814b13: The development of noble-metal-free heterogeneous catalysts for room-temperature aerobic ammoxidation of alcohols to nitriles represents an enduring challenge, primarily hampered by unselective lattice-oxygen over-oxidation via the classical Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) pathway and strong site-blocking effects. Herein, we report a dual-anion (C/N) doped MnO x (C/N–MnO x ) synthesized via a green, solvent-free crystallization strategy, which exhibits excellent catalytic performance (95.3% benzyl alcohol conversion, >99% benzonitrile selectivity) and broad substrate versatility (35 diverse alcohol substrates) under ambient conditions (25°C, 1 atm O2) without external energy inputs. Structural analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that N-doping introduces medium-strong Lewis acidic Mn–N sites to capture NH3, while C-doping generates localized oxygen vacancies for O2 activation. Crucially, kinetic isotope effect experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations prove that this anion dopant-programmed relay catalysis successfully bypasses the MvK pathway, fundamentally shifting the rate-determining step from initial alcohol dehydrogenation to the homolytic α–C–H bond scission of the aldimine intermediate. This work presents a paradigm shift in designing multifunctional non-precious catalysts for ambient-condition green organic transformations.
n5e9c571db756: Thiazoles are ubiquitous motifs in bioactive molecules, making strategies for the stereospecific installation of chiral C(sp3)‐rich substituents on this scaffold particularly valuable for drug discovery. However, achieving such transformations remains nontrivial, as conventional C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross‐coupling approaches are often compromised by catalyst deactivation and deleterious side reactions, such as β‐hydride elimination. Although electrophile‐mediated coupling of alkyl boronic esters with lithiated aromatic compounds offers a potential route to C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation, it is ineffective for thiazoles because the heteroaromatic core lacks sufficient nucleophilicity to engage electrophiles and promote productive 1,2‐migration. Herein, we report a lithiation–borylation–aromatic Pummerer (LiBAP) strategy that enables stereospecific C5 cross‐coupling of thiazoles with boronic esters. A pendant sulfinyl group enables exocyclic electrophilic activation, triggering a Pummerer‐type 1,2‐migration while avoiding unproductive C─B bond fragmentation. The reaction proceeds with complete stereospecificity and broad functional‐group tolerance, furnishing a C2 sulfide handle on thiazole that serves as a versatile linchpin for downstream C–S diversification. A formal asymmetric synthesis of a bioactive thiazole γ‐secretase inhibitor was demonstrated to further highlight the synthetic utility of our LiBAP protocol.
n4c46fe91c424: Understanding how second metal species modulate catalytic performance remains a central challenge in bimetallic heterogeneous catalysis. Here, we report a controllable strategy to construct atomically contacted and spatially isolated structures between Pt3 clusters and Cu atoms on γ‐Al2O3 by atomic layer deposition (ALD), enabling direct interrogation of metal–metal synergy. By regulating anchoring sites around Pt clusters, Cu atoms can be selectively positioned either by bonding to Pt to form Pt3Cu1 clusters or by separating into isolated Cu single atoms. Comprehensive characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that Cu single atom can act as an effective promoter only when directly bonded to Pt3 clusters. As electron donator, the bonded Cu atom can enhance the hydrogen dissociation ability of Pt clusters, weaken their strong acetylene adsorption, and facilitate ethylene desorption, thereby overcoming the activity‐selectivity trade‐off in selective hydrogenation of trace acetylene. In contrast, isolated Cu single atom fails to promote Pt3 clusters and even deteriorate selectivity. These results demonstrate that Pt─Cu bond formation, rather than simple proximity, governs synergistic effects in bimetallic cluster catalysts. This work establishes a clear design principle for atomically engineered catalysts and offers a general strategy to independently optimize catalytic activity and selectivity.
n0c7ac7d0ad77: Despite the importance of heteroaryl atropisomers in medicinal chemistry and catalysis, straightforward access to these motifs via direct enantioselective C─H heteroaryl‐aryl coupling remains challenging. We report an enantioselective Pd(0)‐catalyzed arylation at the C4‐position of thiazole N‐oxides, forging the critical atropochiral axis. A designer point‐ and axially chiral monodentate phosphine is instrumental to enable high reactivities along with tight stereocontrol. A broad range of substrate combinations is coupled in high enantioselectivities, including two different heteroarenes. The enantioenriched thiazole N‐oxides are amenable to derivatizations around the substituents contributing to the stability of the chiral axis, including a reduction of the N‐oxide moiety without racemization.
n15248444703d: Herein, we report the Aza‐Büchner–Curtius–Schlotterbeck reaction (ABCS)– a novel method for the uncatalyzed C─C insertion reaction of photogenerated donor‐donor diazo compounds into aryl aldimines. The transformation proceeds under very mild conditions and high chemoselectivity, favoring C─C over C─H insertion pathways. In a single step, two C(sp2)─C(sp3) bonds are formed, granting access to homologated imines bearing a newly constructed quaternary carbon center in good yields. Subsequent hydrolysis gave homologated aldehydes, enabling versatile downstream transformations. The diazo intermediate is generated using a continuous‐flow microreactor, enhancing both safety and scalability. Mechanistic insights, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, reveal the origins of the observed selectivity and reactivity.
n320d9e8f9aff: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production has emerged as a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive anthraquinone process, yet its efficiency remains fundamentally limited by inefficient charge transport and electron-hole recombination. Here, we report a bioinspired strategy for constructing face-to-face supramolecular co-assembled arrays (FF-SCAAs), in which periodic co-facial organization serves as a structural platform for programming electron transport pathways toward enhanced photocatalytic H2O2 production. Inspired by the signal-transport arrays of natural compound eyes, cationic trioxatriangulenium (TOTA+ ) and electron-rich benzophenanthrene derivatives are integrated into highly ordered FF-SCAAs through directional cation-π interaction. The resulting FF-SCAAs feature enhanced dipole moments and favorable orbital alignment, enabling extended charge transport channels while intrinsically suppressing electron-hole recombination. On this basis, FF-SCAAs achieve a H2O2 photosynthesis rate up to 6.46 mmol g−1 h−1 with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.84%. Ultrafast spectroscopic and mechanistic studies demonstrate that the periodic co-facial arrays promote directional excited-state electron migration and selective two-electron oxygen reduction pathways for H2O2 generation. Furthermore, the in situ generated H2O2 is fed into a cascade wastewater treatment system and consumed in a downstream Fenton process for efficient degradation of phenolic pollutants.
n3d132543698e: Sluggish bulk hole transport fundamentally limits the performance of bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) photoanodes in photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Herein, we report a BiVO4/Fe-MOF/NiFeOOH trilayer photoanode, wherein an iron-based bipyridine dicarboxylate metal–organic framework (FeBPDCA), grown on BiVO4 via coordination-assisted in situ synthesis, serves as a dedicated hole-transport layer. The Fe-MOF layer provides a favorable band alignment and a built-in electric field at the BiVO4/Fe-MOF interface to drive directional bulk hole extraction, while NiFeOOH acts as a surface water-oxidation cocatalyst. Experimental characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Fe-MOF primarily accelerates bulk hole extraction, whereas NiFeOOH suppresses surface recombination through rapid water oxidation, together boosting both bulk charge-separation efficiency (η bulk) and surface charge-transfer efficiency (η trans) up to 97%. The optimized photoanode achieves a high photocurrent density of 7.15 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, with an onset potential of 0.24 V and a maximum applied bias photon-to-current efficiency (ABPE) of 2.56%. This work demonstrates that deliberate tuning of MOF energy levels through metal node and ligand selection enables the simultaneous engineering of favorable band alignment and efficient charge separation at semiconductor/MOF junctions, providing a practical design strategy for photoanodes where bulk charge extraction is the primary efficiency bottleneck.
n5a6df1c85780: We report that water undergoes rapid oxidative addition to readily accessible dioxaphospholes and ‐phospholanes within minutes at room temperature. The resulting phenylphosphinate esters release dihydrogen under mild conditions (room temperature to 60°C) in a borane‐catalyzed process. Remarkably, a pinacol‐derived dioxaphospholane reacts spontaneously with atmospheric moisture under ambient conditions to form the corresponding phenylphosphinate ester, thereby enabling the direct utilization of water from air for catalytic hydrogen evolution. The mechanism of the borane‐catalyzed dehydrogenation was investigated by variable time normalization analysis, targeted synthesis of intermediates, and DFT calculations. These studies support a catalytic pathway initiated by hydrogen elimination from the borane adduct of the phosphinate ester, followed by retro‐hydroboration to regenerate the catalyst.
n4f10ecefb24d: Lenacapavir (LEN), the first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor (CAI) with picomolar potency and long pharmacokinetics (PK), is approved for both treatment and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). However, the frequently selected M66I mutation confers complete resistance to LEN. Potent antivirals against the M66I variant remain elusive. In this work, we have designed LEN analogs featuring a distinctive R 2 moiety to directly address the molecular mechanism of resistance. Our analog synthesis also entailed developing a new synthetic procedure for R 2 incorporation. Significantly, the newly designed analogs were highly potent against both WT HIV-1 and the M66I mutant. Particularly, lead compound 3S conferred 2.6-fold higher potency than LEN against WT HIV-1 and remained highly potent (EC50 = 5.8 nM) against the M66I mutant, a drastically advanced activity profile over LEN (EC50 > 15 µM). The unprecedented potency of our lead 3S against M66I was corroborated by a thermal shift assay. In a head‑to‑head intravenous (IV) PK study in rats, lead 3S demonstrated superior systemic exposure, showing a 4.6‑fold greater plasma area-under-curve (AUC) than LEN and largely retaining the long PK characteristic of LEN. These results strongly validate our design and represent a breakthrough in LEN-based HIV-1 therapy and prophylaxis.
nb58f0620a7be: Transition‐metal‐catalyzed nitrene transfer reactions offer a powerful strategy for direct C─H bond amination; however, the nature of the key reactive intermediates, particularly with Cp*Co(III) systems, remains elusive. Herein, we report a cobalt‐catalyzed allylic C─H amidation of unactivated alkenes using dioxazolones as practical nitrene precursors. The isolation of a well‐defined π‐allyl‐cobalt(III) complex provides a platform for direct interrogation of the reactive nitrene species. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, support the involvement of an open‐shell singlet cobalt–nitrenoid intermediate. Both the neutral cobalt(III) precatalyst and the synthesized π‐allyl‐cobalt(III) complex are catalytically active, and the catalytic system displays broad substrate scope, good functional‐group tolerance, and moderate to high regioselectivity. These results provide key mechanistic insights into cobalt‐mediated nitrene transfer reactions and establish a foundation for the development of selective cobalt‐catalyzed C─H amination reactions.
n7674ca4520f5: The introduction of ortho‐methyl substituents on aryl‐substituted ortho‐tetrafluoroazobenzene photoswitches breaks the π‐conjugation and improves photoswitching selectivity and increases the thermal half‐life of the metastable isomer. Using this approach, a visible‐light‐responsive ligand was assembled with a non‐switchable ligand and palladium(II) ions into a mixture of molecular cages. When irradiated with 530 nm light, the system converges to form a single product, a metastable, mixed‐ligand molecular cage. This cage can be reversibly disassembled using 424 nm light, an example of integrative self‐sorting controlled by light. The metastable assembly can catalyze both Michael addition and nitroaldol reactions. Importantly, visible light accesses a metastable catalytic state inaccessible under thermodynamic control. We demonstrate that the active assembled species can be switched on and off at will using visible irradiation and the metastable species is the most catalytically active assembly.
nafacf0e3f208: Catalyst‐controlled nitrene transfer enables divergent amination reactions of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes through distinct modes of activation of their highly strained central σ‐bond. Under Rh(II) catalysis, bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes undergo selective strain‐release amination to furnish aminocyclobutenes, which provide efficient access to cyclobutane amino acids through a simple amination–hydrogenation sequence. In contrast, photocatalytic nitrene activation redirects the reaction pathway toward double amination and skeletal remodeling, affording functionalized dihydropyrrolidines that can be readily converted into pyrrole heterocycles under acidic conditions. The synthetic utility of both approaches is further demonstrated, for example, in a telescoped synthesis of cyclobutane amino acids from diazo precursors or downstream diversification reactions. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies reveal distinct catalyst‐dependent nitrene activation pathways that govern the fate of a common reactive intermediate and underpin the observed divergent reactivity.
n0b1aa42e57c4: Photo‐induced hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalysis has become a powerful platform for the direct and selective functionalization of ubiquitous C─H bonds. Traditionally, the outcome of these transformations is dictated by the interplay between C─H bond dissociation energies and polar effects, enabling predictable yet inherently substrate‐controlled selectivity. Recently, a fundamentally new strategy has emerged that relies on the catalytic and reversible modulation of substrate electronics to transiently enhance the reactivity of targeted C─H bonds. Notably, catalytic full or partial deprotonation of oxygen‐ and nitrogen‐containing functional groups has proven remarkably effective in selectively activating adjacent C─H bonds toward HAT, a phenomenon known as the anionic substituent effect. Rather than relying solely on the intrinsic properties of a substrate, this concept allows chemists to reprogram C─H bond reactivity in situ, unlocking previously inaccessible levels of selectivity in the direct functionalization of abundant functional groups under mild photocatalytic conditions. In this minireview, we discuss the mechanistic principles underpinning catalytic anionic substituent effects (CASE), the diverse strategies developed to generate them, and their impact on photocatalytic HAT‐mediated C–H functionalization. By highlighting recent advances and emerging opportunities, we illustrate how transient electronic activation is reshaping the design of selective C–H functionalization reactions.
na1a3b0fa4025: There has been a recent surge in research aimed at synthesizing inherently chiral macrocycles that lack point, axial, planar, or helical chirality. To overcome the structural limitations of existing inherently chiral macrocyclic systems, which often suffer from facile racemization due to conformational flexibility, we report herein an asymmetric synthesis of a new class of inherently chiral double‐macrocyclic molecules through an intramolecular macrocyclization strategy, employing calix[4]arenes as the starting platform. Catalyzed by [Pd(allyl)Cl]2 and a chiral phosphoramidite ligand, calix[4]arene derivatives bearing a monoaryl bromide linker at the upper rim underwent a facile enantioselective remote transannular Suzuki–Miyaura coupling with the adjacent upper‐rim position of the neighboring arene unit, furnishing the desired inherently chiral double‐calixarene macrocycles in up to 71% yield and 91% ee. The resulting double macrocycles feature stable conformations and unique semi‐enveloped chiral cavities, and exhibit promising chiral catalytic and chiroptical properties.
n647b387306d5: Purely organic luminescent materials are pivotal for optoelectronics, with chalcogen‐fused phenazines serving as basic building blocks owing to their strong electron donating ability and enhanced spin–orbit coupling effect. However, a systematic understanding of how the chalcogen identity governs intrinsic conformational preference between quasi‐axial (QA) and quasi‐equatorial (QE) forms remains elusive. To address this, we designed a series of derivatives featuring phenoxazine, phenothiazine, and phenoselenazine donors coupled with a terpyridine acceptor. We demonstrate that the chalcogen atom dictates molecular conformation: phenoxazine derivative exclusively adopts the QE conformation, phenothiazine derivative predominantly favors QE, while phenoselenazine derivative stabilizes in the QA form. Notably, heating induces a phase transition in polymorphs toward their thermodynamically favored conformations. Furthermore, Zn2+ coordination enhances intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) strength, shifting the thermodynamically preferred conformation and triggering a switch from room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) to dual RTP–delayed fluorescence (DF) emission. This work validates the chalcogen‐determined conformation and ICT strength can effectively modulates DF/RTP performance, deepening the fundamental understanding of the chalcogen‐mediated conformation and properties for the rational design of organic luminescent materials.
n4bf9e90ab524: Polyketides constitute a major class of natural products with remarkable structural diversity and biological activities. While bacteria predominantly produce polyketides via modular type I polyketide synthases (PKSs), eukaryotic modular PKSs remain largely unexplored. Here, we report the functional characterization of a fungal modular PKS system from Lasiodiplodia theobromae through heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae, leading to the production of the antimalarial macrolide strasseriolide C (1). Intriguingly, biosynthesis of 1 involves C‐methylation of the starter malonyl unit despite the absence of a methyltransferase domain in the loading module. Furthermore, module 2 of the PKS system contains an unusual arrangement of four consecutive acyl carrier protein (ACP) domains. Although the catalytic basis of this methylation remains unresolved, our isotope‐labeling experiments, mutational analyses, and in vitro biochemical assays support a model in which the malonyl unit loaded onto the module 2 ACPs is transferred to the loading ACP, where starter‐unit methylation is proposed to occur prior to chain initiation. Our study reveals unexpected biosynthetic logic and establishes a foundation for mechanistic studies and engineering of eukaryotic modular PKSs.
n67e637e15c0f: The stereochemical outcomes of pericyclic reactions provide direct insight into the geometry and directionality of concerted bond reorganization. Although torquoselectivity has emerged as a defining concept for electrocyclizations, an analogous principle for sigmatropic rearrangements on a single cyclic π system has remained unknown. We coin the term calderoselectivity for such an unreported stereoselective sigmatropic rearrangement. The switching process is reversible, proceeds to photostationary mixtures of homoannulene and iso‐homoannulene isomers, and furnishes diastereomeric products in a 56:44 ratio; combined chiral HPLC, NMR, ECD, and DFT studies assign the major directionality of acyl migration in pro‐R directionality. This study provides the first experimental realization of calderoselectivity and reveals a direct analogue in sigmatropic rearrangements to torquoselectivity with implications for both mechanistic physical organic chemistry and chiroptical switch design.
n98bb4c98dc6c: Achieving general asymmetric catalytic manifolds that accommodate broad substrate diversity remains a long‐standing and highly sought‐after goal in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an efficient cobalt‐catalyzed desymmetric hydrogenation of structurally diverse cyclic 1,2‐ and 1,3‐diacid anhydrides, enabling access to pharmaceutically relevant chiral γ‐ and δ‐lactones with broad substrate scope and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is readily scalable, as demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis of several representative products. Notably, this 3d‐metal catalytic platform represents a rare example that outperforms platinum‐group‐metal‐based counterparts in both generality and stereoselectivity. DFT studies identify a catalytically active d7 Co(II) dihydride complex with an outer‐sphere hydride transfer mechanism, wherein a relatively flexible chiral pocket underlies the broad substrate compatibility of this catalytic system.
n3c8cebfcd1c6: Strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) have emerged as versatile precursors for accessing highly reactive intermediates, enabling unconventional bond constructions through strain‐release pathways. Mechanistic investigations, including 31P NMR spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), and density functional theory (DFT) studies, provide insights into the plausible reaction pathway. The involvement of paramagnetic Co(II) species is consistent with the broad features observed in both EPR and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of the catalyst. In addition, four structurally distinct Co(II) complexes were synthesized, fully characterized by UV–Vis and Fourier‐transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and evaluated as catalysts for the transformation. The cationic nature of the Co(II) species was further confirmed by phosphine oxide trapping experiments and single‐crystal X‐ray crystallography.

nc4e865cc4d4b: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

n227f7a0289e3: Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic skyrmions hold great promise for next-generation high-density information storage, yet their low-dimensional behavior and controllable size remain challenging. Here, combining first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, we identify monolayer CrGaTe3, derived from the Ga2S3 structure, as a ferromagnetic half-metal and a robust platform for hosting topological spin textures. The system exhibits a substantial Dzyaloshinskii−Moriya interaction (DMI) of 2.36 m V, arising from intrinsic inversion asymmetry and strong spin−orbit coupling, alongside sizable Kitaev exchange and magnetic anisotropy. At zero field, the ground state adopts a Néel-type cycloid state, which evolves into stable skyrmion phases under moderate external magnetic fields. Remarkably, beyond field tuning, we find that biaxial strain not only modulates the skyrmion size but also induces skyrmion states under tensile conditions, offering an additional degree of freedom for topological phase engineering. Furthermore, our parameter-resolved analysis reveals that while DMI is pivotal for skyrmion nucleation, the Kitaev interaction and magnetic anisotropy collectively govern the size and density of the skyrmion lattice. These findings establish monolayer CrGaTe3 as a promising candidate for sub-10 nm spintronic devices and demonstrate that the synergy between intrinsic symmetry breaking and external stimuli provides a generalizable strategy for designing functional 2D magnets.
ne120cc753fcc: Directional charge transport is essential for efficient photocatalysis, yet carrier transfer in semiconductor nanocrystals is often random and limited by recombination. Here, we construct a ZnO vacancy homojunction composed of donor-type oxygen vacancies and acceptor-type zinc vacancies, establishing an intrinsic pathway for directional charge transfer. The resulting n−p junction introduces both an internal electric field and asymmetric lattice distortion, enabling phonon-assisted directional carrier transport under ultrasonication and leading to significantly enhanced photocatalytic performance in methylene blue degradation compared with conventional ZnO. Combined spectroscopic measurements, radical-trapping experiments, and density functional theory calculations reveal a phonon-enhanced directional charge-transfer mechanism. These findings provide a general strategy for regulating directional charge transport through lattice dynamics.

nb5bcd12a1be3: This review examines how the intrinsic properties of zinc metal influence its stability in aqueous electrolytes, highlighting multiscale correlations among morphology, microstructure, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior. n583e5ff018c5: Hybridization of light and excitons can change how materials absorb and emit light, but achieving this in the ultraviolet remains challenging. We show that a layered silver phenylthiolate forms hybrid light-matter states in simple mirror structures. This material expands the options for controlling ultraviolet light and provides a foundation for exploring future light sources and light-driven chemistry.
n294045e42341: Tunnel junctions are essential for various technologies ranging from classical microelectronics to quantum information and cryogenic electronics. Aluminum and its oxide (AlOx) have long dominated cryogenic and quantum tunnel junction applications for their excellent material quality and superconductivity. However, some applications require junctions to remain normal conducting, either as standalone components or integrated with superconducting circuitry. Magnetic fields, impurity doping, or proximity effects can suppress superconductivity, but often pose challenges for scalability and integration. Here, we present a CMOS-compatible normal conducting tunnel junction platform using TiW alloy electrodes and AlOx tunnel barriers, achieving high yield and uniformity through wafer-scale fabrication. As a cryogenic use-case, the wafers incorporate junction arrays designed for Coulomb blockade thermometry, confirming reliable normal conducting state performance down to 20 mK. These results demonstrate a scalable and integrable normal conducting junction technology, supporting its use in cryogenic, quantum, and nanoelectronic systems, including hybrid superconducting-normal metal circuits.
n424346185a23: The sodium–potassium pump (Na,K-ATPase) is an essential plasma-membrane transporter that consumes 20%–30% of cellular energy, and up to approximately 50% in the kidneys. Whether it assembles into defined oligomers in its native membrane has been debated for decades. Resolving this question demands imaging precision at molecular length scales. Here, we combine 3D MINFLUX nanoscopy with DNA-PAINT to map EGFP-tagged Na,K-ATPase α1 and β1 subunits in mammalian cells with 3–5 nm localization precision. We introduce two point-cloud analysis tools: a data-driven algorithm that assigns localizations to the apical or basal membrane, removing trans-membrane artifacts, and a sequential nearest-neighbor analysis that estimates oligomer stoichiometry without structural priors. Both subunits show preferential nearest-neighbor distances of approximately 7 nm, direct evidence of dimerization, and are further organized into nanoclusters of approximately 7 to 12 molecules. These results provide direct structural evidence of Na,K-ATPase self-assembly and a framework for quantifying membrane-protein clustering at single-molecule resolution.
nb46f2ff9db3b: Resistance threatens to render antibiotics ineffective, which is posing a threat to global public health. Innovative strategies against drug-resistant bacteria are urgent. The outer membrane protein BamA, a hollow barrel with a pore of 2–4 nm, is a unique and essential structure in Gram-negative bacteria. We prepared chiral 3 nm gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) targeting BamA, exhibiting enantiomer-dependent antibacterial activity against drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The AuNCs with right-handed wavelike lattices (D-AuNCs) preferentially interacted with BamA through the screw-in effect, creating pores in the cell wall and resulting in bacterial death. P. aeruginosa was still susceptible to D-AuNCs due to their excellent antibiofilm activity even after 20 successive passages. D-AuNCs were applied to P. aeruginosa-infected skin wounds in mice, achieving superior wound healing compared to levofloxacin. Our work documented that chiral nanoclusters targeting BamA can efficiently kill P. aeruginosa through the screw-in effect, providing an innovative strategy to combat Gram-negative bacteria.
nf79138ed7cc3: Hafnia-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for post-Moore memories, offering fast, low-power polarization switching and compatibility with the technological maturity of the hafnia platform. Yet nanometer-scale barrier thinning, while desirable for higher speed and energy efficiency, introduces a critical reliability bottleneck. Here, we develop an all-atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for reliable sub-2 nm hafnia FTJs through precise growth and low-roughness interface formation. The resulting devices combine sub-2-V operation with a high breakdown field of ∼12.1 MV/cm, while maintaining stable ferroelectric switching through 1010 cycles without breakdown. Further interface optimization extends the resistance-state endurance toward 1010 cycles, reconciling aggressive barrier scaling with reliable device operation. We further exploit 4-bit nonvolatile multilevel operation to demonstrate an in-memory computing simulation with 95.78% accuracy. By combining the advantages of scaling with high reliability, this work advances hafnia-based FTJs toward high-speed, energy-efficient, and robust memory applications.
n7f5f71f80ad5: Moiré superlattices provide a versatile route to engineering correlated electronic and topological states in van der Waals heterostructures, yet their use to organize structural polymorphism and phase-selective charge, magnetic, and superconducting states within a single two-dimensional material remains elusive. Here, we report modulated charge order and proximity superconductivity in an intrinsically moiré-patterned 1T/1T′ polymorphic network of monolayer VTe2 grown epitaxially on superconducting NbSe2. Scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy and first-principles calculations show that in situ annealing of twist-moiré VTe2/NbSe2 creates alternating 1T and 1T′ domains. The origin of the selective 1T-to-1T′ conversion is due to the moiré-induced anisotropic strain. This moiré-registered network hosts phase-specific short-range charge orders: 4 × 4 in 1T and 3 × 3 in 1T′. In the proximity-superconducting regime, spatially modulated in-gap bound states and suppressed coherence peaks reveal phase-dependent magnetic pair breaking. This work establishes intrinsically moiré-patterned polymorphism as a route to programmable two-dimensional quantum materials.
nc5565cf971f1: Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional-theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.
n20a5388c4996: Dielectric nanoparticles and microparticles show rich optical responses due to their electric and magnetic multipolar Mie modes and low losses. These optical resonances can be modified via the particle size, shape, and dielectric environment. Here we tune the infrared multipolar Mie resonances of dielectric polystyrene microspheres using the plasmonic phase-change material In3SbTe2 (IST). IST exhibits a phase change between a dielectric amorphous phase and a crystalline phase that is metallic in the infrared. We show that a reversibly switchable particle-on-mirror geometry can be created by locally switching the IST under the polystyrene microspheres. Measuring the light-scattering spectra of single polystyrene microspheres before and after crystallization and reamorphization, we observe huge shifts of the resonance wavelength, e.g., from 5.2 to 8.9 μm and back for 6 μm diameter spheres. Our work is a first step toward a controlled tuning of multipolar Mie modes of various particles using reprogrammable IST mirror structures.
n4ac446f0c4d8: Recent transport experiments reported a quantum spin Hall insulator phase in monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 gated away from charge neutrality. This phase is not predicted by band structure calculations and has been attributed to an electronic instability induced by strong correlations at a putative Van Hove singularity. Here, we investigate the electronic structure of exfoliated monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 using microfocus laser angle resolved photoemission. We find a strongly anisotropic band structure susceptible to density wave instabilities. Our data further reveal a saddle point singularity in the density of states. However, we find that the saddle point lies at a density for which linear transport experiments found no anomalies. Moreover, the quasiparticle line widths suggest weak electron correlations only. This points to a secondary role of Van Hove singularities and electron correlations in the transport phase diagram of monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4.
nd0cc627381fb: Noble metal nanoparticles with sharp edges and corners, such as triangles, tetrahedrons, bipyramids, etc., support superior plasmonic field enhancement for enhanced spectroscopy. However, high-yield synthesis of gold right bipyramids (Au RBPs) with sharp tips has remained limited because they have a single-twinned (ST) crystal structure whose growth pathway is hard to control. Here, we report the seed-mediated growth of Au RBPs using ST seeds, achieving a yield exceeding 70% by moderately increasing the size of these seeds. Au RBPs with sizes from 34 to 94 nm and controlled corner sharpness are achieved through the regulation of seed and bromide amounts. Uniform and strong near-field enhancement is generated in the Au RBPs-on-mirror configuration, which outperforms the well-established nanocube-on-mirror configuration in Raman enhancement. This work highlights the merits of ST seed-mediated growth for anisotropic nanocrystals and their potentials in plasmonic near-field focusing.
nbc1c1e21b62d: 3D nanohelices provide a direct route to control light–matter interactions with circular polarization at the nanoscale. Here, we report periodic arrays of W–C nanohelices fabricated by He+ focused-ion-beam-induced deposition (FIBID), combining direct-write 3D growth with high spatial resolution and W-rich deposits (∼65 at. % W). Two arrays with the same lateral geometry were fabricated while varying only the vertical pitch, corresponding to helical ratios HR ≈ 1 and HR ≈ 2. Transmittance measurements under circularly polarized light reveal a clear geometry-dependent response. The compact nanohelices (HR ≈ 1) show a larger circular-polarization-dependent transmission contrast (g ≈ 0.17, θ ≈ 2.35°), moderate transmittance (∼30–50%), and a sign inversion near 600 nm. The larger-pitch helices (HR ≈ 2) show higher transmittance (∼35–100%) with a weaker but stable response (g ≈ 0.13, θ ≈ 1.60°). Qualitative simulations reproduce the main spectral trends and support distinct optical responses of the two pitch geometries.
ne268ce2eb88a: The performance of electrocatalytic reactions has rapidly advanced in recent years, yet there remain numerous controversies in the underlying mechanistic understanding of these systems. This Perspective proposes a framework for rating the strength of evidence and cross-community validation of mechanistic claims for the most-studied electrocatalytic reactions.
nd63a2498399a: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. nf8033d4b8d5c: Direct biological conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is severely restricted by sluggish enzyme kinetics and inefficient intracellular carbon flux. Here, we address these catalytic bottlenecks by synergizing multimodal deep learning, mechanistic enzyme engineering, and synthetic organelle assembly. Using CASKP, a TransKP-guided candidate-prioritization framework that integrates sequence representations with a docking-derived scalar feature, we prioritized and experimentally identified a highly active β-carbonic anhydrase, PbCA, for improving intracellular CO2 supply. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of the R71A and V112A variants. The R71A–V112A variant displayed a specific activity of 26.1 U/mg and increased the intracellular 13C-labeled 3-phosphoglycerate ratio 4.9-fold. The simulations were consistent with a more hydrated active-site environment and a strengthened Tyr108-centered hydrogen-bond network. To overcome diffusion and thermodynamic limitations, these optimized biocatalysts were encapsulated into hybrid carboxysomes and coupled with an ATP-generating carboxykinase. 13C tracing confirmed incorporation of inorganic carbon into l-malate, with 95.2% of malate detected as 13C-labeled isotopologues. Subsequent promoter optimization yielded an l-malate titer of 22.7 g/L. This multiscale approach provides an integrated strategy for heterotrophic CO2-incorporating biocatalysis.
n161b17c373f1: Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction. Detailed computational and deuterium labelling experiments strongly suggest that the diastereoselective formation of this complex core involves a stepwise in situ generation of a short-lived, highly reactive azadiene. Moreover, the negative slope (ρ = –0.29) from the Hammett plot indicates the formation of a partial positive charge and that the electron-donating groups enhance the reaction rate. Notably, the concise tagging of drug molecules and downstream synthetic transformations with good yields and diastereoselectivity should highlight the potential applications of this methodology in drug discovery settings in medicinal chemistry.
nc1289907da8f: The discovery of doped spinel Co3O4 electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by the large catalyst design space and the high computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we establish a hierarchical interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that decouples electronic structure prediction from catalytic activity prediction. By starting with predicting the electronic descriptor (d-band center) from readily accessible structural descriptors and subsequently predicting adsorption energetics, the framework removes the need for expensive electronic structure DFT calculations during catalyst screening while preserving physical interpretability. A random forest model was trained on adsorption free energies of OH*, O*, and OOH* from 144 representative active sites and achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.21 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified surface energy, active site undercoordination, and the d-band center as the dominant descriptors governing adsorption energetics. To avoid additional DFT calculations of the d-band center during screening, a second ML model predicted it directly from structural and elemental descriptors with a test mean absolute error of 0.23 eV. The resulting framework enabled rapid evaluation of OER overpotentials across 252 active sites, while subsequent targeted DFT calculations identified Al-, Ca-, Fe-, and Mn-doped Co3O4 as promising candidates. Targeted DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements further validated the improved OER activity of Al- and Fe-doped Co3O4. This work establishes an interpretable and computationally efficient strategy for connecting structural descriptors, electronic properties, adsorption energetics, and experimentally measurable catalytic activity, thereby accelerating the discovery of high-performance spinel oxide catalysts.
n0deddbc45b3b: SktA from the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme NIES-2108 belongs to the versatile heme oxygenase-like domain-containing nonheme oxidase superfamily, whose natural function is to transform 5-bromotryptophan (5-Br-Trp) to 5-bromoskatole in an oxygen-dependent manner. As SktA is also capable of transforming tryptophan (Trp) to skatole, this enzyme represents a skatole synthase that operates under aerobic conditions. Here, the crystal structure of SktA and its complex with 5-Br-Trp and Trp are reported. The amino acids responsible for the substrate binding and the diiron cluster formation were revealed, and their roles in the catalytic reaction were examined via mutagenesis experiments. In addition, we found that SktA is capable of transforming 7-bromotryptophan and 5,7-dibromotryptophan to yield 7-bromoskatole and 5,7-dibromoskatole, respectively, and resolved the crystal structures of SktA in complex with these alternative substrates to elucidate the plasticity of the substrate-binding pocket. Finally, we show that combining SktA and regiospecific self-sufficient Trp halogenases in one-pot reaction systems efficiently transforms Trp to 5-bromo-7-iodo-skatole or 5-iodo-7-bromo-skatole. In summary, this study reveals the structural information, substrate scope, and potential applications in synthetic biology as a module to generate differentially halogenated skatoles of SktA.
n072860963a38: The selective hydrogenation of acetylene is a key reaction step for purification in ethylene production, as trace amounts of acetylene can poison downstream polymerization catalysts. Industrial acetylene hydrogenation is currently performed almost exclusively using palladium-based catalysts, motivating the search for more abundant alternatives. In this study, supported Fe-Ag catalysts with different Fe:Ag ratios were synthesized and evaluated for the selective hydrogenation of acetylene under industrially relevant front-end conditions. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, N2-physisorption, TPR, XPS, STEM-EDX, ICP-OES and XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs were used to investigate composition-dependent trends in adsorption energetics. Catalyst characterization revealed no evidence for the formation of an extended Fe-Ag alloy phase after air exposure. Instead, Fe- and Ag-rich domains were found to coexist in close nanoscale proximity providing a structural basis for considering possible local Fe-Ag interactions. Accordingly, the DFT calculations were performed on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs to investigate how the local chemical environment around adsorption sites affects the adsorption energetics of reaction intermediates. DFT calculations predict a gradual weakening of adsorption strength with increasing local Ag content, while the experimental catalyst series independently shows a decrease in ethane selectivity with increasing Ag loading. Under CO-containing front-end conditions, catalyst selectivity increased further due to competitive adsorption effects, while the influence of catalyst composition became less pronounced. The combined experimental and computational results indicate that changes in the local Fe-Ag environment influence adsorption energetics and may contribute to the composition-dependent catalytic behavior in acetylene hydrogenation. These findings provide design principles for the development of palladium-free hydrogenation catalysts based on earth-abundant metals.
n20e604698cd6: Perovskite quantum dot (PQD)-polymer composites are widely pursued for display devices due to their excellent film-forming capacity, low cost, and favorable process compatibility. However, interfacial incompatibility between PQDs and polymers from mismatched surface chemistry triggers PQD aggregation and severe photoluminescence quenching, hindering microdisplay applications. Herein, a dual-solvent screening strategy is demonstrated for I-184-initiated crosslinked PQD-PMMA photoresists to balance solubility and lead-ion coordination strength. Undesired lead-solvent intermediate formation and residual solvent accumulation are suppressed to homogenize PQD dispersion and preserve optical performance. The 20 μm green patterned film retains 93% of the initial photoluminescence quantum yield with no photoluminescence peak shift and a narrow full width at half-maximum of 16.6 nm. The PQD pattern presents sharp pixel edges, 7.10% critical dimension deviation, 97.1% replication rate, and intersection over union of 0.92. This solvent engineering enables the revitalization of conventional polymers and addresses bottlenecks in photolithographic patterning of PQD-polymer composites.
nea4417bc3a71: Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g−1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.
n3199a75e17b4: Renewable intermittency is widely regarded as a durability stressor in water electrolysis, yet its impact on competing degradation and recovery processes within the cell remains unclear. Here, we show that realistic intermittent operation redistributes catalyst recovery and membrane degradation in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). A Ni–Fe‐based AEMWE single‐cell was operated under high‐resolution, solar‐mimicking load profiles that reproduce day–night intermittency without external buffering. Electrochemical diagnostics reveal reversible changes in activation, Ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, indicating partial performance recovery during zero‐current intervals. In situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy attributes this behavior to reversible oxidation‐state and coordination changes of Ni and Fe, associated with the reversible formation and relaxation of amorphous (oxy)hydroxide surface layers. In contrast, hydrogen crossover measurements reveal increased crossover under low‐current operation, while post‐mortem membrane analyses provide independent evidence of membrane deterioration, identifying a critical system‐level limitation. These results show that intermittency does not uniformly mitigate degradation but redistributes it across cell components, enabling catalyst self‐restoration while exacerbating membrane vulnerability. This work establishes intermittency as a double‐edged operational parameter and provides a framework for designing materials and operating strategies for durable, battery‐free AEM water electrolysis.
n07b5cfb1ef94: Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li+ transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

n13aa0410aad5: Composite electrodes containing physical mixtures (“blends”) of multiple active materials have generated commercial interest for lithium battery applications due to the possibility of enhanced electrochemical performance, which are not fully characterised. This investigation uses mixtures of well-known LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 (LMFP) and LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC) materials as a model blend system to investigate rate- and composition-dependent effects on performance. A combination of electrochemical and operando techniques reveals that deviations in performance with respect to the linear combination of the component materials originate from uneven current distribution, leading to different effective rates between components and spontaneous lithium-ion redistribution, commonly termed the “buffer effect”. Results of experiments using a specially adapted three-electrode setup show that the effective rates of the components vary considerably depending on the cell state of charge, with much higher effective rates being reached than the applied cell rate. The same setup allows the direction of lithium redistribution to be visualised when the system relaxes following a current pulse, and this directionality also varies with cell state of charge. Electrochemical investigations and Raman spectra reveal that blending reduces chemical sensitivity to ambient storage conditions and leads to reduced degradation by forming a protective LMFP layer around the more reactive NMC particles. Operando data shows that the blend components evolve largely as expected when taking into account their specific effective rates, in line with the materials retaining their individual electrochemical properties. This study highlights the importance of considering relative windows of electrochemical activity when selecting blend components and paves the way for future optimisation of electrode blends for high rate lithium-ion batteries.
n588d850fb5ac: Hollow particles are designed to keep their cavities open, but a cavity can also be consumed as a structural resource. Thin-walled hollow α-V2O5 converts in aqueous ZnSO4 at 80 °C into a filled, hydrated, amorphous phase, Zn0.23(OH)0.46V2O5·1.0H2Oa charge-balanced composition from ICP-OES and TGA that assumes V5+ and hydroxide compensation of the zinc. Electron tomography shows the cavity disappearing as the particle grows from 246 to about 420 nm, with 6% of the vanadium lost to solution. The hollow shell takes up three times the water of commercial V2O5. Diffraction and vibrational spectroscopy show loss of long-range order and a 13 Å hydrated gallery; V K-edge XANES shows the vanadyl V5+ site of α-V2O5 surviving. Zn K-edge EXAFS gives Zn−O = 2.03 Å with a six-coordinate model in every state. The transformed phase has a smaller slow-process impedance and a larger initial utilization than crystalline controls, and DFT + U models of a reduced amorphous network with the same Zn content stabilize ionized Zn in O-rich disordered sites. Cycling changes the vanadium site, which does not recover on charge, and buries the surface under zinc hydroxy-sulfate. Internal free volume directs hydration-induced amorphization; stabilizing the product is a separate problem.
n2c8a76c446ba: Controlling matter with nanoscale spatial selectivity is a key hurdle for plasmonic applications such as nanophotonics, sensing, and catalysis. Plasmon-assisted nanolithography has recently emerged as a powerful strategy to address this challenge by exploiting the highly confined electromagnetic fields and hot carriers generated during plasmon excitation to confine organic or inorganic layers at the nanoscale. Among the surface chemistries compatible with this approach, aryl diazonium salts are particularly attractive because their reduction produces highly reactive aryl radicals that form robust covalent bonds with metallic surfaces under mild conditions. Under light excitation, the plasmon-induced reduction of aryl diazonium salts enables the rapid and site-selective grafting of functional organic layers confined to plasmonic hot spots. The resulting functional films provide versatile chemical handles for further modification. However, to date, the use of plasmon-mediated diazonium grafting as a spatially controlled primer layer to direct the site-selective immobilization of colloidal nanoparticles remains unexplored. We address this gap by using lithographic gold nanodisc arrays as optically programmable templates. Under plasmon excitation, these nanostructures enable the formation of positively charged nanoscale anchoring domains at plasmonic hot spots, derived from diazonium salts bearing amine groups. These localized charged domains can then guide the spatial organization of negatively charged colloidal gold nanoparticles. The geometrical parameters of the plasmonic arrays, including nanodisc diameter and interparticle spacing, were carefully tuned to access different plasmon excitation regimes around the 633 nm laser wavelength, enabling blue-shifted, near-resonant, and red-shifted conditions, and expanding the variety of achievable hybrid patterns. Complementary characterization using SEM, UV−vis spectroscopy, and FDTD simulations demonstrates that this approach provides a straightforward and versatile strategy to direct the assembly of colloidal nanoparticles on lithographic nanostructures via optical excitation.
ne30347718e7f: The lithium–sulfur battery is one of the most promising next-generation battery technologies for high-energy applications due to its high gravimetric energy density of 2567 Wh kg −1 .
