nb3ee2b4edd11: Combining nanoimprint lithography with functional nanoparticles brings two design levers into the same platform: the geometry of a metasurface and the optical properties of its material. This review shows how these two levels of control are combined across the metallic, dielectric, light-emitting, and hybrid systems, providing a scalable framework for flat optics with tunable and multifunctional responses.
n76afa301dd70: Turning CO2 into useful hydrocarbons usually means broad product mixtures and high-pressure reactors since conventional catalysts offer little control over chain length and require high pressures to form C–C bonds. Here, we provide a generalizable route to C–C selectivity control through the formation of distinct catalytic interfaces via exsolution engineering. Hence, product choice is set by parent material design rather than reaction condition requirements. Beyond performance, this establishes a design strategy connecting interface structure to product selectivity.
n79573cb3e99b: Neutrophil elastase (NE) is a key driver of neutrophil-mediated inflammation and tissue injury across diverse diseases. However, current NE inhibitors often lack sufficient target selectivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in suppressing inflammation and promoting organ repair. Here, we report that single-atom V doping programs atomically precise Au15 clusters into a relatively selective and potent NE inhibitor. The ultrasmall size of Au14V1 enables selective accommodation within the NE binding pocket. Multiscale mechanistic analyses demonstrated that Au14V1 inhibits NE through a reversible mixed inhibition mechanism with an inhibition rate of 87.6%, while exhibiting minimal activity toward closely related proteases, highlighting its preferential inhibition toward NE. In LPS- and CLP-induced systemic inflammatory injury models, Au14V1 reduced NE activity and NET formation, alleviated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, mitigated tissue injury, and improved survival. These findings establish a single-atom engineering strategy for developing selective enzyme modulators and precise therapy targeting the NE-NETosis axis.
n435231550824: Solid-state batteries promise improved safety and energy density, but their performance is governed by buried interfaces where ion transport, chemical reactions, and stress evolution are strongly coupled. Resolving these processes during operation remains challenging. Here, we present an operando spectroscopic strategy that jointly analyzes broadband optical backgrounds and characteristic electrolyte Raman features within a single measurement. Asymmetric least-squares baseline (ALS) estimation extracts broadband optical contrast associated with lithium distribution, while Raman band intensities and peak positions provide complementary information on interfacial chemistry and local stress estimates. This capability provides a unified optical framework for visualizing structural, chemical, and mechanical evolution at battery interfaces and offers a broadly applicable route to interrogate buried interphases in diverse electrochemical systems. More generally, by enabling real-time, multimodal insight into interfacial dynamics, this method advances efforts toward safer, longer-lasting, and more predictable energy-storage technologies.
n26c45ed45f87: Quantum relaxometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is an easy-to-use technique that detects magnetic noise by measuring the longitudinal relaxation of NV centers. It is favored in chemical and biological applications due to the robustness against imperfect spin control. By tuning the energy level, NV relaxometry can detect magnetic noise generated by other spins and obtain magnetic resonance spectra through cross relaxation. However, the spectral resolution is greatly limited by the inhomogeneous broadening of NV centers, especially for nanodiamond-based relaxometry. Here we demonstrate a hole-burning technique to remove the inhomogeneous broadening. We utilize a weak pump field to deplete specific NV centers during the relaxation measurement, which contribute a reverse signal in the cross-relaxation spectra with a much narrower line width. Our method retains the convenience and sensitivity of NV relaxometry, opening up new avenues for high-resolution magnetic resonance spectroscopy in complex scenarios.
n5603464e0d39: Understanding the behavior of ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) materials under high electric fields is essential for advancing next-generation power electronics. While electrical degradation processes have been widely studied, the influence of high electric fields on thermal transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first experimental measurements of changing thermal resistance under an applied electric field in a UWBG material, using single-crystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as a model system. We observe substantial, and sometimes reversible, changes in thermal resistance during prolonged exposure to a strong DC electric field. These results reveal a previously unrecognized sensitivity of phonon transport to high-field electrical stressing and show that thermal resistance can serve as a sensitive probe of electric-field-induced material evolution that remains undetected by conventional electrical characterization. More broadly, this work establishes thermal transport measurements as a powerful tool for investigating high-field phenomena in UWBG materials.
n8b2f3dbeb9c2: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as versatile light emitters for a broad range of applications, where they are typically operated in the dilute- or single-exciton regime. Scintillation under ionizing radiation, however, represents a fundamentally different mode of operation. A single absorbed X-ray photon can generate a large number of electron–hole pairs within a nanoscale interaction volume, driving individual NCs into extreme exciton occupancies. In this Perspective, we argue that scintillation in NCs should be viewed as an extreme exciton-density problem and show how simple occupancy considerations impose fundamental limits on achievable scintillation light yield. We further outline two complementary strategies to overcome these limitations: (i) engineering NCs for enhanced multiexciton radiative yields and (ii) designing NC composites that redistribute deposited energy across larger NC populations. We anticipate that exciton-density engineering will provide a unifying framework for designing the next generation of NC scintillators.
n7cfb30048626: High-quality freestanding GaN membranes are fabricated using a single-reactor-run metal–organic chemical vapor deposition. The procedure begins with the growth of a single-crystalline GaN template, followed by the formation of a 20 nm-thick full-coverage disordered BN layer on GaN, which remains stable under high-temperature GaN growth conditions. We introduce a heat-treatment step to generate numerous nanoscale apertures in the BN layer, enabling aperture-mediated homoepitaxial regrowth. Meanwhile, the BN layer suppresses strong epitaxial bonding, where the regrown GaN is mechanically detachable from the GaN template. In addition, multiple disordered BN interlayer formations are established, enabling epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Moreover, GaN Schottky diodes are fabricated to demonstrate minimal material degradation through the aperture-mediated lift-off process, enhanced device performance with BN-assisted ELOG, and the feasibility of ultralight wearable UV detectors. This approach eliminates the need for ex situ transfer or substrate-specific lift-off processes, providing a simple and thermally robust platform for manufacturing freestanding wide-bandgap semiconductor membranes.
n2f2ba9d1b780: Chemical recycling of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is limited by harsh depolymerization conditions and the low-value utilization of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). Herein, we report a “one-stone-three-birds” strategy that couples PET depolymerization, TPA utilization, and EG upgrading for total-product upcycling. Waste PET serves as an in situ slow-release terephthalate precursor, whose gradual, incomplete hydrolysis dynamically perturbs metal–ligand stoichiometry, generating missing-linker defects and oxygen-deficient, coordinatively unsaturated environments in a bimetallic MOF (NiCo-PET). Relative to NiCo-MOF prepared from commercial TPA, NiCo-PET exhibits 67% higher spin concentration and enhanced EG oxidation, requiring only 1.29 V vs RHE at 50 mA cm–2 while achieving 93.6% formate Faradaic efficiency and stable operation for 24 h at 2 A cm–2. Operando analysis confirms favorable reconstruction into high-valence oxyhydroxides. This work valorizes both PET-derived products without additional purification or isolation, offering a sustainable route to total-product plastic upcycling.
nb76f9d573f9f: The recent experimental realization of goldene, an atomically thin form of gold, provides a unique platform to investigate collective electronic excitations in the ultimate two-dimensional (2D) limit of a noble metal. Here we reveal that goldene is a plasmonic material whose collective response is strongly shaped by its reduced dimensionality and underlying electronic structure. Using first-principles many-body calculations, we show that monolayer goldene supports intrinsic acoustic and optical plasmons arising from the interplay between the low-energy metallic response and dispersive s and more localized d states. As the number of layers increases, interlayer coupling and enhanced screening progressively quench this directional anisotropy, driving the system toward the isotropic response of bulk gold. In finite nanostructures, the plasmonic resonance follows the size scaling characteristic of confined 2D metallic systems. Our results establish the foundations of goldene plasmonics, with technological implications for nanophotonic sensing, photocatalysis, and atomically thin optoelectronic devices.
ne2e166c8d352: Photocatalysis can expand the reactivity of transition-metal catalysts by enabling new reaction pathways under mild conditions. Now, a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system is developed that combines photochemical, redox and Lewis acid catalysis for the modular assembly of diverse benzylamines directly from aryl aldehydes, alkanes and nitriles under mild conditions.
n4ca2915ffb0e: The chemical assembly of oligosaccharides hinges on the reactivity of the anomeric site. In 1980, the introduction of a Lewis acid-catalysed method for the activation of anomeric imidates marked an important step in carbohydrate synthesis, becoming the foundation of complex synthetic strategies to this day.
n1fb4d4eb8f97: Particle density effects in heterogeneous catalysis are elusive because particle density usually changes simultaneously with particle size. Here we show that the size and shape of Ru particles, formed by reducing epitaxial rutile-RuO2 structures supported on rutile TiO2 with closely matched lattices, remain constant with 16-fold change in density. Using the Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts, we demonstrate that, in polyolefin hydrogenolysis, high Ru particle density enhances the multiparticle adsorption of polymer chains, leading to lower coverage of adsorbed H (*H), and thus higher selectivity towards CH4, with desorption being the rate-determining step. Short-chain alkanes accommodatable on a single Ru particle do not show such particle density effects, and C−H bond activation is the rate-determining step. This work provides a strategy to deconvolute particle density effects from size and shape effects in high-temperature thermal catalysis, while revealing how the large size of polymer substrates impacts catalytic mechanisms. Particle density effects in catalysis are difficult to disentangle from other factors. Now the synthesis of Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts with constant size and shape at varying densities enables the elucidation of particle density effects in polyolefin hydrogenolysis.

ncf50885b0f99: Stereochemistry greatly influences polymer structure and assembly, yet its use in controlling polymer network topology remains underexplored. Now, homochiral self-sorting is used to suppress primary-loop formation in end-linked polymer networks, offering a strategy for controlling network topology.

neac2914fc100: An in situ-generated iminophosphorane enables C–O, C–N, C–S and C–C bond formation from primary and secondary alcohols. The process overcomes the pronucleophile pKa limitation associated with traditional Mitsunobu reactions while simplifying purification and avoiding the requirement for explosive azodicarboxylate reagents.
nd7dac975691d: Selective water oxidation in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions remains a major challenge for photocatalytic systems. BiVO4 is one of the most efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for water oxidation and exhibits high activity in Fe3+-mediated water-oxidation systems. However, although accumulated Fe2+ can introduce competing oxidation pathways under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ redox conditions, effective strategies for suppressing these processes and maintaining selective water oxidation remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a surface-engineering strategy that overcomes this limitation in BiVO4. Systematic investigation revealed that the poor activity of BiVO4 under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions arises not only from catalyst degradation but also from competition with Fe2+ oxidation reactions. Surface modification of BiVO4 with W species, originally intended to improve acid durability, not only suppressed catalyst dissolution but also mitigated Fe2+-related performance losses, resulting in a marked enhancement of photocatalytic water oxidation. The activity enhancement correlated with highly dispersed surface W species localized near the outermost region of BiVO4. Notably, the highest activity was obtained before or near the onset of detectable WO3 crystallization, suggesting that the surface state of W species in this temperature range is more closely associated with the enhanced activity than crystalline WO3 domains under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions. The optimized photocatalyst maintained efficient water oxidation while suppressing Fe2+-related performance losses, achieving an apparent quantum yield of 63% under Fe3+-based conditions and approximately 30% even under strongly acidic and concentrated Fe(ClO4)3 conditions relevant to hybrid water splitting. The optimized photocatalyst maintained selective water oxidation even as Fe2+ accumulated to approximately 100 mM, enabling nearly quantitative Fe3+-to-Fe2+ conversion under strongly acidic conditions. When incorporated into a photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid system, the enhanced photocatalytic activity was directly translated into approximately 1.5-fold higher water-splitting performance than that of the benchmark H-Fe-Cs-WO3 system. These findings demonstrate that selective water oxidation can be maintained even in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions through appropriate photocatalyst surface engineering, providing a useful strategy for photocatalysts operating in redox-mediated reaction environments, including photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid water-splitting systems.
n48bb8642c5df: Impurities exert profound effects on electrocatalytic measurements and interpretations. Trace levels of contaminants introduced through electrolytes, electrodes, gases, or cell materials routinely generate false activity signals, accelerate degradation, and alter product selectivity. This review categorizes impurity effects by functional impact, including misleading activity, compromised stability, and shifted selectivity, and offers strategies to recognize, isolate, and mitigate these influences. We argue that reliable and reproducible electrocatalytic data require an impurity-aware approach, integrating both experimental protocols and systems engineering. By intentional design, impurities can be transformed from hidden liabilities into controlled variables, ensuring that reported advances in electrocatalysis reflect intrinsic catalyst properties and translate into durable energy technologies.
n2cca62a8ea7d: Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.
nc274a3c3909c: Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm−2. The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.
ne866c971ba96: Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton-coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high-rate CO2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic-and-gap-confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)-modified Bi (Bi-PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near-surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen-bond environment, while slow-growth proton-transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton-delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to *OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential-dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate-related pathway response. Bi-PDMS-30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm− 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface-deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO2-to-formate electrosynthesis.
n5fd394f9c8b3: Non‐radiative energy loss originating from triplet exciton generation and intrinsic energetic disorder severely restricts the efficiency breakthrough of organic solar cells (OSCs). To address this dual bottleneck, herein, two benzodiimide‐based solid additives with distinct photophysical properties, namely fluorescent HPmDI and room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) BrPmDI, are developed to simultaneously suppress triplet exciton dissipation and mitigate energetic disorder for high‐efficiency OSCs. Both additives construct favorable intermolecular interactions with the D18 donor and L8‐BO acceptor, optimizing active layer molecular packing, enhancing film crystallinity, and reducing Urbach energy to alleviate intrinsic energetic disorder. Benefiting from the unique long‐lived triplet exciton characteristics of organic RTP BrPmDI, an efficient Dexter energy transfer (DET) pathway is additionally enabled, which effectively inhibits non‐radiative decay channels, including intersystem crossing and charge recombination‐induced triplet exciton formation. Consequently, the optimized D18:L8‐BO‐based OSCs modified with BrPmDI achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.52% with a low non‐radiative energy loss of 0.217 eV, far outperforming the pristine device (19.01% and 0.226 eV) and HPmDI‐modified device (19.70% and 0.219 eV). This work reveals the dual regulatory mechanism of organic RTP additives on triplet exciton dynamics and energetic disorder, providing a facile strategy for the design of high‐efficiency additive materials toward low‐energy‐loss and high‐performance OSCs.
naed4de931479: Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm2. The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.
nd0b2394516c7: The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru-based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen-containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement-pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine-doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru3ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru3ON6Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru3ClNC delivers a high alkaline half-wave potential (E 1/2) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc-air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru3ON6Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non-planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d-band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate-determining step of Ru3NC and OH* desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept for Ru-based catalysts to overcome the thermodynamic limitations and thereby improve the ORR activity.
nccc3776d3695: Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy-level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active-layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S-SMA and AS-SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8-BO with a weaker electron-withdrawing 2-(3-ethyl-4-oxothiazolidin-2-ylidene)malononitrile (CN-Rh) unit. This terminal-group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8-BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid-to-solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S-SMA, asymmetric AS-SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8-BO:AS-SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open-circuit voltage (V OC) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal-group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy-level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high-performance ternary organic solar cells.
n38366de562d5: Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long-term stability. Herein, (1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual-site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH3 +) and electron-rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI6]4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl-modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non-radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy-level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp-heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80.52% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85°C and 800 h at 85°C, 85% relative humidity, respectively. This work demonstrates a practical molecular-interaction strategy for efficient and durable inverted PSCs based on multifunctional, dual-site passivation and crystallization regulation.
n8a1ae8896119: Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li5.4PS4.4Cl0.8Br0.8) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm−2 and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm−2). For electrochemical performance, HICCM exhibits fast ion transport kinetics and electrical insulation, allowing the ASSB configured as FeS2//HICCM//LiF‐Li to achieve an energy density of 416.5 Wh kg−1 at a high loading of 3.4 mAh cm−2. This work demonstrates that by combining HICCM with a stable interface design, ASSBs can achieve longevity and high cell‐level energy density.
n7eff699c0df1: The ZIF-8/Ag2SeO3 heterostructure was designed to combine the adsorption capacity and porous architecture of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) with the multifunctional response of Ag2SeO3 (ASO), seeking synergistic interactions that could yield a material with enhanced, complementary functionalities. We report the synthesis and interfacial evolution of ZIF-8/ASO heterostructures and the in situ formation of metallic Ag nanoparticles (NPs) under electron irradiation. X-ray diffraction confirms the coexistence of cubic ZIF-8 (I43m) and monoclinic ASO (P21/c) phases, with a microstructure consisting of ZIF-8 NPs uniformly anchored on ASO microrods in intimate interfacial contact. Time-resolved electron microscopy directly captures the nucleation and growth of Ag NPs on the ZIF-8 surface during electron irradiation, as confirmed by HRTEM-SAED and elemental maps, indicating spatially confined cubic Ag NPs with exposed (111) and (200) planes. Photoluminescence measurements show pronounced emission quenching and spectral redistribution, indicating modified optoelectronic behavior following heterostructure formation. First-principles calculations identify the ZIF-8/ASO(010) interface as a favorable configuration, characterized by strong interfacial interaction and significant charge redistribution. These results are consistent with the experimentally observed localized formation of Ag NPs and suggest that interfacial electronic interactions contribute to Ag+ reduction. Overall, the ZIF-8/ASO heterostructure provides an electron-responsive platform for localized Ag NP formation and interfacial optoelectronic modulation, offering insights into electron-beam-induced processes in ZIF-8-based heterostructures.
nf0eefd93a180: No single scalar captures disorder in high-entropy and compositionally complex fluorites. This Perspective evaluates compositional and structural descriptors by physical meaning, reference frame, covariance, and transferability. Pairwise cation mismatch contains the same information as size variance, whereas host-referenced misfit adds a reference-dependent mean-radius offset. Analysis of twenty-four published compositions from three systematic datasets illustrates the limits of configurational entropy and size variance as independent descriptors of phase formation and transport. With equal Hf, Zr, and Ce fractions, changing the host reference reverses misfit rankings and alters the host-offset term up to 78-fold. In twelve dual-phase zirconates and mixed zirconate-hafnates, the nominal rA/rB ratio correlates with phase fraction but describes neither coexisting phase, whereas measured phase compositions give non-overlapping fluorite and pyrochlore values, distinguishing descriptor limitations from inappropriate evaluation frames. Structural observables are assessed by specificity, reproducibility, and relevance. Together, these criteria and the compositional analysis define a framework that distinguishes compositional inputs, multiplicity and crystal-chemical mismatch, from their structural realization. Its purpose is to test descriptor relevance and limits rather than predict untested compositions.
n1a277cd90f77: Template-guided crystal-chemical design offers a route to oxonitridosilicates, but transfer of an oxide topology requires compatible cation coordination and charge balance. Here, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of the 6-ring host La2Ca3[Si4N4O8], designed by considering [SiN]+ for [AlO]+ substitution in the Ca3[Al2O6] template together with aliovalent La3+/Ca2+ substitution. The idealized structural description contains isolated rings of corner-sharing [SiN2O2] tetrahedra and partially occupied or vacant cation sites. The nominal substitution scheme, 3Ca2+ → 2La3+ + VCa, provides a charge-balanced crystal-chemical rationale for the cation deficiency. Theoretical calculations reveal that the aliovalent substitution induces cation vacancies accompanied by local charge redistribution and coordination rearrangement, which may alleviate the lattice strain arising from the cation-size mismatch. Eu2+ activation produces broadband orange emission centered near 600 nm, with a reported photoluminescence quantum yield of 29.3%. The phosphor was further applied to a white LED by combining it with multiple phosphors. This work illustrates how cation composition and occupancy can be considered alongside the topology in template-guided exploratory synthesis.
n8efab071cfee: Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.
nfecb34b17aec: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnet-based heterostructures provide a vital platform for manipulating magnetic ground states and hosting complex spin textures. The topological Hall effect (THE) is a powerful tool for probing these textures in such systems. However, achieving a sizable THE in 2D vdW ferromagnets remains challenging due to the absence of broken inversion symmetry and sufficiently strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we report an emergent giant topological Hall resistivity of 6.9 μΩ·cm at 10 K by interfacing the 2D ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) with the topological insulator BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS). Systematic temperature- and thickness-dependent studies suggest the origin of this pronounced signal to be the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI). Furthermore, temperature-field mapping reveals the coexistence of two distinct phases that we identify as having opposite topological charge. Our results establish these vdW ferromagnet/topological insulator heterostructures as a robust platform for enhanced interfacial THE, opening new avenues for high-efficiency topological spintronics.
n70f75f0de887: Controlling doping density in correlated quantum materials offers a route to tuning their electronic states, but chemical doping can introduce disorder and limits dynamic control. Here, we demonstrate optically tunable electron doping of the layered Mott insulator α-RuCl3 through photoinduced interlayer charge transfer in MoS2/α-RuCl3 heterostructures. Photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements support electron transfer to α-RuCl3, leaving holes in MoS2. The layer-separated carrier population persists for more than 100 ps with an estimated doping density tunable through the excitation fluence. Selective excitation of α-RuCl3 further reveals hole transfer to MoS2. Transient absorption microscopy yields an early time effective hole diffusion coefficient of approximately 100 cm2 s–1 in the heterostructure, supporting a predominantly unbound carrier population. These results establish photoinduced charge transfer as a means of dynamically controlling carrier doping in α-RuCl3, providing a route toward optical manipulation of correlated electronic states.
n72d73a2d9bd9: Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.
n13fe6e555fad: Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) crystals have been widely used in photonic and electronic devices owing to their outstanding intrinsic optoelectronic properties. However, fabricating hundreds-of-micrometer-thick LiNbO3 wafers remains dominated by diamond wire sawing, which causes substantial material loss. Although ultrafast laser processing offers a promising alternative, the intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice, spontaneous polarization, and anisotropic photothermal response of LiNbO3 severely hinder high-quality laser cutting. Here, a thermal dissipation-guided vector scanning technology is proposed to realize ultrafast laser slicing of LiNbO3 crystals for the first time. By tailoring the scanning direction according to the anisotropic thermal dissipation, we achieve crystal exfoliation with an ultrathin subsurface damage layer of 10 μm and an exceptionally high-quality separation surface. The results establish vector scanning technology as an innovative route for high-quality femtosecond laser processing and low-damage separation of anisotropic crystals.
naad0a4dfa2c3: Redox processes in oxides are central to materials synthesis and functionality, but their control is often hindered by surface instabilities. Using ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we show that a nominally 1 nm-thick SrTiO3 (STO) cap markedly enhances the surface stability of La0.05Sr0.95FeO2.5-δ (LSFO) thin films during H2 reduction by suppressing the formation of a secondary metallic Fe0 phase. Kinetic analysis indicates that the STO cap reduces the effective Fe0 formation rates by more than 6-fold at both 250 and 350 °C. These findings highlight ultrathin capping layers as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxide surfaces during redox.
nab3528a186d8: Ru single-atom catalysts are promising for NH3 oxidation but still suffer from poor activity and N2 selectivity, mainly owing to the poisoning of the isolated Ru active sites by the over-strong NH3 adsorption. Herein, we fabricated an asymmetric Ru-W atomic pair anchored on CeO2 (Ru1–W1/Ce) exhibiting considerable low-temperature activity (∼90% at 200 °C), high N2 selectivity (∼85% at 350 °C), and notable stability (∼500 h at 200 °C), surpassing most of the previously reported catalysts for NH3 oxidation. Systematic experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrated that a strong d-f orbital interaction between Ru and W atoms was revealed, inducing the smooth electron transfer from W to Ru atoms. The electron-rich Ru single atom not only weakened NH3 adsorption strength to alleviate NH3 poisoning but also reduced the energy barrier of the rate-determining step of NH3 activation. Besides, isolated W atoms coordinated with active Ru species, leading to a decrease in Ru–O–Ce coordination number. This could suppress the activation of O2 and thereby the deep oxidation of NH3. Accordingly, the reaction mechanism over this asymmetric Ru–W catalyst changed from the initial i-SCR to an imide-like pathway, accounting for its considerable catalytic performance. This work provided a paradigm for advanced Ru-based catalysts enabling both high activity and high N2 selectivity in NH3 oxidation.
n8d31f1b33dd3: A fundamental challenge in harnessing substrate promiscuity for industrial biocatalysis lies in reconciling broad substrate acceptance with high catalytic specificity. Although promiscuous enzymes provide attractive starting points for accessing non-natural transformations, their native active-site architectures and conformational dynamics often lack the precision required for efficient and selective conversion of desired unnatural substrates. Thus, systematically decoding and reprogramming the interplay between promiscuity and specificity remains a key obstacle toward versatile biocatalysts. Here, we address this challenge by integrating virtual screening, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations into a unified engineering framework. A tropinone reductase from Cochlearia officinalis (CoTR) was identified as a broadly promiscuous scaffold. By converting complex enzyme–substrate interaction dynamics into quantifiable and actionable design principles, we predict and validate key residues that govern substrate promiscuity. Guided by these insights, distinct CoTR variants were engineered for three representative substrates. The optimized variants—CoTR‑8M, CoTR‑5M‑1, and CoTR‑5M‑2—exhibited 7.0‑ to 16.3‑fold higher catalytic efficiencies than wild-type CoTR toward their respective target substrates and supported substrate loadings of up to 50 or 100 g L–1 while maintaining >99% ee. This work not only delivers scalable routes to three industrially valuable chiral alcohols but also provides mechanistic insights into the synergistic modulation of promiscuity and specificity. This study demonstrates a general strategy for translating intricate molecular-recognition features into rational design principles, thereby facilitating the development of tailored biocatalysts for non-native substrates.
nf27e7805d3f1: Tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites are essential narrow-bandgap absorbers for two-terminal perovskite–perovskite tandem solar cells, yet their extreme air sensitivity has confined stability studies indoors, leaving real-world durability unexplored. Here, we substantially lower this barrier using industrially relevant, lamination-based encapsulation that enables, to our knowledge, the first outdoor demonstration of Sn–Pb devices. Combining polyisobutylene edge sealing with polyolefin elastomer encapsulation, we demonstrate that the lamination process is highly compatible with Sn–Pb devices, causing negligible performance loss while preserving optoelectronic quality during short-term air exposure. Under package-oriented accelerated aging, epoxy-based encapsulation fails rapidly, whereas the lamination-based package remains intact. Outdoors under tandem-relevant filtered illumination, lamination-encapsulated devices retain ∼80% of initial efficiency after 12 days, while epoxy-encapsulated devices lose all output within 6 days. By adapting manufacturable module packaging to Sn–Pb devices, this work enables their realistic field evaluation, marks a critical step toward deployable all-perovskite tandems, and strengthens confidence in their commercial viability.
nd3dab6df8142: The rational design of heterogeneous catalysts for selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains challenging. Here, inspired by the diiron center of methane monooxygenase, we synthesized two enzyme-mimicking Fe...
n0b0bf9068817: Methane decomposition is a promising route for CO x -free hydrogen production, but the rapid deactivation of Ni-based catalysts remains a major challenge. This study investigates the effects of SiO 2 support crystallinity...
nc9d2b13c1bf1: A Pd-catalyzed atroposelective ring-opening coupling of cyclic tetracoordinate borons affords tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes while retaining the boron moiety. The reaction integrates boron and silicon within a configurationally stable chiral framework and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance. More broadly, this strategy expands the reactivity of tetracoordinate borons beyond conventional migration pathways and provides a distinct approach to tetrasubstituted axially chiral molecules.
nbdfc15a2b905: Complex, dynamically heterogeneous environments such as lipid membranes, electrocatalytic interfaces, soft polymer matrices, crowded biological media, and phase-separated assemblies are characterized by spatially distinct microenvironments, multiscale structural dynamics, and short-range interactions. Microscopic interactions are poorly captured by bulk descriptors. In this article, we review how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy and related vibrational methods provide direct access to these complex molecular landscapes by resolving inhomogeneous ensembles, picosecond environmental fluctuations, and exchange between local states. When combined with vibrational probes and modern molecular simulation, these spectroscopic observables reveal how local interactions, such as electrostatics, hydrogen bonding (H-bonding), and ion pairing and aggregation generate microscopic heterogeneity and govern multiscale dynamics. We organize discussions around representative classes of complex environments, including hydration and electrostatics in lipid membranes, molecular environments and dynamics in biomolecular condensates, confinement and crowding in self-assembled and interfacial systems, including electrochemical interfaces, polymers/gels and soft matter, electrolytes and ion-specific effects, and aqueous cosolvent mixtures relevant to solvation and cryopreservation. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements in vibrational probe design, multidimensional spectroscopy, and molecular simulation are expected to enable more quantitative and predictive analyses of heterogeneous molecular environments across chemistry, materials science, and biology.
na4dfb7e46889: Light-conversion materials hold considerable promise for addressing global energy and environmental challenges, with applications spanning photocatalysis, optical wireless communication (OWC), and high-energy photon detection and imaging.
n9e6e84bce412: This review presents the recently developed non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals for various key energy conversion reactions.
n9f228178d0ca: We illustrate the physical pictures, performance evaluation criteria, and microscopic mechanisms of persistent luminescence, and further highlight the application-oriented multicolor design principles of inorganic persistent luminescent materials.
n538e88554fe1: Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of ligand engineering on the stability and electrocatalytic performance of Cu NCs during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that both NCs possess a highly similar S@Cu14 core architecture stabilized by twelve positionally different methyl-substituted thiolate and six triphenylphosphine ligands, allowing direct evaluation of ligand effects without changes in core structure. Despite their structural similarity, positional variation of the methyl substituent generated distinct electronic environments, intermolecular interactions, and crystal-packing arrangements. The relatively electron-deficient Cu environment in S@Cu14-3MBT resulted in superior CO2RR performance, achieving highly selective Faradaic efficiencies of 52% for formate and 18% for CO at −1.4 V vs. RHE with suppressed hydrogen evolution, whereas S@Cu14-4MBT exhibited lower selectivity and stability. Theoretical calculations, together with comparison with structurally analogous metal NCs, reveal that precise modulation of the electronic configuration plays a critical role in promoting formate selectivity. Post-catalytic analyses revealed degradation and ligand loss in S@Cu14-4MBT, whereas S@Cu14-3MBT remained structurally intact. These results highlight ligand engineering and anion templation as key strategies for tuning the stability and CO2RR performance of atomically precise metal NCs.
ndcfcdee41585: Boron carbide (B4C) is a ceramic of considerable interest due to its high hardness, elevated melting point, excellent thermal stability, low density, and chemical inertness. Decaborane-functionalized preceramic polymers (PCPs) prepared from ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) are excellent single-source precursors of B4C, but the mechanistic details for the decomposition and ceramic conversion during pyrolysis have been overlooked, preventing advances in redesigning preceramic polymers that have high char yields and desirable chemical compositions. Herein, we reveal insights into the role of decaborane during the polymer-to-ceramic transition of poly(cyclooctenyldecaborane) (PCD) to boron carbide. ROMP of the cyclooctenyldecaborane monomer enabled controllable molecular weight and produced a series of polymers with molecular weights up to 35 kg/mol and dispersities (D̵) in the range of 1.3-1.6. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry (TGA-IR and TGA-MS, respectively) of PCD revealed the evolution of small hydrocarbon species following an initial release of hydrogen at low decomposition temperatures around 250 °C, which is in stark contrast to the decomposition profile of unfunctionalized poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD) that transitions into volatile hydrocarbon species at approximately 450 °C. ReaxFF molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the experimental findings that hydrogen release from decaborane initiates the polymer-to-ceramic conversion. MD simulations indicate that the release of H2 results in the exothermic formation of boron clusters, which promote the thermal decomposition of the hydrocarbon polymer backbone. These findings indicate that decaborane plays an active role in the polymer-to-ceramic conversion rather than serving solely as a boron source, providing mechanistic insight that will enable the rational design of next-generation PCPs with enhanced ceramic yields and tunable compositions.
na86b19af39ba: Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mechanistic study have made diameter, growth direction, crystal phase, and axial composition into design parameters. For oxides, carbides, and chalcogenides, including emerging van der Waals materials, which we refer to collectively as non-conventional nanowires, one-dimensional structures have been reported in abundance, but comparable deterministic control has not been achieved despite their predicted functional properties and broad application potential. This review examines where and why the two groups diverge. We survey and categorize the literature on VLS and VLS-related synthesis of non-conventional nanowires, following the sequence of the growth process itself, namely, precursor creation and delivery, seed particle formation and evolution, and nucleation and growth of one-dimensional structures. Each step is compared against the group IV and III−V baseline to locate shared behavior and genuine differences. From this comparison, we identify seed particles, spanning the choice of seed material, the chemical composition of the seed during and after growth, and its dynamics, as the principal bottleneck restricting deterministic synthesis, with precursor creation and delivery acting as an upstream constraint that narrows the accessible seed design space. We discuss potential solutions, including new precursor chemistries, improved reactor designs, and in situ characterization of growth, that would deepen the mechanistic understanding of nanowires already demonstrated by VLS and extend seeded growth to emerging quantum and functional materials, ultimately paving the way for deterministic synthesis and integration of complex one-dimensional nanomaterials.
nf16a976f4b1f: Transforming plastic waste into valuable organosulfur chemicals, this work presents a solar-driven, continuous-flow photoelectrochemical platform. Centered on a bismuth single-atom molecular catalyst with precision-engineered local coordination, the system uniquely enables selective carbon-sulfur bond formation via a controlled interface microenvironment, establishing an efficient and bias-free route for sustainable plastic upcycling.
n28c1f913945c: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacity through transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen loss and structural reconstruction cause large first-cycle irreversibility. Here, we examine Li1.2Ni0.13Co0.13Mn0.54O2 at four states of the first charge–discharge cycle using atomic-resolution STEM, nanobeam electron diffraction with electron pair distribution function (NBED-ePDF) analysis, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), image simulations, and DFT. Up to 4.3 V, Li extraction is dominated by interlayer sites and the slab framework remains largely preserved. At 4.8 V, changes in Li/O contrast and O K-edge features coincide with a short ePDF correlation near 1.57 Å. Seeded DFT relaxations stabilize short O–O pairs near vacancies in the transition-metal slab. After discharge, incomplete spectroscopic recovery accompanies near-surface reconstruction and oxygen-related contrast changes consistent with oxygen depletion. Together, the results implicate Li depletion from the transition-metal slab in high-voltage oxygen rearrangement and suggest that controlling this site occupancy may improve oxygen-redox reversibility.
na5d68d45a0e0: Spin-based multivalued logic offers compelling advantages for next-generation computing. Thus far, only binary systems─exploiting domain walls, skyrmions, and vortices─have been realized. These schemes rely solely on the manipulation of the chirality or polarity of magnetic carriers, precluding the implementation of multivalued logic operations. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of ternary logic operations using a one-dimensional vortex chain, via the co-manipulation of both the chirality and polarity of magnetic vortices. We show that ternary AND logic functionality can be achieved via dipole-mediated chirality modulation and domain-wall-assisted polarity reversal in the vortex chain, with operation times on the nanosecond scale. Our work establishes a viable and scalable platform for multivalue magnetic logic, thereby paving the way for next-generation spintronic logic applications.
n22cbeb01c9c5: The modular assembly of protein nanoparticles has enabled the design of highly immunogenic and cross-protective viral vaccines. However, downstream translation is hampered by labor-intensive purification methods that lack the resolution needed to efficiently sort molecular assemblies. Here, we report an affinity tag-free nanoparticle sorting platform that exploits electro-viscoelastic microfluidic (EVM) migration for the high-fidelity, continuous-flow isolation of virus-like particle (VLP) assemblies. This migration mechanism can overcome Brownian fluctuations, which are typically dominant on the nanoscale, confining the target assemblies to central streamlines for selective collection. In a single pass, the system segregates 40 nm VLPs from 6 nm excess antigen monomers, increasing the VLP purity by 20.2%. A sacrificial electrode outlet directs undesired electrohydrodynamic effects to the waste, preserving the VLP-rich product stream. Our results offer an alternative downstream framework for the rapid purification and quality control of complex bionanomaterials, establishing a scalable pathway for precision nanomedicine processing.
n065c87963aaa: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need an external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co3Sn2S2), outperforming conventional semiconductor InAs. Furthermore, we propose material design recipes. Strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors a large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive material discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.
n26648c93b2ae: Fe(Te,Se) is a prototypical iron-based superconductor and a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity. However, growing high-quality ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) films on magnetic substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate epitaxial growth of monolayer-to-trilayer Fe(Te,Se) on the van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) via direct selenization of the substrate, without external Fe or Te deposition. Combined scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) characterizations reveal large-area, atomically flat tetragonal films with well-defined rotational alignment to the hexagonal FGT lattice. Cross-sectional STEM-EDS confirms Se incorporation and interfacial elemental redistribution. Thickness-dependent spectroscopy reveals evolving electronic structures and progressive decoupling from the ferromagnetic substrate. Measurements across lateral monolayer–bilayer interfaces further uncover asymmetric band bending and charge redistribution driven by Fermi-level equilibration. These findings establish substrate-mediated selenization as a versatile route to ultrathin superconducting heterostructures and magnetic quantum platforms.
n56005a3d50fa: Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic–ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color–direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.
nb7480ae71ab3: The simultaneous presence of multiple (quasi)particles is a challenge for ultrafast imaging. Measurement at a few intensities disentangles the single- and multi-particle spatiotemporal dynamics.
n57d7a7ca2c44: Targeted lipid nanoparticles reprogram TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages in ascitic fluid into chimeric antigen receptor macrophage cells, providing an in situ cell engineering strategy that alters the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumour cell elimination in rodent models.
nc85174faba53: A lipid nanoparticle formulation degrades an immunosuppressive receptor on tumour-associated macrophages through its lipids alone, while its messenger RNA cargo reprograms these cells in situ into anti-tumour chimeric antigen receptor macrophages, reshaping the immune microenvironment of malignant ascites in gastrointestinal cancer.
n827896aac4b0: Intensity-cycling spatiotemporal microscopy separates single-particle and multi-particle transport, enabling imaging of charge mobility, exciton interactions, and correlated many-body states in van der Waals semiconductors, including Mott transitions.
nebfe0bce8874: In this issue, we focus on the synthesis of porous liquids, fluids that combine the permanent, well-defined pores of porous solids with the flow and processability of liquids.
nd92aa2b1bf86: A low-symmetry eight-crossing knot was assembled from a binuclear rhodium unit and a semi-rigid ligand featuring a conformationally flexible bithiophene spacer and π-stacking azaindole donors. Size-directed assembly of the same system also afforded a five-crossing knot.
na765e5d6c329: Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) synthases share similar architectures, yet produce distinct PUFAs. Recent mechanistic studies reveal how substrate recognition by dehydratase, ketoacyl-acyl carrier protein synthase, and acyltransferase domains controls double bond formation, chain elongation, and release, highlighting chemical principles underlying PUFA structural diversity and product distributions. These insights inform rational engineering.
n763a13f11dfa: Carboxylic acids are attractive precursors to boronic esters, but redox requirements of decarboxylation are poorly matched to diboron reagents. Juliá-Hernández and coworkers report an iron ligand-to-metal charge transfer strategy activating coordinated carboxylates through photoinduced electron transfer. Free acids, from acetic acid to drug molecules, give boronic esters in one step.
n5eec01b94f9e: Following Wender’s pioneering studies, the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids has undergone a remarkable renaissance over the past decade. This resurgence has been driven by the emergence of unified synthetic platforms, radical-based coupling strategies, and strategic cycloaddition reactions. These developments have not only enabled the concise and scalable synthesis of flagship molecules such as phorbol, prostratin, resiniferatoxin, and pedrolide, but also provided chemical probes for exploring their promising biological activities. This review summarizes the total syntheses of these four molecules, with a particular emphasis on the strategic innovations and emerging trends across the different synthetic routes developed for each, aiming to provide timely guidance for future synthetic efforts.
nb4b7f87fda11: The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. In this work, we applied a sequence similarity network (SSN)-guided approach to identify cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) with O-dealkylation activity within the growing sequence diversity found in public databases. We investigated six CYPs, three of which exhibited significant activity toward structurally diverse ethers bearing methyl, ethyl, propyl, or allyl groups. While P450ThcB and P450Terp enabled the deprotection of aromatic and aliphatic primary and secondary ethers, P450Sca2-mut complemented the substrate scope by effectively deprotecting sterically demanding tertiary ethers. In particular, P450ThcB and P450Terp exhibited high regioselectivity, preferentially cleaving phenolic over benzylic ethers. Furthermore, P450ThcB enabled the regioselective deprotection of veratryl alcohol. Preparative scale reactions of three substrates yielded up to 74% of the isolated and (regioselectively) cleaved alcohol product. Together, these findings substantially expand the enzymatic toolbox for the selective removal of alkyl PGs and highlight the suitability of SSN-guided database mining approaches for the identification of biocatalysts with the desired function.
n2918c82c5505: Precise control of catalytic active centers and their interfacial strain is central to accelerating heterogeneous reactions, yet systematic regulation of strain at subnanometer metal–oxide interfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a class of 3d metal/heavy rare-earth metal oxide oligoatomic catalysts, in which finite metal ensembles are anchored on oxide surfaces to form nuclearity-dependent, strain-coupled metal–oxide interfaces. By varying the metal species, oxide support, and, most critically, the average number of metal atoms in each ensemble, we show that interfacial strain can be systematically tuned across diverse 3d metal/oxide combinations. In the Ni/Y2O3 system, an optimal nuclearity range of approximately 4–6 Ni atoms maximizes both compressive Ni–Ni strain and tensile Y–O distortion, creating a strained Ni–O–Y interface that balances CH4 oxidation and CO2 reduction during dry reforming of CH4. The resulting catalyst sustains near-equilibrium CH4 and CO2 conversion for over 1200 h without coke accumulation or detectable active-site collapse and remains stable under natural-gas reforming conditions. Theory and in situ spectroscopy reveal that nuclearity-regulated interfacial strain redirects carbon-containing intermediates away from deep dehydrogenation and toward continuous oxidation, thereby establishing a dynamic carbon balance. These findings position oligoatomic catalysts within the structural regime situated between single-/dual-atom and nanoparticle catalysts and highlight ensemble nuclearity as a tunable parameter for modulating interfacial strain in demanding catalytic reactions.
nc3c7a5169471: The active site of the classical Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 (CZA) catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation remains elusive as its surface structures undergo dynamic change under reaction conditions. Here, we combine neural network interatomic potential molecular dynamics simulations and grand-canonical density functional theory calculations to investigate the evolution of the representative CuZn alloy and inverse ZnO/Cu surface phases, and we consistently observe drastic restructuring under hydrogenation conditions, forming fragmented Zn-based ensembles at Cu support. Among the pathways examined, CO2 hydrogenation on these ensembles preferentially proceeds through the HCOO pathway, with different ensemble compositions being thermodynamically favored for the intermediates formed at different reaction stages. Importantly, these Zn-based ensembles are highly dynamic on Cu, allowing the inert HCOO within the ensembles to access highly active Cu/Zn interfacial sites, thereby making its hydrogenation kinetically accessible. The formation of ensembles and their dynamic behavior may be related to a suitable Cu–Zn interaction, which stabilizes Zn on Cu while preserving its mobility. Overall, these findings identify dynamic Zn-based ensembles as potential operando active sites in the Cu–Zn component of CZA and show that catalyst restructuring not only changes surface morphology but also couples directly to the reaction mechanism.
nba9787d58afa: Cyclopropane fatty acid synthase (CFAS) enzymes catalyze the formation of cyclopropane rings within bacterial membrane lipids, a transformation implicated in membrane homeostasis, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of biochemical investigation, the molecular determinants governing CFAS regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, chain specificity, and substrate scope remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate how enzyme orthology, lipid structure, and membrane environment shape CFAS selectivity. Comparative analysis of CFAS orthologues from Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Streptococcus thermophilus reveals that the extent of mono- versus di-cyclopropanation, regioselectivity, and stereochemical outcome are not conserved properties but diverge substantially across the enzyme family. A simple two-carbon variation in phospholipid acyl chain length (C16 versus C18) reverses the absolute configuration of the cyclopropane product, revealing an unrecognized structural determinant of stereochemical outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CFAS catalysis extends beyond native phospholipids to synthetic pseudo-phospholipids bearing non-phosphate anionic headgroups and to fatty acids embedded within lipid vesicles, substantially expanding the substrate scope of this enzyme family. Together, these findings provide insight into the molecular basis of CFAS selectivity, advance the understanding of bacterial lipid cyclopropanation, and broaden the synthetic potential of these enzymes for the stereoselective preparation of non-natural cyclopropyl lipids.
na44d8c686724: Hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising piezoelectric materials, yet the use of high-quality single crystals in flexible ultrasound sensing remains largely unexplored. Here, we report intrinsically noncentrosymmetric chiral two-dimensional perovskite single crystals, (S/R-NEA)2PbBr4, that exhibit strong piezoelectricity arising from chirality-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced lattice polarizability. By integrating these crystals into a polymer matrix, we realize flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators delivering high output (∼8 V) under ultrasonic excitation. The devices enable reliable detection and clear resolution of 50 kHz ultrasound signals, along with excellent mechanical durability and environmental stability. This work establishes a single-crystal strategy for flexible piezoelectric devices and highlights chiral 2D perovskites as a compelling platform for high-sensitivity ultrasound detection and energy harvesting.
n484feb4ee38e: Bicarbonate electrolysis offers a direct route for converting captured CO2 into high-value chemicals without energy-intensive CO2 regeneration and compression. However, multiphase transport within liquid-fed porous cathodes remains poorly understood. We found carbon paper and carbon cloth yielded drastically different performance, and further analysis revealed gas retention, i.e., localized and temporary entrapment of internally generated gas within the pore network, as an important transport limitation. Flow pulse and recovery experiments under galvanostatic operations showed largely reversible performance losses, while operando X-ray imaging directly visualized gas retention. Gas retention intensifies with denser electrodes, lower catholyte flow rates, and higher current densities. Guided by these observations, an interdigitated flow field was employed to enhance through-plane convection and gas removal, increasing the maximum formate partial current density to 304 mA cm–2 and enabling 120 h of stable operation. These findings establish gas management as a critical design criterion for bicarbonate electrolyzers.
