n8da6a96460eb: Solid-state batteries pairing lithium metal anodes with inorganic solid electrolytes promise a step change in energy density, but during charging at practical rates lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte, short-circuiting the cell. Our current understanding of dendrite propagation derives largely from symmetric Li−Li cells with millimetre-thick electrolyte pellets, whereas practical cells will employ solid electrolyte separators less than 100 μm in thickness. In this work, we use in situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography to show that dendrites in a thin Li6PS5Cl separator, which generally propagate from the lithium anode to the cathode, can be made to propagate laterally by the cathode. Volume contraction of the NMC cathode during charge places the thin separator under lateral compressive stress, deflecting dendritic cracks to propagate laterally (parallel to the electrodes) rather than transversely (across the separator). The result is that the cell resists short circuit even after passing 3 mA h cm−2 capacity at a rate of 3 mA cm−2. Replacing NMC with zero-volume-change pre-lithiated Li4Ti5O12 removes this compressive stress, and the cell rapidly fails by transverse cracking. Chemomechanical modelling rationalises both behaviours, with cathode volume change emerging as a design parameter that can suppress or accelerate failure, with direct implications for cathode selection and cathode/separator interface engineering in practical solid-state batteries.
n2216855ec587: Rare-earth hybrid nitrate double perovskites (REHNDPs) have recently emerged as an intriguing subclass of functional materials, combining structural diversity with rich intrinsic optoelectronic, magnetic, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Although notable progress has been made in three-dimensional (3D) and 2D REHNDPs, 1D counterparts have yet to be discovered. Herein, by introducing the bulky organic cation 1-adamantyltrimethylammonium (TMAA+), we report a family of 1D REHNDPs with the general formula (TMAA)2LnCs(NO3)6 (Ln = La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Sm3+, and Eu3+). Distinct from the μ2-κ3(O,O′,O″) mode characteristic of 2D and 3D REHNDPs, the bridging NO3− ligands adopt a μ2-κ3(O,O′) coordination mode in 1D counterparts. Strikingly, (TMAA)2SmCs(NO3)6 possesses a step-like high-temperature dielectric switch at 431.7 K. (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 shows brilliant photoluminescence with a quantum yield of 65.46% and a lifetime of 5.21 ms. The X-ray detector based on (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 demonstrates high X-ray sensitivity of 560 μC Gyair−1 cm−2 and a low detection limit of 153 nGyair s−1 under a bias of 25 V. This work bridges a critical dimensional gap and significantly expands the structural and functional portfolio of the REHNDPs.
n986a0e2cfb8f: Rechargeable Zn−air batteries (ZABs) have attracted considerable attention as promising energy storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density and environmental compatibility. However, their practical application is hindered by the sluggish ORR/OER kinetics at the air cathode. This study investigates low Pt-modified Fe- and Ni-doped hexagonal perovskites (BaTi0.8M0.2O3−δ, M = Fe and Ni) as robust bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, focusing on the modulation of their participating metal and electronic structures. Structural analysis confirms the formation of stable hexagonal phases, while Pt deposition induces distinct electronic reconstruction depending on the dopant species. With a higher ORR catalytic behavior than the Pt/BTO-Ni catalyst, the Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst demonstrates remarkable bifunctionality driven through dopant-dependent surface interaction modulation by Pt with optimized surface/lattice oxygen distribution. Notably, in full-cell ZAB tests, the optimized Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst achieved a comparable peak power density of 124.8 mW cm−2 with a remarkably low round-trip efficiency decay rate of 0.41%/h under stable operation for 60 h, compared to the commercial IrO2 + Pt/C benchmark (125.2 mW cm−2 and 1.39%/h) even at lower Pt content. These findings highlight the critical role of Pt2+-mediated interfacial interactions in governing catalytic durability, providing a rational strategy for designing highly durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for next-generation energy storage systems.
n774c976db3fb: The number of possible crystal structures vastly exceeds the number realized among thermodynamically stable inorganic materials, suggesting that experimentally accessible structure space is organized around a limited set of preferred structural frameworks. Analysis of 23,160 structures on the thermodynamic convex hull identifies 6820 distinct structural frameworks, of which 2382 recur across multiple chemically distinct materials and are therefore classified as structural prototypes. Within a filtered dataset, metallic systems exhibit particularly strong structural recurrence, with 6270 materials grouped into 535 frameworks and 327 prototypes, while 5557 ionic compounds occupy 1704 frameworks and 696 prototypes. These results demonstrate that stable inorganic materials naturally coalesce into recurrent structural prototypes and do not require any a priori definition through manual curation. The resulting recurrence-based catalog also provides an empirical measure of framework prevalence, enabling the relative likelihood of structural frameworks in future materials to be estimated from their recurrence among known compounds.
n70e42d8e642f: To understand the nature of multicenter interactions in periodic solids and their associated materials (transport) properties, we investigate and quantify multicenter bonding on the basis of the underlying wave function, namely by a combination of quantum-chemical tools for a diverse series of functional materials. First, we probe all compounds by projected force constants based on plane-wave phonon calculations, followed by a projection from plane waves onto a local-orbital framework and its thorough quantum-chemical analysis. While the three-center crystal orbital bond index is used to quantify multicenter bonding between atomic orbitals, the linear combination of fragment orbitals provides a molecular-orbital lens. Eventually, both approaches are fused into the molecular orbital contribution index that directly attributes the contributions of a single molecular orbital to a multicenter bond.
n185e0085945e: SAPO-34 is an excellent catalyst for methanol-to-olefins (MTO) reaction. Simultaneously alleviating the diffusion limitations and optimizing the acidity of SAPO-34 is extremely challenging. Herein, a three-dimensional hollow square array SAPO-34 (SAPO-34-HSA) with a sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon was synthesized in a simple way. The role of triethylamine (TEA) switches between the etchant and structure-directing agent according to the reaction temperature. In the heating stage, the seed with high silicon content was etched by TEA; during the crystallization process, TEA guides the epitaxial growth of raw materials on the seed crystal, forming a hollow core−shell structure; after crystallization, the shell was partly leached to form a hollow square array structure. The sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon is conducive to promoting olefin cycling in the hydrocarbon pool mechanism and significantly improving the selectivity of ethylene. So the SAPO-34-HSA catalyst exhibits 70%−400% longer catalytic lifetime in MTO reaction compared with the seed under different reaction conditions.
na923104221b9: Amid escalating energy demand and severe environmental effects, green hydrogen production via water electrolysis has emerged as a cornerstone technology. Conventional alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) generally suffers from low hydrogen purity and current density, while proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) relies on high-cost noble-metal catalysts and harsh acidic conditions. To mitigate these limitations, researchers have turned to anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) as a promising alternative, offering an intermediate pathway that pairs the non-noble metal-based catalysts of AWE with the high purity and compact architecture of PEMWE. However, AEMWE technology remains comparatively underdeveloped. Herein, we have summarized transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs) as a low-cost catalyst platform for AEMWE devices. The current review focuses on a comparative analysis across the chalcogen family and discusses how variations in their physicochemical properties influence the overall catalytic performance of anion exchange membrane devices. In addition, the underlying mechanisms of AEMWE, the membrane-electrode assembly, and cell configurations have also been explored in detail. The review critically examines the intrinsic activity of the transition metal chalcogenide-based catalyst layer against device-level performance metrics and further highlights emerging future directions. The review aims to provide a clear roadmap toward the development of highly efficient and commercially competitive AEMWE systems for next-generation green hydrogen production.
n09b6b63883fd: Seawater electrolysis for green hydrogen production urgently demands high-performance electrocatalysts that simultaneously deliver fast reaction kinetics with robust chloride ion (Cl−) resistance. Herein, we report an ultralow Pt-loaded (<1 wt %) Pt/Fe2O3 catalyst rich in Pt−Fe atomic pairs synthesized via a photoreduction synthetic strategy. Photogenerated electrons drive the selective reduction of Pt precursors at low-coordinate Fe3+ sites on α-Fe2O3 (012) facets, constructing Pt−Fe pair interfaces that enable directional electron transfer from Fe-dz2 to Pt-dz2 orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes the Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption, weakens the intrinsic affinity of active sites toward Cl−, and accelerates water dissociation. The as-synthesized catalyst achieves ultralow overpotentials of 9 and 51 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm−2 respectively in alkaline simulated seawater, with a slight potential decay of only 0.08 mV h−1 over 1000 h of continuous operation, outperforming most state-of-the-art electrocatalysts. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer, it delivers a low cell voltage of 2.0 V at 500 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm−2.
n15bde14f6444: Introducing homologous acceptors into PM6:L8-BO tailors aggregation kinetics during film formation, extending the crystal-growth window to ∼100 ms and reducing excited-state energetic disorder, enabling ternary devices to achieve efficiencies >20%.
n884ee42aebac: All-solid-state sodium batteries (ASSBs) offer high energy density and safety, but conventional solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers suffer from low efficiency and severe side reactions. This work proposes a novel strategy based on a borate-enriched SEI that effectively suppresses side reactions and enables dendrite-free Na plating/stripping, providing valuable mechanistic insights and a feasible pathway toward high-performance ASSBs.
n9818df8af9b2: Binuclear metalloenzymes remain underexplored for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Now binuclear copper enzymes, particularly a Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase, are used as a catalytic platform for stereoselective radical azidation, bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions, expanding metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems.
n77d71dfc8d8a: Aptamers have generally been understood as nucleic acids that recognize a specific ligand. Now it has been shown that secondary aptamers can recognize the ligand-bound conformation of a primary aptamer, enabling recognition of molecules that lack multiple binding sites for sandwich assays. n56772df9d20d: Predictive human-relevant model systems are outlined in a Review by integrating engineered materials and microenvironments, human tissue and organ models, computational approaches, and closed-loop strategies. n280d12d67af2: Low-energy photoredox catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for promoting mild, chemoselective transformations through radical intermediates. While various red-light-absorbing photocatalysts, including molecular porphyrins, have enabled diverse synthetic transformations, these processes operate almost exclusively under homogeneous conditions in organic solvents. Here, we demonstrate that integrating a photoactive porphyrin as the organic linker in a metal–organic framework (MOF) affords an air- and aqueous-compatible, heterogeneous photoredox catalyst. Using porphyrinic zirconium MOFs such as PCN-224, we enable a range of bond-forming reactions, including Giese additions, C(sp2)–H alkylations, C(sp2)–H arylations, formal cycloadditions, and radical polymerizations under mild red-light irradiation. While preserving the intrinsic reactivity of molecular porphyrins, heterogenization provides practical advantages including efficient photocatalysis independent of catalyst solubility and reaction medium, structural tunability, high turnover number (TON), and easy catalyst recovery and reuse. Mechanistic studies indicate that radical generation occurs predominantly within the framework pores.
n7a5744b31780: Nickel oxyhydroxide (NiO(OH)) is the catalytically active species during electrochemical alcohol oxidation at nickel electrodes. Herein, we demonstrate that the adopted phase structure of NiO(OH) (β- and γ-NiO(OH)) can dramatically influence the catalytic properties of nickel electrodes. We show that β-NiO(OH) oxidizes aliphatic alcohols preferentially to aldehydes and that carboxylates are formed at γ-NiO(OH). By combining the effect of the NiO(OH) phase with reagent effects (electrolyte pH, alcohol concentration, and trace amounts of Fe), we achieve aldehyde formation with ∼90% selectivity or carboxylate formation with ∼85% selectivity. Furthermore, we perform an in situ Raman spectroelectrochemical study to elucidate the reaction conditions that favor the formation of β- and γ-NiO(OH) phases, respectively. Freshly deposited nickel electrodes form γ-NiO(OH) phases upon oxidation, whereas an electrochemical conditioning protocol can be employed to transform γ- to β-NiO(OH). Finally, we show that the efficiency of this transformation depends on the precise reaction conditions and the precursor used. Hence, we showcase that the exact surface structure of the phase formed in situ on top of transition metal (oxides) affects the product distribution of electrochemical reactions. Moreover, we highlight how the “history” of these catalysts affects their performance via an intricate interplay among the reaction environment, pre-treatment, and surface structure.
n0c7be96d28db: Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.
n1519c51a3729: Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. Building on a comprehensive understanding of charge-transfer and transport mechanisms, we found that potentiodynamic modulation enables selective capture of uranium species using a uvanite electrode. By allowing competing cations to deintercalate at lower potentials and preventing proton deintercalation, UO3 dissolution is inhibited, achieving a high UO3 recovery capacity of 515 mg/g at 10 times the competing cation concentration. The new electrochemistry of the uvanite electrode helps develop cost-effective, sustainable battery electrodes for critical ion extraction from water.
n6f24301ad204: The development of an efficient and reversible hydrogen storage and transport system is crucial for a sustainable hydrogen economy. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a potential solution due to their high hydrogen storage density and ease of transport, but conventional thermal approaches for the hydrogenation and dehydrogenation of LOHCs remain heavily reliant on harsh operating conditions. Here, we demonstrate a plasmonic photocatalysis approach for toluene hydrogenation to methylcyclohexane and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation to toluene under substantially milder conditions. We observe changes in reaction orders and substantial reductions in activation barriers by 0.34 and 1.11 eV for toluene hydrogenation and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation, respectively, as compared to thermocatalysis due to the role of hot carriers. Both reactions exhibit high activity, stability (>70 h), and excellent selectivity (>95%), offering a sustainable pathway for on-demand hydrogen storage and release.
ne5813f627e66: Ethylene oligomerization is pivotal in the petrochemical industry to produce olefins and polymers. In this work, we conduct density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate ethylene oligomerization catalyzed by a...

ndd2015aa7900: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.
nbfcf0cc0b1a8: Atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) combines increasingly sustainable polymerization processes with precise macromolecular engineering to create materials with extended lifetimes, improved circularity, and advanced functions for energy technologies. This perspective discusses recent advances and future opportunities for greener, scalable ATRP processes and the design of high-performance polymeric materials that integrate functionality and sustainability.
n865b42e4fa17: Combining quantitative live-cell imaging, electrophysiology, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we establish a mechanism by which CPP additives drive the direct translocation of proteins across cellular membranes through membrane potential-dependent water pores. This framework provides a basis for intracellular delivery of protein therapeutics to expand access to intracellular, previously undruggable targets.
neb9bf52fa7d4: Zhou et al. develop an oxygen-independent photocatalytic strategy that converts glutathione to its oxidized form while generating hydrogen in cancer cells, thereby disrupting the intracellular redox balance. This catalytic redox remodeling induces ferroptosis and antitumor immune activation, establishing an oxygen-independent mode of photocatalytic cancer therapy.
n44a90ab06014: A battery stability prediction model covering LIBs, SIBs, and ZIBs has been proposed. The electron-ion transport mismatch is identified as a key determinant of battery stability. A linear correlation between the battery stability and the electron-ion transport mismatch has been revealed: the closer the transport rates of electrons and ions, the more stable the battery. The battery stability could be predicted rapidly from the electron-ion mismatch, with no need for time-consuming long-term cycling.
n660917528ddd: Hollandite-type α-MnO2 is a prototypical tunnel-structured host for rechargeable batteries, yet the atomic-scale mechanisms governing multivalent-ion insertion remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal how guest-ion species dictate electrochemical reaction pathways through distinct occupation modes within the one-dimensional tunnels of α-MnO2. By combining electrochemical analyses, atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we directly correlate reaction kinetics with guest-ion configurations and the accompanying structural and electronic responses of the host framework. Electrochemical measurements reveal substantial diffusion-controlled contributions for both Na+ and Mg2+, whereas Ca2+ exhibits predominantly surface-controlled behavior. Atomic-resolution imaging demonstrates that, despite their comparable macroscopic kinetic contributions, Na+ and Mg2+ exhibit distinctly different microscopic insertion modes: Na+ homogeneously occupies the tunnel-center sites throughout the particles, whereas Mg2+ occupies both tunnel-center and off-center sites, with pronounced near-surface enrichment accompanied by local tunnel distortion. In contrast, the Ca2+ reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, with no clearly detectable occupation of the internal tunnel sites. Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals spatially heterogeneous Mn reduction, with more pronounced reduction near the structurally less constrained particle surface. These results establish a direct relationship between guest-ion occupation modes, electrochemical reaction pathways, and the resulting structural evolution, providing an atomic-scale design principle for engineering tunnel-type host materials for multivalent-ion insertion.
n16c95d1fb977: Multielectron redox in Li2FeS2 involves both cation and anion contributions. While prior studies have investigated this process experimentally, questions remain about the Fe-to-S redox transition, persulfide formation, and incomplete delithiation. Here, we revisit the electrochemistry of Li2FeS2 using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Initial Fe oxidation is shown to proceed via increased Fe−S covalency driven by ligand-to-metal rehybridization. This accounts for only ∼60% of the Fe capacity, after which phase separation into Li1.5FeS2 and Li0.5FeS2 induces a shift to S oxidation. We identify nonbonding S 3p orbitals as redox-active centers. To track their evolution during delithiation, we isolate the localized nonbonding states by subtracting the bonding and antibonding contributions from the total electronic densities of states. These orbitals undergo S-to-Fe rehybridization, progressive oxidation, and eventual reorganization into persulfide bonds. At high states of charge, Li vacancies enable FeS4 tilting and facilitate S−S bond formation. Further delithiation beyond Li0.5FeS2 would require unstable S hole formation or conversion to pyrite FeS2, explaining why it is challenging to fully delithiate this material. These findings offer insights into the interplay of cation and anion redox, guiding the design of high-capacity sulfide cathodes.
n251675295ae6: Diabetic wound healing is severely impaired by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and especially disrupted bioelectrical signaling. The HGP@D hydrogel had strong mechanical property, great tissue adhesive strength, glucose/pH dual-responsive drug release behavior, alongside robust broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, and potent intracellular antioxidation. The HGP@D hydrogel restored local bioelectrical signaling and created an anti-inflammatory wound microenvironment, thereby modulating the behaviors of skin-resident cells involved in diabetic wound repair, including fibroblast migration, macrophage M2-like polarization, and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic analyses suggested that the HGP@D hydrogel promoted infected diabetic wound healing through two Ca2+-associated regulatory axes: the Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NF-κB axis for inflammatory regulation and the Ca2+/PI3K/Akt/mTOR/HIF-1α/VEGF axis for angiogenesis and tissue reconstruction. Overall, HGP@D provides a promising clinical therapeutic strategy for the advanced healing of diabetic wounds and other non-healing wounds by integrating glucose/pH-responsive microenvironment regulation with bioelectrical modulation.

n9f6bd4657bfc: Sulfur can remain physically present in a lithium-sulfur pouch cell while becoming electrochemically inaccessible. This perspective links local electrolyte availability and the transport of lithium ions and soluble sulfur species to sulfur conversion, lithium-metal degradation, and variations in pressure and temperature. n1d15a7c24786: While additives direct Zn electrocrystallization and impact battery performance, the mechanism remains disputed. nfc7a5077d98f: Nucleophilic substitution is a fundamental strategy for alkyl functionalization, traditionally relying on alcohols and alkyl halides as alkylating reagents. Now a deaminative nucleophilic substitution strategy that uses alkyl amines as direct alkylation reagents is reported. Harnessing the reactivity of N-alkyl nitroamines, this process enables the efficient construction of diverse alkyl C–halogen, C–C, C–N, C–O and C–S bonds.
n601441f434af: Using molecular bows to impose intramolecular tension on olefins, Liu and colleagues reveal an unexpected divergence in metathesis kinetics: increasing strain slows cis-olefins but accelerates trans-olefins. Calculations attribute this contrast to configuration-dependent changes in the relative energies of catalytic intermediates and transition states, highlighting the complexity of strain-controlled reactivity.
n8ef7139db71a: The operational stability of halide perovskite photovoltaics is critically limited by progressive defect generation and nonradiative losses. Self-healing of defects offers a promising route to sustained performance, yet the coupled microscopic processes underlying it remain poorly understood, particularly at device-relevant interfaces. Here, we elucidate self-healing and defect evolution in photodamaged triple-cation mixed-halide (TCMH) perovskite films and their device-relevant charge-transport-layer (CTL) heterostructures. Using correlation clustering imaging (CLIM), our recently developed microscopic functional imaging tool, we map spatiotemporal photoluminescence heterogeneity to track defect dynamics. Each CTL distinctly modulates local trap activity, healing kinetics, and spectral redistribution in the TCMH layer, and the heterostructures exhibit faster optical recovery than pristine films, beneficial for device resilience. Healing follows biphasic kinetics, with fast electronic relaxation over minutes to tens of minutes and slower ionic redistribution and lattice relaxation over hours. Although quantitative device stability improvements are not established here, these microscopic insights into dynamic evolution of defects and ion redistribution at interfaces provide a framework for rationally designing stable perovskite optoelectronics.
nd95894dbc91d: Calcium-ion batteries (CIBs) are promising for next-generation energy storage. However, their development is hindered by the lack of high-performance cathode materials. n4051198ef524: Electrospinning produces lightweight, breathable fiber networks that can reflect sunlight and radiate heat without electricity. nf1d28800f1e1: This work proposes a configurational-entropy strategy to optimize the phase distribution of Dion-Jacobson 2D perovskite indoor photovoltaics. n79d26d1e8ae9: The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.
n929edd1b75c4: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.

n8c07533c9366: Inorganic solid-state electrolytes are being developed for safer, energy-dense batteries, yet many contain nearly an order of magnitude more lithium than liquid electrolytes. n95efb48b4ac5: Leveraging their extended π-conjugation, structurally tunable backbones, and superior film-forming processability, two-dimensional (2D) organic polymers have emerged as a highly promising class of materials for third-order nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Herein, a series of porphyrin-based donor−acceptor (D−A) 2D polymer films, namely, TAPP-TAPZ, TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA, are successfully fabricated via a liquid−liquid interfacial polymerization approach. These films exhibit broad absorption profiles across the visible region alongside markedly narrowed optical bandgaps, underscoring the extensive π-electron delocalization inherent to the 2D polymeric frameworks. Femtosecond open-aperture Z-scan measurements conducted at 515 and 800 nm unambiguously reveal pronounced reverse saturable absorption in all samples. Strikingly, the TAPP-TAPZ film delivers exceptional nonlinear absorption coefficients (β) of 8.8 × 103 cm GW−1 at 800 nm and 5.2 × 103 cm GW−1 at 515 nm, values that not only substantially outperform the analogous TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA counterparts but also rival or surpass those of numerous reported covalent organic frameworks, 2D inorganic nanomaterials, and small-molecule NLO systems. Complementary density functional theory calculations ascribe this remarkable performance to the incorporation of benzothiadiazole units, which stabilize a donor−donor−acceptor (D−D−A) electronic configuration and facilitate efficient intramolecular charge transfer. Collectively, our findings establish interfacial polymerization as a robust and generalizable route for constructing ordered, defect-minimized 2D films, thereby offering actionable design principles for the development of next-generation ultrafast photonic devices.

n1ea9da55a0c2: Formamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI3, is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. n1dc2d1788181: Atomically thin amorphous materials combine atomic-scale thickness with local structural disorder, creating unusual transport, interfacial, electronic and catalytic properties. n8f7cf49f1fe6: Understanding ion transport in the limit of infinite dilution is necessary for predicting the performance of electrochemical devices. nb4e49d194ace: Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). n22a028a1c444: The lattice plainification and Ga substitution strategy in PbSe enhances the thermoelectric performance of n-type PbSe across a wide temperature range, enabling a segmented single-leg device with an energy conversion efficiency of ∼10.4%.
nf84916023377: Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. ned7849efb334: Lead halide perovskite precursor salts exhibit deliquescence, where water spontaneously condenses from the air above a discrete onset relative humidity to form a saturated aqueous salt solution. n316c5d639a7e: Microporous layers (MPLs) improve catalyst utilization in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), but must accommodate rapid oxygen removal at high current densities. Under limited water supply, the G-MPL retains stable operation at high current density. ne261e8dfc54c: Semiconducting quantum dots (QDs) are key building blocks for optoelectronics, with tunable properties that depend on their size, shape, and surface chemistry. n7509b39084ec: Suppression of mobile-ion accumulation at the perovskite interface is critical for perovskite photovoltaic (PV) stability. n0cb25c6982f1: Protein-based biological nanopores have emerged as versatile tools for sequencing biopolymers, identifying molecules, and probing reactions at the single-molecule level. Through a combination of structural insights, rational design, systematic screening, and molecular dynamics simulations, researchers have developed nanopores capable of distinguishing between ions, nucleic acids, peptides, and folded proteins with remarkable specificity and sensitivity. Building upon three decades of progress, this Review highlights recent engineering innovations, discusses ongoing challenges, and explores the prospects in the field.
n86c10ac47798: Rearrangement reactions are critical transformations in organic synthesis, and a comprehensive look at how they have been utilized so far in polymeric contexts is missing. Considering these efforts, we compile the history of rearrangement reactions as applied in polymer contexts, detailing mechanisms, reaction conditions, goals for implementation of rearrangement, and location of implementation (i.e., propagating species, side chains, polymer backbones). In organizing this work, we hope to guide the further development of rearrangements as general tools for polymer modification and design.

nd984e838b9c5: The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) can convert CO2 into value-added chemicals, but its efficiency and selectivity are limited by the thermodynamic stability of CO2 and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). hydrogen bonding offers a design strategy beyond direct metal-site modification by stabilizing CO2-derived intermediates and mediating proton transfer. n0334ac4d993b: Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4–2 Gt CO2 yr–1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without reparameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.

nf9305c8813aa: Rational design of oxide photocatalysts with intrinsically efficient bulk carrier transport remains a major challenge because carrier migration is strongly governed by the complex interplay among crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding. Here, we propose a Frontier orbital engineering strategy to regulate intrinsic carrier transport by reconstructing the Frontier orbital composition within a structurally robust oxide framework. Orbital-resolved electronic structure and chemical bonding analyses demonstrate that the valence band maximum (VBM) and conduction band minimum (CBM) are mainly derived from Zn 3d−O 2p and Nb1 4d−O 2p antibonding orbitals, respectively. Such orbital decoupling of Frontier orbital contributing units and the continuous covalent networks along the b-axis provide favorable pathways for bulk carrier migration and establish the structural and electronic basis for the proposed Frontier orbital engineering strategy. Experimentally, Pd-loaded K2Zn2Nb4O13 exhibits enhanced photocatalytic H2 generation activity, achieving a rate of 119(3) μmol/h. This work provides Frontier orbital engineering as a design paradigm for functional materials, enabling the rational manipulation of intrinsic charge transport properties through the synergistic regulation of crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding.
n465bd8456283: Metal nanoparticle sintering in high-temperature oxidizing atmospheres remains a primary deactivation pathway for platinum-group metal catalysts on alumina supports. Here, atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to deposit alumina on supported Pt catalysts and develop alumina-encapsulated Pt/Al2O3 catalysts that were aged at 800 °C under different atmospheres and characterized by time-resolved high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (CO-DRIFTS), and propene combustion kinetics. Within the alumina-encapsulated system, a sub-2 nm Pt cluster population formed under all oxidizing atmospheres tested but not under inert atmosphere, and this population persisted for at least 12 h at 800 °C under propene complete combustion (PCC) conditions. Unencapsulated Pt/Al2O3 controls, by contrast, developed only a transient sub-2 nm population, detected within 1 min of aging in air at 800 °C and no longer present afterward, consistent with the rapid disappearance of small particles predicted by Ostwald ripening theory. CO-DRIFTS confirmed the presence of undercoordinated Pt surface sites in all oxidatively aged samples, with no detectable signal when the sample was aged under inert atmosphere. Propene combustion rates measured after aging for an alumina-encapsulated catalyst were approximately two and five times higher than the fresh encapsulated catalyst for catalysts aged under inert atmosphere and under oxygen and steam, respectively. DFT calculations of Pt diffusion through defective Al2O3 identified kinetically accessible diffusion pathways at 800 °C, with activation barriers as low as 0.76 eV. Furthermore, Pt surface binding was calculated to be favored in the presence of O2. These results identify oxygen-driven surface segregation, mediated by defect-assisted diffusion through the ALD overcoat, as a possible mechanism responsible for nanocluster formation in this system. The persistence of the sub-2 nm cluster population for at least 12 h at 800 °C under PCC conditions demonstrates the thermal stability of these sites within the encapsulated architecture.
ndbadc1daa7c1: Layered inorganic materials can exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions in which electronic instabilities and local structural modes are strongly intertwined. Here we compare the isovalent chalcogenides Bi2Rh3Se2 and Bi2Rh3S2 by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density-functional-theory calculations, and identify a static Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion as the common local motif underlying their distinct low-temperature phases. In Bi2Rh3Se2, the transition near 240 K is characterized by the loss of C-centering without a change in the conventional unit-cell volume. The resulting primitive lattice contains inequivalent Rh4 quadrilaterals formed by alternating expansion and contraction, establishing a C-centering-breaking breathing order. Although previous spectroscopic studies have reported CDW-like signatures in Bi2Rh3Se2, the calculated Fermi surfaces of the high-temperature phase do not reveal an obvious nesting vector expected for a simple nesting-driven Peierls-type CDW scenario. Instead, the Rh 4d-derived electronic states at the Fermi level are naturally sensitive to the observed Rh4 breathing distortion, indicating that the transition is best described as a breathing-order transition accompanied by electronic reconstruction. In Bi2Rh3S2, a comparable Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion appears, but its ordering pattern is switched: when described in the high-temperature-cell setting, the Bi2Rh4 units form a large−small−small sequence along the aHT-direction, accompanied by an antiphase relation between neighboring chains, producing a commensurate 3× superstructure consistent with the first-order character of the transition. Calculations based on the experimentally refined structures further reveal a reduction of the density of states near EF and an anisotropic redistribution of occupied low-energy states in the breathing-distorted phases, supporting the coupling between the Bi2Rh4 motif and electronic reconstruction. These results show that isovalent chalcogen substitution selects the in-plane ordering pattern of an intrinsic Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion, thereby switching the collective symmetry-breaking pathway and associated electronic response.
n457564aea7d6: Two-dimensional Cu nanostructures containing noncanonical face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed (fcc/hcp) heterophase boundaries are attractive for CO2 electroreduction but remain difficult to prepare by wet-chemical methods. Here, we report a high-temperature solution reduction route to Cu nanodisks with a thickness of 26.5 ± 2.3 nm and a diameter of 85.6 ± 3.7 nm. Transmission electron microscopy reveals abundant fcc/2H and fcc/4H interfaces on the nanodisk side surfaces, where the 2H and 4H polytypes exhibit AB and ABCB stacking, respectively. In CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3, the nanodisks achieve a methane Faradaic efficiency of 60.4% at −1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode and outperform fcc Cu nanoparticle and microsheet controls tested at the same catalyst loading. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the free-energy penalty for forming the *CHO intermediate is smaller on the fcc/2H and fcc/4H models than on fcc Cu. These results support a thermodynamic contribution of heterophase interfaces to the observed methane selectivity; the calculations do not establish a reduction in kinetic activation barriers. This solution-phase route therefore provides access to phase-engineered Cu nanodisks and enables structure−property relationships relevant to CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis.
n0b819e8ebfc5: Atomically dispersed W activates terrace Mn sites in β-MnO 2 via W–O–Mn charge delocalization, increasing accessible-site density and boosting OER sixfold. Strong W–O bonds suppress Mn dissolution, enabling stable operation for 1250 h at 300 mA cm −2 .
n692210636012: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.
n36967a5e1662: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.
nacf0cbb408c5: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.
n69218a252dae: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.
n10a60b686412: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.
nef61abb22bef: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.
nb5b35a1a035c: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.
nd2fa4369b0d5: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.
n5bc0595f6a2c: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.
n3923abf06e24: Porous liquids combine permanent porosity with fluidity, extending the design of porous materials beyond conventional solid frameworks. This Perspective outlines universal design principles, emerging synthetic strategies and theory-guided methodologies that enable rational control of permanent porosity, fluidity and functionality, accelerating the predictive development of next-generation porous liquids.
n76f9dd444ce1: By decoupling ceramic-film densification from high-temperature sintering, molten-salt-mediated liquid-phase growth enables a dense, compositionally uniform proton-conducting thin film to form at 800 °C, despite its melting point exceeding 2,700 °C. This strategy opens opportunities for low-temperature ceramic fabrication and on-demand materials design.
n7eff34347f13: Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.
ncf6b42c3c595: Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.
n4fcf93d66726: While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.
n9594c2bc857b: A palladium catalyst supported on porous poly( p -phenylene sulfide) (Pd(0)/PPS) was developed for the chemoselective hydrogenation of α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds.
n4787c9ca034a: In situ/operando and rapid freeze-quench Mössbauer approaches enable quantitative tracking of the oxidation state, spin state, and local coordination environment of Mössbauer-active metal sites in single-atom catalysts during catalytic processes, thus providing a deeper understanding of dynamic reaction mechanisms and contributing to the rational design of novel, efficient catalysts at the atomic scale.
nfb1626f9da66: Interfacial hydration fundamentally constrains adhesion in aqueous and physiological environments by preventing intimate contact, competing for binding sites, and weakening the load-bearing interfaces. Although wet adhesives have been extensively designed for durable fixation, emerging technologies in soft robotics, wearable bioelectronics, and minimally invasive medicine require interfaces that can form adhesion, recover after reuse, or detach on-demand under hydrated conditions. This Review discusses reversible wet adhesion through two operational modes: Mode I, cyclic reusability through repeated restoration of adhesion over attachment-detachment cycles, and Mode II, on-demand detachability through trigger-induced conversion of a stable adhesive state into a weakly adherent state through a controlled, low-damage release pathway. We examine supramolecular interactions, dynamic covalent chemistry, mesoscale architectures, biomimetic designs, and hybrid strategies as complementary routes for regulating hydration, interfacial binding, mechanical dissipation, and adhesive state transitions at wet interfaces. We analyze how contact formation, hydration history, fracture pathways, loading history, test geometry, and biofluid exposure shape the measured performance. We further assess current methods for quantifying reusability, switching, durability, and biofluid tolerance, emphasizing failure mode-informed evaluation and standardized reporting criteria. Integrating hydration thermodynamics, binding kinetics, mechanical dissipation, and stimulus-gated interfacial transitions, this Review develops design and evaluation principles for reversible wet adhesive systems in complex aqueous and biointerfacial environments.
n38c22c435a19: High-entropy materials (HEMs) are composed of multiple principal elements stabilized by the configurational entropy. They establish a new design paradigm in electrocatalysis by leveraging local disorder and multielement synergy to create diverse and tunable active site environments. While HEMs have been broadly reviewed, a focused and reaction-specific assessment of their role in gas-involved electrocatalysis is absent. This review fills that gap by examining entropy-driven design principles, entropy-guided synthesis, nanoscale structural control, and advanced characterization of HEMs and by linking these aspects to their reaction-specific catalytic behavior in gas-involved electrocatalysis. We build a unified framework linking high-entropy chemistry to catalytic function across five key reactions: the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR), and nitrogen oxidation reaction (NOR). We provide comprehensive coverage across all major HEM families, including high-entropy alloys, oxides, chalcogenides, hydroxides, fluorides, MXenes, and single-atom configurations, highlighting features unique to each system. Key challenges and future directions are outlined, including scalable synthesis, active-site identification, machine-learning-guided discovery, and interfacial engineering. This review provides a reaction-focused framework for advancing HEM-based electrocatalysis and offers guidance for designing next-generation materials for clean energy technologies.
n38c28a122637: This review outlines design principles, printing methods, stretchable electrodes, structural strategies, and cathode chemistries for body-conformable aqueous zinc-based batteries in medical devices.
n424894bb9d4f: This review critically connects Raman modalities, molecular readouts, data analysis and clinical translation for cancer therapy-response studies.
ndcf5796e5afc: While phosphorus chalcogenides are promising candidates for infrared nonlinear optical (IR-NLO) applications, a fundamental understanding of the microscopic mechanisms driving their second harmonic generation (SHG) response is still lacking. In this work, we address this gap by developing atomate2-ARTATOP, an open-source high-throughput computational framework that integrates atomic response theory (ART) into atomate2 to enable systematic NLO property screening and analysis. Our large-scale screening of 231 non-centrosymmetric compounds spanning thiophosphates (PS), selenophosphates (PSe), and oxygen-containing phosphorus chalcogenides (PSO) reveals a clear SHG performance trend (PSe > PS > PSO), mapping specific chemical families to targeted infrared and ultraviolet spectral windows. Notably, Hg2P2S7 and InPSe4 exhibit exceptional powder-averaged SHG coefficients of 29.15 (∼2.8 × AGS) and 34.28 pm/V (∼3.2 × AGS), respectively, outperforming the industry standard AgGaS2. Interestingly, unlike conventional thiophosphates, ZnGaPS, a mixed phosphide-sulfide, also exhibits a strong SHG response (21.4 pm/V, ∼2.0 × AGS). Additionally, we identify P2S2O3 as a superior ultraviolet candidate, combining a wide band gap (5.35 eV) with an SHG response ∼7.8 times that of KH2PO4. Through partial response function analysis, we demonstrate that the SHG response is fundamentally governed by nonbonding chalcogen p states, with other elements playing a secondary role on average but contributing considerably in individual compounds. Moreover, the net response in many compounds reflects a competition between positive and negative contributions from different structural units. Finally, by identifying compositional features that induce negative SHG contributions, we offer design insights for enhancing constructive SHG contributions. This work provides a quantitative, orbital-level blueprint for the discovery of next-generation NLO materials.
na40199b42991: Phosphorus exhibits rich allotropy that gives rise to diverse polyanionic clusters and networks. The unusual transport phenomena observed in black phosphorus and its magnetic analogue α-EuP3 highlight the potential of extended phosphorus networks to generate emergent electronic properties. At the same time, high pressure has a natural affinity with P-rich polyphosphides, as it offers access to structurally diverse phosphorus networks, presenting them as a promising platform for materials discovery. In this work, P-rich compounds in the Sr−P and Eu−P systems were explored by combining high-pressure synthesis with first-principles calculations. Five previously unknown polyphosphides were synthesized across the P-rich composition range AP8−AP10 (A = Eu, Sr): EuP8, EuP9, EuP10, SrP8, and SrP10. These compounds contain chain-like and cage-like phosphorus frameworks, with varying lone-pair-bearing P concentrations across compositions. Pressure-dependent convex-hull calculations incorporating the experimentally determined structures identify a narrow moderate pressure window of 2−4 GPa in which the discovered P-rich phases become synthetically accessible, thereby providing a practical guide to their high-pressure synthesis conditions. These results demonstrate that computationally assisted high-pressure synthesis provides a powerful approach to discovering unexplored metastable phases and developing magnetic and topological functionalities in anion-rich binary Zintl compounds.
n088519d71e80: As a traditional thermoelectric material, PbTe exhibits a high peak zT value. However, it is highly susceptible to oxidation during either synthesis or device operation. Thus, it is essential to understand the oxidation behavior at finite temperatures and its effects on the geometries of PbTe surfaces. Focusing on oxygen adsorption at two stable PbTe(100) and PbTe(111) surfaces, using cluster expansion, we identify the most stable adsorption configurations of 0.5O−PbTe(100) and 0.33O−PbTe(111) with oxygen coverages of 0.5 and 0.33, respectively. Electronic structure calculations reveal that oxygen atoms form covalent bonds with surface Te atoms. Ab initio molecular dynamics investigations demonstrate temperature is a critical factor that damages PbTe surfaces and drives oxygen atoms into sublayers, forming surface oxides. Oxygen atoms migrate into a deeper sublayer on PbTe(111) than on PbTe(100). Increasing temperature and oxygen coverage aggravate these effects. Surface oxidation fundamentally deteriorates electrical transport characteristics by changing carrier concentration, inducing transitions between n- and p-type conduction, and decreasing carrier mobility. This ultimately leads to significant degradation in its thermoelectric performance. Possible approaches include depositing dense passivation layers to block oxygen adsorption and diffusion.
n92cdca8985a4: Dual-band electrochromic smart windows, capable of independently regulating visible and near-infrared solar radiation, offer an effective route toward reducing building/vehicle energy consumption. However, their practical implementation is often limited by slow switching kinetics, insufficient bistability, as well as challenges in fabricating polychromatic, uniform, and scalable electrochromic films with efficient ion and charge transport. Here, we report an interfacial self-assembly strategy to fabricate large-area polyaniline (PANI) thin films featuring a hierarchically porous architecture and thickness-dependent porosity gradient. The self-assembly process, driven by solvent exchange at the air–water interface and modulated by surfactant confinement, produces interconnected PANI nanoparticle networks with both in-plane hierarchical pores and out-of-plane structural gradation. This architecture facilitates electrolyte penetration and charge transport across the film thickness. As a result, the PANI films enable rapid and stable dual-band electrochromic modulation, exhibiting three distinct optical states (“bright”, “cool”, and “dark”) with independent control of visible and near-infrared transmittance. The assembled devices demonstrate fast response (coloration/bleaching times of 1.8/4 s at 633 nm and 1.2/3.6 s at 1200 nm), high coloration efficiency, and excellent optical bistability, together with effective indoor thermal regulation. These results establish interfacial self-assembly as a versatile approach for engineering functional polymer films for next-generation energy-efficient smart windows.
n49da6049c3ab: Ce-doped HfO2 (HCO) ferroelectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for next-generation integrated ferroelectric devices owing to their excellent compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology and promising ferroelectric properties. However, previously reported HCO films generally require relatively large thicknesses and high processing temperatures, limiting their application in highly scaled devices. Here, we demonstrate HCO ferroelectric thin films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and systematically investigate the effects of Ce concentration and film thickness on their structural and ferroelectric properties. The HCO film with 5.0% Ce doping exhibits the highest ferroelectric orthorhombic phase fraction, which is attributed to the formation of coupled defects involving Ce-substitution on Hf sites and oxygen vacancies, as revealed by first-principles calculations. Moreover, the HCO films annealed at 700 °C exhibit excellent ferroelectric properties at the thickness ranging from 12 to 24 nm. In particular, the 18 nm-thick HCO film with 5.0% Ce achieves a remanent polarization of 19.4 μC/cm2 and an excellent switching endurance exceeding 1 × 109 cycles. These results demonstrate the potential of ALD-grown HCO as a scalable material platform for highly integrated and multifunctional ferroelectric devices.
n08a9af6739bd: Acid-mediated precipitation of aqueous tungstate solutions is widely used to synthesize WO3 nanoparticles, yet the coupling of reagent identity, ionic strength, and speciation equilibria across different synthetic protocols cloud which variables govern resulting polymorph type and nanoparticle morphology, as well as whether polymorph and nanoparticle morphology can be tuned independently. Here, we systematically vary acid and alkali salt identity, alkali cation concentration, and acid addition rate to isolate their individual contributions. By accounting for differences in ion activities and speciation equilibria, we show that apparent structure-directing effects previously attributed to anion identity instead arise primarily from solution-level differences rather than direct anion−WO3 interactions. In contrast, alkali cation concentration exerts an independent influence on the favorability of the metastable hexagonal phase that persists even after accounting for differences in ionic strength and speciation. We further demonstrate that acid addition rate modulates nanoparticle morphology without affecting polymorph outcome, identifying acidification kinetics as a synthetic handle acting independently of the factors governing polymorph selection. Using these mechanistic insights, we then show the systematic tunability of polymorph-dependent photochromic behavior in the resulting particles. Together, these findings provide independent synthetic handles for controlling WO3 nanoparticle phase and morphology which directly impact their functional properties, and offer a quantitative approach for reconciling and comparing outcomes across diverse reagent combinations and protocols in WO3 NP synthesis.
n6aa4236543f2: Zn 2+ coordination couples the optical and electronic evolution of carbon dots with Zn interfacial chemistry, enabling homogeneous deposition, low-temperature adaptability, and ultra-stable cycling over 72 000 cycles.
nc29aa339422a: The narrow electrochemical window and persistent dendrite growth of in-situ polymerized poly(1,3-dioxolane) (PDOL) solid-state electrolytes remain critical bottlenecks for high-energy-density lithium-metal batteries. Herein, we propose a redox-active copper-covalent organic framework...
nd71605935438: The scalable manufacturing of high-efficiency organic solar cells (OSCs) critically depends on the use of environmentally benign solvents. However, uncontrolled solvent evaporation in continuous printing environments poses a fundamental bottleneck,...
n115e746b9287: Life cycle assessment of seven SAM-based perovskite cells shows that the processing route, not efficiency or synthesis, determines environmental performance.
n1d1514f74b65: Predicting productive enzyme–photocatalyst combinations remains difficult. Now, screening of 180 enzyme–photocatalyst pairs uncovers divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings, and evolved PLP enzymes selectively produced branched or linear non-canonical amino acids with high stereocontrol.
n44e95b647922: Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d-wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.
n327ceed1d6ab: Lipid nanoparticles are increasingly adept at delivering therapeutics to specific tissues and cell types, and, in some cases, the nanoparticles themselves can now modulate cellular behaviour, immune function and therapeutic outcome.
n99a396f7751d: The therapeutic potential of mRNA had been on the radar for decades but it took an alliance with lipid nanoparticle research to make it a reality. Researchers are now looking for ways to better increase efficacy and reduce side effects to extend the potential of the delivery agents from vaccines to pulmonary and neurological interventions.
n2b6705536beb: Implantable magnetic sensing offers a route to wireless physiological monitoring, but conventional metallic magnets persist beyond their functional lifetime. Now, a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet is developed that can serve as an implanted magnetic signal source, enabling untethered and continuous monitoring of organ motion.
n368db01e7ac4: Using an artificial intelligence-guided framework combining retrosynthetic prediction, high-throughput DFT screening and chemical expertise, a readily synthesizable self-assembled monolayer for perovskite photovoltaics is identified. The top candidate delivers 27.2% efficiency and retains >95% of its initial efficiency after 2,000 h at 65 °C under maximum-power-point tracking.
n76f2fa058d3f: Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.
n661aa18f14e1: Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.
n0b7fe3b2693b: A supported copper complex ( mPAN-Cu ), prepared by the immobilization of CuCl 2 over modified polyacrylonitrile ( mPAN ) is explored as a reusable heterogeneous catalyst for Ullmann type C–O Coupling between a series of aryl halides and phenols.
